articles.o: Energy Efficiency: A Key to Lower Operating Costs
articles.s: How efficient oven technology can improve the economics of nonwovens production Energy efficiency is becoming an increasingly important factor in nonwovens manufacturing. Rising energy costs are putting pressure on production… The post Energy Efficiency: A Key to Lower Operating Costs appeared first
articles.x: How efficient oven technology can improve the economics of nonwovens production Energy efficiency is becoming an increasingly important factor in nonwovens manufacturing. Rising energy costs are putting pressure on production economics, particularly in processes involving thermal treatment, drying or bonding. For operators of existing production lines, upgrading the oven can therefore offer significant potential to reduce energy consumption and operating costs. A practical example can be found at PT. Hilon Indonesia, where an existing oven was replaced while the production line itself remained in operation. According to PT. Hilon Indonesia, the Schott & Meissner oven now requires only around one third of the energy consumed by the previously installed oven. This represents an energy reduction of approximately 67%. Efficient Thermal Treatment Energy efficiency in a thermal process depends on more than the nominal process temperature. Efficient heat transfer, uniform temperature distribution, efficient process-air circulation and controlled exhaust air are important factors in ensuring that thermal energy is used effectively. The design of the Schott & Meissner oven is specifically focused on minimizing energy losses. The oven features complete thermal insulation with almost no thermal bridges, helping to keep heat inside the process chamber. An efficiently designed air circulation system ensures effective and uniform heat transfer across the material width, while controlled exhaust air minimizes the loss of valuable thermal energy. Another key element is the use of state-of-the-art, energy-efficient heating systems. Together with the optimized air circulation and insulation concept, these systems ensure that the supplied energy is used as efficiently as possible. Schott

articles.t: AI 채택을 방해하는 단편화된 섬유 시스템
articles.o: Fragmented textile systems holding back AI adoption
articles.s: The textile industry’s long-established reliance on proprietary machinery control systems and disconnected production data could become a major obstacle to the widespread adoption of artificial intelligence, according to a new white paper from the International Textile Manufacturers Federation (ITMF
articles.x: The textile industry’s long-established reliance on proprietary machinery control systems and disconnected production data could become a major obstacle to the widespread adoption of artificial intelligence, according to a new white paper from the International Textile Manufacturers Federation (ITMF) and RWTH Aachen University. The report suggests that overcoming these barriers will require greater cooperation between textile manufacturers, machinery suppliers, technology developers and industry associations, rather than further investment in isolated digital solutions. Published jointly by ITMF and the Institute for Technical Textiles (ITA) at RWTH Aachen, AI in the Textile Value Chain: A Strategic Guide to Artificial Intelligence for the Global Textile Industry argues that the industry’s principal challenge is no longer a lack of digital technology, but its inability to connect the systems and data already in place. The authors describe the sector as not under-digitalised, but digitally fragmented – a distinction with significant implications as manufacturers seek to introduce increasingly sophisticated AI applications. Decades of investment in production monitoring, automation and enterprise software have generated substantial quantities of information, but much of it remains confined to individual machines, production departments or business systems. As a result, manufacturers often have considerably less accessible, structured and reliable data than they assume, limiting the effectiveness of AI tools that depend on consistent information from multiple sources. articles.o: Archroma, Prosperity Textile partner to develop sustainable denim solutions
articles.s: Switzerland-based specialty chemicals supplier Archroma has partnered with Prosperity Textile, a vertically integrated fabric manufacturer with major production facilities in China and Vietnam. Under...
articles.x: Switzerland-based specialty chemicals supplier Archroma has partnered with Prosperity Textile, a vertically integrated fabric manufacturer with major production facilities in China and Vietnam. Under the agreement, the two companies will collaborate on the development, evaluation and implementation of processes designed to improve denim products while supporting more sustainable manufacturing practices. Also, the partnership will advance innovation in denim aesthetics, durability and performance. Archroma said the partnership reflects a shared commitment to advancing sustainability across the textile industry and translating innovation into commercially viable solutions. “An innovation only matters once it reaches the market, and that takes a partner who will help shape it, test it and run it at scale. Prosperity Textile brings that partnership, and together we want to give denim brands and consumers the look and lasting performance they crave, made in more sustainable ways,” said Jordi Calucho, Director of Archroma’s Super Systems Denim business. Prosperity Textile supplies global apparel brands and retailers, operating manufacturing facilities in China and Vietnam with an annual production capacity of nearly 100 million yards. The company also maintains research and development operations in Belgium, Italy and China. The manufacturer has previously demonstrated its commitment to responsible textile production. It was the first denim producer in China to join the bluesign system, which promotes responsible practices in textile manufacturing. articles.t: Canopy는 MMCF 생산업체의 기준을 높입니다.
articles.o: Canopy raises the bar for MMCF producers
articles.s: Environmental non-profit Canopy has unveiled new criteria for its Hot Button Report, raising expectations for man-made cellulosic fibre (MMCF) producers as the textile industry moves towards more circular and responsible fibre sourcing. The updated framework, which will take effect with the 2027 Hot
articles.x: Environmental non-profit Canopy has unveiled new criteria for its Hot Button Report, raising expectations for man-made cellulosic fibre (MMCF) producers as the textile industry moves towards more circular and responsible fibre sourcing. The updated framework, which will take effect with the 2027 Hot Button Report, places greater emphasis on scaling next-generation fibre solutions, improving supply chain traceability and strengthening forest protection through landscape-level conservation initiatives. The changes mark a new phase for the Hot Button initiative, which has spent the past decade assessing the environmental performance of viscose, lyocell, acetate and other MMCF producers, particularly their sourcing of wood-based raw materials from Ancient and Endangered Forests. Under the revised framework, Canopy has streamlined its assessment from seven categories to five, introducing clearer targets expressed in both volumes and percentages. The criteria also recognise the differing capabilities of small, medium and large producers, while encouraging greater uptake of next-generation fibres made from alternative feedstocks, including recycled textiles. The rating system has also been simplified to three shirt colours – green, yellow and red. Producers with known high-risk sourcing will receive a red shirt rating, while a green shirt indicates low or no known risk of sourcing from Ancient and Endangered Forests or using controversial fibre. More than 550 fashion and apparel brands participating in Canopy’s CanopyStyle initiative use the annual Hot Button Report to inform their purchasing decisions and assess the environmental performance of their MMCF suppliers. articles.o: 패션그룹형지, 뉴욕 FIT와 산학협력 확대…글로벌 패션인재 육성
articles.s: 패션그룹형지가 한국뉴욕주립대학교 패션기술대학교(SUNY Korea FIT)와 손잡고 글로벌 패션 인재 육성을 위한 산학협력을 강화한다. 인천 송도에 구축한 형지글로벌패션복합센터를 거점으로 글로벌 브랜드의 디자인 자산과 실제 유통 현장을 교육에 접목하고, 향후 친환경 연구개발(R&D)과 인턴십까지 협력 범위를 넓힌다는 구상이다.패션그룹형지는 지난 15일 한국뉴욕주립대 FIT 패션디자인 전공 학생과 교수진을 송도 본사로 초청해 계열사 형지글로벌의 까스텔바작 아카이브 쇼룸과 주요 브랜드 매장을 둘러보는 산학연계 프로그램을 진행했다.학생들

articles.o: 리필드, 미국 얼타뷰티·일본 큐텐서 3분기 자체 최고 실적
articles.s: 콘스탄트가 전개하는 두피 관리 브랜드 리필드가 미국과 일본의 주요 유통 채널에서 올해 3분기 자체 최고 실적을 기록했다고 22일 밝혔다.리필드는 미국 뷰티 유통업체 얼타뷰티(Ulta Beauty)와 일본 온라인 쇼핑 플랫폼 큐텐(Qoo10)을 통해 두피 관리 제품을 취급하고 있다.회사 측에 따르면 올해 8월 얼타뷰티 온·오프라인 판매량은 전월 대비 119.2% 증가했다. 이를 포함한 3분기 실적은 리필드의 해당 채널 자체 최고 기록으로 집계됐다.미국 시장에서는 ‘사이토카인 cADPR™ 스칼프 부스터 토닉’을 중심으로 판매가 이뤄졌다

articles.s: 라엘을 비롯한 뷰티·생활용품 브랜드들이 캐릭터 지식재산권(IP)을 제품 패키지와 사은품 구성에 활용하고 있다. 여성용품부터 화장품, 두피 관리 제품, 세탁세제까지 각 제품군의 특성에 맞춰 협업 대상을 선정한 사례다.여성용품 브랜드 라엘(Rael)은 올리브영의 호빵맨 협업 캠페인에 참여해 ‘유기농 순면 커버 입는 오버나이트’ 호빵맨 에디션을 선보였다.해당 제품은 팬티형 생리대로, 엉덩이 부분을 감싸는 360도 힙 커버와 듀얼 샘 방지 가드, 신축성 있는 웨이브 허리밴드 등을 적용했다. 라엘은 호빵맨 캐릭터 디자인을 제품 패키지와 사은

articles.o: What Fashion Can Learn From Beauty’s AI Feedback Loop
articles.s: Every fashion brand is pursuing personalisation and questioning how AI changes the way they engage with their consumer, but the most important case studies might be found in beauty, where regulated claims, shopper participation, and outcome measurement over time create a potent loop. The post What F
articles.x: THE INTERLINE PODCAST · 52 MIN What Fashion Can Learn From Beauty’s AI Feedback Loop Listen to What Fashion Can Learn From Beauty’s AI Feedback Loop Follow the show Apple Podcasts Spotify Hey, welcome back to The Interline Podcast. I’ve been meaning to do an episode dedicated to beauty for a while now. If you’ve been a reader or a listener this year, you’ll have heard me and Grace talk about the unique market opportunity beauty has to ship consumer devices, and to use hardware to get closer, literally and figuratively, to shoppers. Fashion doesn’t have anything close to that outside of wearables. We haven’t, at least not head-on, talked about the fact that beauty also seems to be further ahead than fashion when it comes to AI-led personalisation and AI-enabled or AI-adjacent experiences like virtual try-on. To be clear, VTO in fashion is having a moment thanks to AI. But broad consumer adoption is still very much a work in progress, which is not the case in beauty. Every fashion brand will tell you that personalisation is the key to increasing basket sizes and customer lifetime values. But the actual levers available for brands to pull if they’re trying to build a personalised look are fairly minimal. You can recommend tops, bottoms, shoes, accessories and outerwear in various permutations and different subjective fits to align with people’s tastes as they stand today. That pales in comparison to how individual everyone’s skin is. It pales in comparison to the huge range of features, needs, biomarkers and other variables a beauty brand can use to build an extremely detailed profile of its customers. articles.t: 유로저지(Eurojersey)와 페트라텍스(Peratex)가 힘을 합친다
articles.o: Eurojersey and Petratex join forces
articles.s: Italian fabric manufacturer Eurojersey and Portuguese technical garment specialist Petratex have developed a cycling apparel capsule collection to demonstrate how textile development and garment engineering can be integrated from the earliest stages of product design. Called Optical Motion, the proj
articles.x: Italian fabric manufacturer Eurojersey and Portuguese technical garment specialist Petratex have developed a cycling apparel capsule collection to demonstrate how textile development and garment engineering can be integrated from the earliest stages of product design. Called Optical Motion, the project brings together Eurojersey’s expertise in warp-knitted performance fabrics with Petratex’s capabilities in garment construction, 3D prototyping and advanced manufacturing. The collaboration is intended to go beyond the development of a single collection, with the two companies exploring a joint service that would support performance apparel brands from initial product specifications through to finished garment production. Cycling was selected as the first application because of its demanding combination of aerodynamic performance, comfort, breathability and freedom of movement. The partners have sought to address these requirements through the simultaneous development of fabric properties, garment architecture and construction techniques. The process incorporates body mapping, fabric selection, 3D prototyping and performance validation, allowing material characteristics and garment design to be refined together rather than through successive development stages. Eurojersey contributes its Sensitive Fabrics range of warp-knitted textiles, manufactured through an integrated production process in Italy, while Petratex brings 37 years of experience in technical apparel development and manufacturing. The resulting Optical Motion collection also explores the relationship between functional performance and visual design. articles.t: Advanced Engineering 2026의 Cygnet Texkimp
articles.o: Cygnet Texkimp at Advanced Engineering 2026
articles.s: UK composites machinery specialist Cygnet Texkimp will highlight its technologies for increasing production rates in advanced composites manufacturing at Advanced Engineering and Composites Engineering 2026, taking place at the NEC Birmingham on November 4-5. Exhibiting on the Composites UK Pavilion
articles.x: UK composites machinery specialist Cygnet Texkimp will highlight its technologies for increasing production rates in advanced composites manufacturing at Advanced Engineering and Composites Engineering 2026, taking place at the NEC Birmingham on November 4-5. Exhibiting on the Composites UK Pavilion at stand W170, the company will present its range of fibre processing and manufacturing technologies for the aerospace, space, automotive, defence and construction sectors. Sales director Joe Summers will provide an update on the company’s award-winning Automated Rapid Tape (ART) technology, developed from an original concept by McLaren Automotive. The system is designed to manufacture high-performance, lightweight composite preforms by laying down large volumes of fibre rapidly and accurately, enabling higher production rates while minimising material waste. Summers will present the technology at the Composites Engineering Forum on November 4th at 13.25, followed by a panel discussion entitled Can composites deliver at rate? “Rate is a key driver for an industry focused on making composite materials and parts viable on a bigger scale,” he says. “At this year’s Advanced Engineering, we’re highlighting the technologies we’re developing to achieve high-grade, composites-intensive components at higher production rates while maximising the quality and performance of the end product.” The company will also showcase its compact, energy-efficient Multi-Roll Stack prepreg processing machinery, designed for rapid set-up and changeovers. The system offers materials manufacturers a flexible, space-saving solution for prepreg production. articles.x: NORTH CAROLINA – Renaissance Fiber has secured US$2.24m in financing for its first commercial-scale hemp processing facility in Mocksville, North Carolina. The facility is designed to process at least 600 lb of refined fibre an hour, with production due to begin after construction is completed. The package comprises US$2m in Small Business Administration-backed financing, a US$100,000 low-interest loan from the Fibers Fund and a US$139,000 zero-interest recoverable loan from Invest Appalachia. articles.o: Thiagarajar Mills Group and Germany’s Euro Textiles Announce Rs.100-Crore Textile Manufacturing Venture in Tamil Nadu
articles.s: Advanced Jacquard Air-jet Weaving Facility to Target Global Markets; Commercial Production Planned Within Eight Months. Thiagarajar Mills Private Limited, Madurai, through its group company, has signed a Memorandum of Understanding… The post Thiagarajar Mills Group and Germany’s Euro Textiles Announ
articles.x: Advanced Jacquard Air-jet Weaving Facility to Target Global Markets; Commercial Production Planned Within Eight Months. Thiagarajar Mills Private Limited, Madurai, through its group company, has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Euro Textiles GmbH & Co. KG, Germany, to establish a new textile manufacturing enterprise at Virudhunagar, Tamil Nadu, with a proposed investment of Rs.100 crore. The venture aims to strengthen India’s export-oriented textile industry through advanced manufacturing technology and enhanced access to international markets. Hari Thiagarajan, Chairman & MD, Thiagarajar Mills The proposed facility will manufacture premium-quality 100% cotton jacquard fabrics and other value-added textile products for export markets, with commercial production targeted to commence within eight months. State-of-the-Art Manufacturing Infrastructure The project envisages the installation of 48 advanced Air-jet looms equipped with Jacquard technology, supported by modern warping and sizing facilities. This sophisticated infrastructure will enable the production of high-quality cotton jacquard woven fabrics featuring intricate designs, consistent quality and the flexibility to meet evolving international customer requirements in the fashion and design industry. The first phase is planned to achieve an annual production capacity of 3 million metres , with the second phase envisaged to double capacity to 6 million metres annually , enabling the venture to scale operations in line with export demand. The second phase will also envisage investment into value added technical textiles and niche patented textile fabrics catering to the growing non-conventional textile space. articles.t: Blue Earth 투자 최종 후보로 선정된 재료 혁신업체
articles.o: Materials innovators shortlisted for Blue Earth investment
articles.s: Ten companies developing new textile fibres, recycling technologies, bio-based materials and automated garment resale systems have been shortlisted for investment through the 2026 Blue Earth competition. The companies make up the Fashion & Materials category of the BE100 programme, which has selecte
articles.x: Ten companies developing new textile fibres, recycling technologies, bio-based materials and automated garment resale systems have been shortlisted for investment through the 2026 Blue Earth competition. The companies make up the Fashion & Materials category of the BE100 programme, which has selected 100 businesses across ten industries from 1,414 applicants worldwide. The finalists were invited to pitch at the Blue Earth Summit, held at Woolwich Works in London from October 14-16, with at least one company from each category set to receive a minimum investment of £100,000, subject to due diligence. The Fashion & Materials shortlist brings together companies addressing different stages of the textile and apparel value chain, from raw material production and processing to recycling and the recovery of used garments. Among them is Finland’s Spinnova, which has developed a mechanical process for converting wood pulp and waste materials into textile fibres without dissolving the raw material, while 29acacia is developing fibres and yarns from agricultural banana waste. Colorifix is applying biotechnology to textile coloration, using engineered microorganisms to produce pigments and apply colour to fabrics. Industrial Microbes is also working with engineered microorganisms, developing processes for producing chemicals and materials from renewable feedstocks. In textile recycling, Re&Up is developing processes to recover fibres from cotton, polyester and blended textile waste for use in new textiles, while OceanSafe is developing alternative polymers designed to combine textile performance with recyclability and biodegradability. articles.o: Billion Rise invests $100 million in new Vietnam Facility for advanced knit development
articles.s: Company’s $100 million investment expands sourcing flexibility and advanced knit development for global sportswear, activewear, lifestyle and intimates brands To better serve and support increasing interest among apparel brands seeking… The post Billion Rise invests $100 million in new Vietnam Facil
articles.x: Company’s $100 million investment expands sourcing flexibility and advanced knit development for global sportswear, activewear, lifestyle and intimates brands To better serve and support increasing interest among apparel brands seeking greater geographic diversification with their sourcing needs, Billion Rise, one of the world’s leading vertically integrated companies focused on the manufacturing of textile-based materials for sportswear, swimwear, underwear, and lingerie products, has opened its doors to a high-tech, new factory in Thanh Hoa, Vietnam. Backed by $100 million investment, the new Vietnam facility that is being developed in three phases, is an estimated 320,000 square meters in total size and is expected to have an annual production capacity of up to 100 million meters. Phase one of the facility is complete representing approximately 110,00 square meters. Additional knitting, dyeing and printing capacity will be added in phase two, to be completed in Q3 2027 and phase three to be completed in Q3 2029. “We’re pleased to give our customers greater sourcing flexibility with the addition of our Vietnam operation to our established manufacturing base in Qing Yuan China,” said Charles Chen, Billion Rise CEO and Owner. “After a decade of investment in developing the facility and building it to the same high standards our customers expect from us, we’re confident Vietnam will deliver the quality, technical expertise and consistency our brand partners require.” The Billion Rise Vietnam facility is being developed with sophisticated capabilities comparable to our China operation to include warp and weft knitting, dyeing, digital, flat-bed and heat-transfer printing, stentering, and finishing proficiencies. articles.o: India opportunities for Karl Mayer
articles.s: India’s drive to diversify its textile industry into higher-value products is creating new opportunities for warp knitting and technical textile machinery, according to German textile machinery manufacturer Karl Mayer. articles.x: India’s drive to diversify its textile industry into higher-value products is creating new opportunities for warp knitting and technical textile machinery, according to German textile machinery manufacturer Karl Mayer. At India ITME 2026, taking place in Greater Noida from December 4-9, the company will highlight developments in warp knitting, warp preparation and technical textiles, reflecting changing investment priorities among Indian manufacturers. One notable trend is a growing interest in warp knitting technology from established circular knitters looking to diversify their production capabilities, particularly in athleisure, footwear and functional apparel. “We’re seeing a great deal of interest in our technology from circular knitters,” says Mark Smith, deputy vice president of sales for Karl Mayer’s warp knitting business unit. “They recognise the advantages in terms of output and consistent quality and want to expand their product range to include warp knitted fabrics.” Two- and three-bar tricot machines are among the company’s established bestsellers in India, while its latest developments include jacquard double needle bar raschel machines for producing patterned shoe uppers. Recently introduced at ITMA Asia, the new raschel models offer greater design flexibility for footwear manufacturers. Karl Mayer will also present textile concepts covering four-way stretch fabrics, seamless body mapping and warp knitted constructions designed to resemble woven materials. Beyond apparel, the company sees increasing opportunities in India’s expanding technical textiles sector, particularly in infrastructure, transport and renewable energy. articles.t: IFKT 의회, 공예와 기술을 연결하다
articles.o: IFKT Congress bridges craft and technology
articles.s: The International Federation of Knitting Technologists (IFKT) congress recently (30 September – 2 October 2026) brought together researchers, academics and textile specialists in Zagreb, Croatia for a diverse programme examining the future of knitting, from traditional fibres and craftsmanship to ad
articles.x: The International Federation of Knitting Technologists (IFKT) congress recently (30 September – 2 October 2026) brought together researchers, academics and textile specialists in Zagreb, Croatia for a diverse programme examining the future of knitting, from traditional fibres and craftsmanship to advanced digital technologies, robotics and artificial intelligence. The IFKT’s 52 nd international congress, which marked the federation’s 70 th anniversary, highlighted the increasingly interdisciplinary nature of knitting research, with presentations covering textile engineering, three-dimensional modelling, automated quality control, education and the preservation of regional knitting traditions. Founded to promote international cooperation and the exchange of technical knowledge, the IFKT provides a forum for scientists, engineers, educators and industry professionals working in knitting technology. Its international congresses bring together specialists from universities, research institutions and industry to present developments in knitting machinery, materials, processes and applications. The federation operates through national sections, with its congresses providing opportunities to strengthen collaboration between researchers and industry while encouraging the exchange of knowledge across different knitting disciplines. Among the presentations at the Croatian congress was research undertaken through Future Island-Island, an Arts and Humanities Research Council (AHRC) Future Observatory project, examining the role of wool and traditional knitting in shaping the cultural identity of Rathlin Island, off the north coast of Northern Ireland. articles.t: 데이터와 기술이 섬유 AI 채택을 방해합니다.
articles.o: Data and skills hinder textile AI adoption
articles.s: The global textile and apparel industry faces significant challenges in adopting artificial intelligence (AI), with fragmented data systems, skills shortages and inadequate governance proving greater obstacles than the technology itself, according to a new white paper published by the International
articles.x: The global textile and apparel industry faces significant challenges in adopting artificial intelligence (AI), with fragmented data systems, skills shortages and inadequate governance proving greater obstacles than the technology itself, according to a new white paper published by the International Textile Manufacturers Federation (ITMF) and the Institut für Textiltechnik (ITA) of RWTH Aachen University. Entitled AI in the Textile Value Chain: A Strategic Guide to Artificial Intelligence for the Global Textile Industry , the report argues that successful AI implementation will depend on coordinated investment in data infrastructure, workforce capabilities and industry-wide collaboration rather than technological development alone. Published on 15 October 2026, the white paper draws on the ITMF and ITA webinar series AI in the Textile Value Chain , held between 2024 and 2026. The ten sessions featured more than 20 experts from industry, research institutions and policy organisations. Additional insights came from discussions with textile industry practitioners at the ITMF Annual Conference 2025 in Yogyakarta, Indonesia. The authors suggest that AI adoption is increasingly being driven by structural pressures, including demographic change, persistent labour and skills shortages, market volatility and growing requirements for product quality, traceability and sustainability. Despite decades of digitalisation, many textile manufacturers continue to operate disconnected systems that generate substantial volumes of data without making that information readily accessible or usable. articles.s: Natural fibers are gaining consumer attention, creating opportunities for textile manufacturers and fashion brands to develop higher-value products and strengthen trust through verified material claim...
articles.x: Natural fibers are gaining consumer attention, creating opportunities for textile manufacturers and fashion brands to develop higher-value products and strengthen trust through verified material claims. Figure: The study found that 71% of consumers consider independent certification or verification of fiber content and quality important. A survey commissioned by Woolmark and conducted by Ipsos found that 82% of consumers would choose natural fibers over synthetic alternatives when price, style and fit are equal. The study covered 1,500 adults across the United States, France, Germany, Italy and China in September 2026. The survey also found that 45% of consumers consider fiber composition more important than before when buying clothing. Another 31% said natural materials had become more important in their clothing choices. 67% willing to pay more for natural fibers This creates a potential opportunity for brands to target consumers who value material quality. However, willingness to pay more does not guarantee higher sales. Brands still need to offer suitable designs, reliable quality, and prices that consumers can accept. Merino wool is also gaining online attention. Google search interest in the term has more than doubled worldwide over the past five years, according to Woolmark. The increase suggests growing interest in the fiber, although search activity does not directly measure sales. 71% want proof of fiber quality Consumer interest in natural fibers also comes with a demand for reliable information. The study found that 71% of consumers consider independent certification or verification of fiber content and quality important. articles.o: Stäubli showcases automated weaving systems at ITMA ASIA 2026
articles.s: Stäubli will showcase automated weaving technologies at ITMA ASIA + CITME 2026 as textile manufacturers seek greater production reliability, consistent fabric quality, and more advanced weaving capabi...
articles.x: Stäubli will showcase automated weaving technologies at ITMA ASIA + CITME 2026 as textile manufacturers seek greater production reliability, consistent fabric quality, and more advanced weaving capabilities. Figure: 1692_cam-motion-Staubli The company will exhibit at Booth D05 in Hall 3, presenting technologies for weaving preparation, shedding, Jacquard production, and industrial 3D weaving. The event will run from November 20–24 in Shanghai, bringing together more than 1,800 companies that have applied to exhibit across approximately 180,000 square meters. Industrial-scale denim production provides a key example of the technology’s application. China-based JIEDE Textile operates 430 Stäubli S3060 rotary dobbies and has an annual denim fabric production capacity of 100 million meters. According to Stäubli, the systems have helped improve production stability, reduce downtime and fabric defects, and maintain consistency between batches. The company has not disclosed numerical results for these improvements. “For us, Stäubli is more than an equipment supplier. It is a key technology partner. From solution design to ongoing service, they support us throughout the entire lifecycle,” said Wang Lihua, General Manager at JIEDE Textile. Stäubli will also present the S1628 cam motion, designed for air-jet and rapier weaving at speeds of up to 1,200 revolutions per minute (rpm), and the S3060 rotary dobby, which supports air-jet weaving at speeds of up to 800 rpm. Actual speeds depend on machine configuration and application. Its Jacquard portfolio spans 80 to 25,600 hooks, supporting applications from apparel and upholstery to technical fabrics. articles.s: Cotton Brazil Strengthens International Partnerships and Advances Natural Fiber Dialogue at ICA 2026. Participation in one of the world’s leading industry events reinforces the importance of natural fibers and strategic relationships with international partners Cotton Brazil participated in the ICA
articles.x: Cotton Brazil Strengthens International Partnerships and Advances Natural Fiber Dialogue at ICA 2026. Participation in one of the world’s leading industry events reinforces the importance of natural fibers and strategic relationships with international partners Cotton Brazil participated in the ICA Trade Event Istanbul 2026, one of the leading international gatherings of the cotton supply chain, bringing the importance of promoting natural fibers to the global discussion and strengthening relationships with industry partners. Held on October 14 and 15 at the Hilton Istanbul Bomonti Hotel in Istanbul, Turkey, ICA 2026 brought together approximately 600 delegates from the global cotton community, including growers, exporters and representatives of major consumer markets. During the event, the Brazilian delegation presented the “Hanging by a Thread” movement, known in Brazil as “Microplástico é o Fim da Linha,” which seeks to raise awareness about the presence of microplastics in everyday life and their potential impacts on health and the environment. Primarily focused on engaging the Brazilian public and promoting public policies, the movement joins other initiatives across the supply chain to expand access to information and transparency, encourage research and innovation, and create new opportunities for the use of natural fibers whenever technically appropriate. “The goal is not to eliminate synthetic fibers, but to encourage debate and promote more conscious choices,” says Gustavo Piccoli, president of the Brazilian Cotton Growers Association (Abrapa). articles.t: Archroma와 Prosperity Textile이 데님 혁신을 위해 협력합니다
articles.o: Archroma and Prosperity Textile to collaborate on denim innovation
articles.s: Archroma, a global leader in specialty chemicals, and Prosperity Textile, an international fabric manufacturer with production bases in China and Vietnam, have announced a partnership to drive denim innovation. They will collaborate to develop, evaluate and implement new approaches to improve denim
articles.x: Archroma, a global leader in specialty chemicals, and Prosperity Textile, an international fabric manufacturer with production bases in China and Vietnam, have announced a partnership to drive denim innovation. They will collaborate to develop, evaluate and implement new approaches to improve denim aesthetics, durability and performance, with a shared commitment to sustainability. “An innovation only matters once it reaches the market, and that takes a partner who will help shape it, test it and run it at scale,” said Jordi Calucho, Super Systems Denim Director, Archroma. “Prosperity Textile brings that partnership, and together we want to give denim brands and consumers the look and lasting performance they crave, made in more sustainable ways.” “After 25 years in denim, we know what it takes to turn a good idea into a great fabric,” said Stafford Lau, Director, Prosperity Textile. “Our smart factory infrastructure lets us develop and test new ideas quickly and take the best of them into production. We look forward to exploring what’s possible with Archroma, from classic to creative.” The post Archroma and Prosperity Textile to collaborate on denim innovation appeared first on Textile Focus .

articles.o: Textile wearable robotics: A new paradigm
articles.s: The growing convergence of textile engineering, robotics and human-machine interaction is opening new possibilities for wearable technologies, with knitted structures playing an increasingly important role in the development of lightweight, flexible and functional robotic systems. Leonardo Cappello,
articles.x: The growing convergence of textile engineering, robotics and human-machine interaction is opening new possibilities for wearable technologies, with knitted structures playing an increasingly important role in the development of lightweight, flexible and functional robotic systems. Leonardo Cappello, Assistant Professor at the BioRobotics Institute of Scuola Superiore Sant’Anna in Pisa, Italy, outlined developments in textile robotics and wearable assistive technologies during a technical presentation at the recent The Loop – Chapter One: Medical Textiles event (7-8 October, Albstadt, Germany), examining how advanced materials and robotic systems can be integrated to support human movement, rehabilitation and physical performance. The presentation highlighted the potential of soft robotic technologies to move beyond conventional rigid mechanical systems, using compliant materials and textile-based structures to create devices that interact more naturally with the human body. Applications range from robotic gloves and movement-assistance systems to wearable devices designed for rehabilitation, gripping and reaching, thermal regulation, haptic feedback and therapeutic compression. Integration A central theme was the integration of structural, functional and programmed properties within textile systems. Rather than treating fabrics simply as passive materials, researchers are investigating how textile structures can provide mechanical functionality and contribute directly to the operation of wearable robotic devices. Knitted fabrics are particularly relevant because of their inherent flexibility, stretchability and ability to conform to complex body shapes. articles.o: Ready for India’s next phase of textile growth at ITME 2026
articles.s: Advanced finishing, coating and energy-efficient processing will be highlighted by Monforts at India ITME 2026, as the region’s textile manufacturers increasingly look beyond volume production towards higher-value fabrics. The German finishing machinery specialist sees considerable potential in Indi
articles.x: Advanced finishing, coating and energy-efficient processing will be highlighted by Monforts at India ITME 2026, as the region’s textile manufacturers increasingly look beyond volume production towards higher-value fabrics. The German finishing machinery specialist sees considerable potential in India as investment continues in conventional apparel and home textiles alongside rapidly developing markets for technical textiles, activewear, sportswear, filtration and automotive applications. Supporting this next phase of growth will be newly appointed Monforts area sales manager for Asia Daniel Rütten, who is taking over responsibility for India and the wider region from Hans Wroblowski. Daniel Rütten brings extensive Monforts experience to the position, having joined the company in 1998 and worked for many years in head office sales and logistics before more recently taking on responsibility for customers in Latin America. Scale and breadth “India remains one of the most important markets for Monforts, not only because of the scale of its textile industry but because of the breadth of its manufacturing base,” he says. “Indian manufacturers are looking much more closely at energy, water and chemical consumption, as well as the level of automation required to achieve consistent quality. “Productivity remains essential, but increasingly it has to be combined with lower operating costs, greater flexibility and the ability to manufacture more sophisticated products.” At India ITME 2026 at stand A5 in Hall 1 from December 4-9, Monforts will emphasise the opportunities for manufacturers to create greater value at the finishing stage. articles.t: GarmentTechBD가 주관한 DataDevelop Prize(DDP) 2026 Bangladesh 사례 대회
articles.o: The DataDevelop Prize (DDP) 2026 Bangladesh Case Competition, organized by GarmentTechBD
articles.s: The DataDevelop Prize (DDP) 2026 Bangladesh Case Competition, organized by GarmentTechBD, brought together talented students, participating companies, industry stakeholders, trade associations, and academic institutions to promote data-driven innovation and strengthen industry–academia collaboration
articles.x: The DataDevelop Prize (DDP) 2026 Bangladesh Case Competition, organized by GarmentTechBD, brought together talented students, participating companies, industry stakeholders, trade associations, and academic institutions to promote data-driven innovation and strengthen industry–academia collaboration in Bangladesh’s garment and textile sector. The competition provided a platform for young talents to develop and present innovative, data-driven solutions addressing emerging challenges and opportunities within the apparel and textile industry. The initiative also highlighted the importance of collaboration among industry, academia, and future professionals in advancing the competitiveness and transformation of Bangladesh’s RMG sector. Representing the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA), Ahmed Jabed, Chairman, Standing Committee on SDP, attended the competition and served as a Judge for the DDP 2026 Bangladesh Case Competition. His participation reflected BGMEA’s continued commitment to supporting initiatives that promote innovation, knowledge development, and the engagement of young professionals and students with the RMG industry. The winning team of the Bangladesh Case Competition will represent Bangladesh at the DDP 2026 Hong Kong Case Competition, scheduled to be held on 7 November 2026 at Hong Kong Science and Technology Parks (HKSTP), providing the team with an opportunity to showcase its ideas and capabilities on an international platform. Their valuable contributions, active engagement, and continued support are highly appreciated in strengthening such collaborative initiatives between the industry and academia. articles.o: Renaissance Fiber Secures $2.24 Million To Scale Domestic Hemp Fiber Manufacturing
articles.s: MOCKSVILLE, N.C. — October 20, 2026 — Renaissance Fiber has secured $2.239 million in combined financing to complete and operate its first commercial-scale hemp fiber processing facility in Mocksville, North Carolina. The package includes $2 million in SBA-backed financing, a $100,000 low-interest l
articles.x: MOCKSVILLE, N.C. — October 20, 2026 — Renaissance Fiber has secured $2.239 million in combined financing to complete and operate its first commercial-scale hemp fiber processing facility in Mocksville, North Carolina. The package includes $2 million in SBA-backed financing, a $100,000 low-interest loan from the Fibers Fund, and a $139,000 zero-interest recoverable loan from Invest Appalachia. The financing moves Renaissance Fiber from years of research and development into commercial production. It provides capital for manufacturing infrastructure, raw material purchases, inventory, and the company’s transition to full-scale operations. “Getting from a proven process to a working factory is one of the most challenging steps in advanced materials manufacturing,” said Daniel Yohannes, founder and CEO of Renaissance Fiber. “This financing gives us the infrastructure and working capital to process American-grown hemp at commercial scale, using the textile manufacturing base that already exists in North Carolina and across the US.” Catalytic capital unlocks commercial financing The Fibers Fund and Invest Appalachia announced their support for Renaissance Fiber in April 2026. Their early commitments helped the company obtain a larger SBA-backed financing package, demonstrating how flexible, first-in capital can unlock conventional financing for manufacturing companies operating in emerging markets. articles.o: Polartec redesigns Alpha insulation to improve durability and design flexibility
articles.s: Polartec, the performance textile brand owned by Milliken & Company, has introduced an updated version of its Alpha active insulation. The new, patent-pending construction is designed to improve s...
articles.x: Polartec, the performance textile brand owned by Milliken & Company, has introduced an updated version of its Alpha active insulation. The new, patent-pending construction is designed to improve snag resistance and give apparel brands more design options. Figure: Polartec redesigns Alpha insulation to improve durability and design flexibility. Courtesy: Collected The development targets a key challenge in performance apparel: making fabrics more durable without reducing breathability or thermal regulation. The updated construction aims to maintain Alpha’s core performance while improving resistance to snags during wear. Alpha active insulation is designed for garments that need to manage body heat during physical activity. This makes durability important for outdoor clothing, endurance sportswear and other performance apparel. The improved construction could help brands develop garments that balance thermal comfort, breathability and durability. Greater design flexibility may also support new garment structures and applications. The update expands Polartec’s active insulation platform. It reflects the industry’s focus on developing performance fabrics that combine comfort with durability for demanding activities.

articles.o: Bangladesh plans 70 MW solar plant at coal power station
articles.s: The European Investment Bank (EIB) is anticipated to assist fund an organized 70 MW solar energy plant at Bangladesh’s Matarbari coal-fired power station, with commissioning targeted for December 2028. Bangladesh prepares to develop a 70 MW solar energy plant on unused land at the Matarbari coal-fir
articles.x: The European Investment Bank (EIB) is anticipated to assist fund an organized 70 MW solar energy plant at Bangladesh’s Matarbari coal-fired power station, with commissioning targeted for December 2028. Bangladesh prepares to develop a 70 MW solar energy plant on unused land at the Matarbari coal-fired power station in the southeastern part of the nation, with electrical energy generation anticipated to start by December 2028. State-owned Coal Power Generation Company Bangladesh Ltd. (CPGCBL) will establish the job in an ash pond location at the 1,200 MW Matarbari coal plant. The EIB is anticipated to co-finance building and construction along with CPGCBL and the Bangladeshi federal government. A current conference chaired by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman required expedited building amidst fuel supply lacks impacting the nation’s electrical energy supply. Bangladesh intends to create 20% of its electrical energy from sustainable sources by 2030 and 30% by 2040. The job is planned to increase the share of renewables in the nation’s energy mix, decrease reliance on nonrenewable fuel sources, and lower greenhouse gas emissions, according to the advancement task proposition. The suggested website lies within the coal plant’s protective embankment, where security facilities is currently readily available. Existing transmission facilities neighboring is likewise anticipated to minimize extra building and construction expenses. Bangladesh has actually authorized numerous massive solar tasks in current months, consisting of a proposed 442 MW plant at Rampal on unused land at a coal-fired power station. articles.t: Accotex DAYTEX T868: DTY 생산을 위한 안정적인 성능
articles.o: Accotex DAYTEX T868: Reliable Performance for DTY Production
articles.s: The new DAYTEX T868 Apron is designed for stable draw textured yarn (DTY) processing, extended service life and consistent production quality. In modern draw-texturing operations, process stability and consistent yarn quality are key to maintaining productivity and meeting increasing quality require
articles.x: The new DAYTEX T868 Apron is designed for stable draw textured yarn (DTY) processing, extended service life and consistent production quality. In modern draw-texturing operations, process stability and consistent yarn quality are key to maintaining productivity and meeting increasing quality requirements. To support these objectives, Accotex has developed the DAYTEX T868 apron – a high-performance solution for reliable DTY processing. Stable performance for high-speed texturing The DAYTEX T868 apron provides smooth and vibration-free running characteristics throughout the production process. This supports stable yarn processing, improves process control and reduces operational disturbances. Advanced material technology for a longer service life The apron is based on a specially formulated NBR rubber compound with high ACN content. It offers strong resistance to oil, heat and wear, supporting a long service life. Consistent quality throughout the entire service life Field experience shows that the DAYTEX T868 operates reliably for up to 90 days while maintaining stable processing conditions and consistent yarn quality. With these properties, the DAYTEX T868 apron offers a reliable foundation for demanding DTY applications. articles.t: Blue Tomato의 디지털 업그레이드
articles.o: Digital upgrade for Blue Tomato
articles.s: Blue Tomato – Europe’s largest board sports retailer – is using two Kornit Atlas Max Plus systems to support a more agile approach to in-house apparel production. The systems are helping Blue Tomato respond faster to changing consumer trends, produce high-quality apparel for its network of 86 retail
articles.x: Blue Tomato – Europe’s largest board sports retailer – is using two Kornit Atlas Max Plus systems to support a more agile approach to in-house apparel production. The systems are helping Blue Tomato respond faster to changing consumer trends, produce high-quality apparel for its network of 86 retail stores across Europe and reduce inventory by printing only what the market demands. Following a comprehensive market evaluation, the company selected Kornit to support its retail production strategy. The systems support Direct-to-Garment (DTG) printing across a broad range of fabrics, rather than being limited to cotton applications. For more than 30 years, Blue Tomato has served the snowboard, skate and surf communities across Europe. As retail evolved from two seasonal collections to multiple product drops throughout the year, the company recognised the need for a more agile production model. Rather than committing to large production runs months in advance, Blue Tomato can now introduce smaller batches into stores, monitor customer demand and quickly replenish successful designs, reducing storage requirements while avoiding unnecessary inventory. “Retail has changed dramatically,” says Blue Tomato team manager Karl Brandl. “Today it’s all about reacting to trends as they happen. By bringing production in-house with Kornit, we’ve gained much greater control over our supply chain. We can test new products quickly, replenish successful designs and avoid investing in large inventories before we know what our customers really want.” Since implementing the Atlas Max Plus upgrade, the company has achieved machine availability of more than 90%, significantly reducing downtime while improving print quality for complex, high-colour designs. articles.t: Hyosung, Vietnam에서 상업용 bio-BDO 생산 시작
articles.o: Hyosung starts commercial bio-BDO production in Vietnam
articles.s: Hyosung TNC has commenced commercial production of bio-based 1,4-butanediol (bio-BDO) in Vietnam, marking a significant milestone in its strategy to develop an integrated manufacturing network for bio-based elastane and other sustainable materials. The development establishes a production chain link
articles.x: Hyosung TNC has commenced commercial production of bio-based 1,4-butanediol (bio-BDO) in Vietnam, marking a significant milestone in its strategy to develop an integrated manufacturing network for bio-based elastane and other sustainable materials. The development establishes a production chain linking sugarcane-derived raw materials with the manufacture of regen BIO spandex, supporting the South Korean textile manufacturer’s ambitions to expand its renewable materials business and strengthen its position in the global performance textiles market. The new bio-BDO facility in Vietnam has an initial annual production capacity of 50,000 tonnes, with phased expansion planned to reach 200,000 tonnes in response to market demand. The project forms part of a planned US$1 billion investment by Hyosung. Hyosung Chairman Hyun-Joon Cho has identified bio-based materials as a strategic growth area for the group, building on its established portfolio of recycled and renewable textile fibres. The company previously commercialised corn-based regen BIO spandex in 2022 and has developed recycled fibre technologies using PET bottles and discarded fishing nets. “We have established an integrated production system that connects bio-based raw materials with finished spandex fibre,” said Cho. “This will be a core pillar of Hyosung’s next century. Building on our pioneering work in bio-based fibres, we aim to lead the development of this market and strengthen Hyosung’s position in premium textiles worldwide.” The Vietnam facility produces bio-BDO through the fermentation of sugars derived from sugarcane, replacing the fossil-based feedstocks traditionally used in conventional BDO manufacturing. articles.t: AI는 니트 원단 디자인을 변화시킬 수 있다
articles.o: AI could transform knitted fabric design
articles.s: Artificial intelligence could play an increasingly important role in the development of knitted textiles, helping designers translate creative concepts into technically feasible structures that can be manufactured on industrial knitting machines. A research presentation by Germany’s Hochschule Albst
articles.x: Artificial intelligence could play an increasingly important role in the development of knitted textiles, helping designers translate creative concepts into technically feasible structures that can be manufactured on industrial knitting machines. A research presentation by Germany’s Hochschule Albstadt-Sigmaringen University outlined a vision for AI as a ‘middle layer’ between design intent and machine-specific knitting languages and constraints. The approach aims to bridge the gap between creative freedom and the technical requirements of industrial knitting production. The researchers, Dr. Ing. Christian Kaiser and Research Associatte, Ellen Judith Mueller, highlighted growing international competition in the textile sector, increasing demand for mass customisation, shorter development cycles and higher performance requirements. At the same time, the complexity of industrial knitting technology presents challenges for designers who may lack detailed knowledge of machine programming and production limitations. Working intuitively The proposed AI-assisted approach would enable designers to work more intuitively with textile structures while receiving guidance on whether their ideas can be knitted successfully. Rather than replacing existing computer-aided design systems or machine programming software, the technology would provide an intelligent interface connecting creative design, textile engineering and manufacturing. Central to the research is the concept of topology and ‘knittability’. In conventional knitting development, designers must understand the relationship between stitch structures, yarn behaviour, machine capabilities and the physical limitations of knitted fabric construction. articles.o: Recognition for algae-based black pigment
articles.s: Living Ink Technologies has been named among TIME magazine’s Best Inventions of 2026 for its development of a renewable black pigment made from algae and other biological waste streams. The Colorado-based company’s Algae Black technology is already being used in commercial applications by brands inc
articles.x: Living Ink Technologies has been named among TIME magazine’s Best Inventions of 2026 for its development of a renewable black pigment made from algae and other biological waste streams. The Colorado-based company’s Algae Black technology is already being used in commercial applications by brands including Patagonia, New Balance and Stella McCartney, providing an alternative to conventional petroleum-derived carbon black in textiles, apparel, packaging and other products. Selected in TIME’s Sustainability category, Algae Black is produced using a process that converts underutilised agricultural, food and industrial waste, including algae byproducts and brewery yeast, into high-performance pigments. The technology has been developed by Living Ink co-founders Scott Fulbright and Stevan Albers as a means of reducing dependence on fossil-based colourants while creating new value from organic waste streams that might otherwise be discarded. The company describes its pigments as carbon-negative and says they can be incorporated into existing manufacturing processes without requiring changes to equipment or production infrastructure. This compatibility is central to its commercial strategy, allowing manufacturers to substitute conventional carbon black with a bio-based alternative while maintaining the colour consistency and performance required for established products. Living Ink has been working with a growing network of manufacturing and packaging partners, including EcoEnclose, Yuto Eco-Tech, Trimco Group and NextGen Packaging, to introduce its technology into commercial supply chains. articles.o: Digital knitting bridges fashion and architecture
articles.s: Researchers at Kent State University in Ohio, USA, have demonstrated how digital flat knitting technology can be used to create adaptable textile structures that move between fashion, furniture and architecture, opening up new possibilities for sustainable, multifunctional design. The interdisciplin
articles.x: Researchers at Kent State University in Ohio, USA, have demonstrated how digital flat knitting technology can be used to create adaptable textile structures that move between fashion, furniture and architecture, opening up new possibilities for sustainable, multifunctional design. The interdisciplinary research, entitled Soft Boundaries: Making Spaces , was conducted by Krissi Riewe Stevenson and Jennifer Meakins and published in the International Foundation of Fashion Technology Institutes (IFFTI) Annual Proceedings. The project explores how computer numerical control (CNC) knitting can combine digital fabrication with traditional textile knowledge to produce three-dimensional structures for wearable and spatial applications. Central to the research is the ability of digital knitting to manufacture shaped textile structures with minimal material waste, while engineering functional and aesthetic properties directly into the knitted fabric. Unlike conventional cut-and-sew manufacturing, which can generate significant waste, digital knitting allows complex three-dimensional shapes to be produced directly from yarn. Characteristics such as stretch, strength, porosity and cushioning can also be incorporated through the selection of knitted structures and materials. The researchers used double-bed digital knitting technology to develop a multilayered textile resembling the quilted construction of a puffer jacket. The structure incorporates exaggerated knitted tubes that can be filled to create volume, cushioning and separation from the body or surrounding surfaces. Extensive prototyping and iterative sampling led to the development of a versatile knitted structure suitable for several applications. articles.o: Rice husk offers low-cost textile wastewater treatment: Research
articles.s: Sabrina Mostafa, Senior Scientific Officer at IGCRT‑BCSIR and PhD researcher at RMIT University, highlights rice husk as a low‑cost alternative to conventional de‑coloring agents. This innovation coul...
articles.x: Sabrina Mostafa, Senior Scientific Officer at IGCRT‑BCSIR and PhD researcher at RMIT University, highlights rice husk as a low‑cost alternative to conventional de‑coloring agents. This innovation could cut textile wastewater treatment costs while reducing environmental pollution. Sabrina Mostafa presented the findings at a discussion at the Ministry of Science and Technology in the Secretariat. Courtesy: Collected In the research titled “Process Development for the Treatment of Wastewater from Textile Industries in Bangladesh,” Sabrina said that the use of locally available natural materials could make wastewater treatment more affordable and environmentally friendly. She added that the technology could help textile industries comply with the government’s 2024 environmental guideline, which requires color units in wastewater to remain within 150. Dr Narshad Haque, a scientific officer who joined the discussion virtually from Australia, said the low-cost method could help make Bangladesh’s textile sector greener and more competitive in the global market. Speaking as the chief guest, Md Anwar Hossain, Secretary, Science and Technology stressed the need to treat harmful wastewater from the textile and garment sectors using modern technologies to ensure sustainable industrialization and environmental protection. He called for joint research and process development by BCSIR and the sustainability departments of industry bodies, including the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA) and the Bangladesh Knitwear Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BKMEA). articles.x: NOVARA – A new €8m textile recycling plant in northern Italy has opened with the capacity to process up to 19,200 tonnes of textile waste annually. The plant will convert discarded clothing and industrial textile waste into materials suitable for spinning. The facility, developed by Italian recycling company Igers in partnership with German sorting technology specialist Stadler, is located in San Pietro Mosezzo, near Novara. articles.o: Heimtextil holds steady for 2027
articles.s: Heimtextil is expecting around 2,900 exhibitors at its next edition in Frankfurt from January 12-15, 2027, maintaining its previous year’s level despite continuing uncertainty across international home and interior textile markets. Organiser Messe Frankfurt says that pressure on consumer spending, i
articles.x: Heimtextil is expecting around 2,900 exhibitors at its next edition in Frankfurt from January 12-15, 2027, maintaining its previous year’s level despite continuing uncertainty across international home and interior textile markets. Organiser Messe Frankfurt says that pressure on consumer spending, increasing demands for product durability and functionality and disruption to global supply chains are influencing purchasing decisions throughout the sector. Against this background, the exhibition is placing greater emphasis on material performance, product quality and reliable international sourcing, alongside a number of new initiatives for 2027. Among these is the Functional Futures Lab, developed in partnership with Future Fabrics Expo, founded by Nina Marenzi. Located in Hall 4.1, the new area will explore new materials and design solutions for hotels, offices, healthcare facilities and other commercial interiors, where textiles must meet increasingly demanding functional requirements. The initiative forms part of the exhibition’s Interior.Architecture.Hospitality programme, which brings together suppliers of specialist contract textiles. An accompanying programme of presentations and guided tours will examine practical applications for new materials. Heimtextil is also introducing a new premium segment, Carpets & Rugs Excellence, featuring international manufacturers selected by an independent jury on the basis of product quality, workmanship and production capabilities. Meanwhile, the exhibition’s 2027/28 design trends, developed with Milan-based design platform Alcova under the theme Home-Maxxing – The Performance of Everyday Living , will explore the relationship between functionality, construction and tactile qualities in interior textiles. articles.t: Techtextil North America, 2027년 모멘텀 구축
articles.o: Techtextil North America builds 2027 momentum
articles.s: Techtextil North America, one of the leading exhibitions for technical textiles and nonwovens in the Americas, will return to Atlanta, Georgia, from 11–13 May 2027, bringing together manufacturers, suppliers, technology developers and industry professionals from across the technical textiles value c
articles.x: Techtextil North America, one of the leading exhibitions for technical textiles and nonwovens in the Americas, will return to Atlanta, Georgia, from 11–13 May 2027, bringing together manufacturers, suppliers, technology developers and industry professionals from across the technical textiles value chain. Organiser Messe Frankfurt is inviting companies to secure exhibition space for the 2027 edition, highlighting opportunities to showcase innovations, establish new commercial relationships and expand their presence in the North American market. The three-day exhibition will provide a platform for companies developing and supplying technical textile materials, machinery, production technologies and nonwoven solutions to connect with buyers, sourcing specialists and industry decision-makers. For manufacturers of knitted technical textiles, the event offers opportunities to present developments in warp knitting, weft knitting, spacer fabrics, functional materials and engineered textile structures for demanding industrial and specialist applications. Technical textiles are increasingly important in sectors including automotive, aerospace, construction, healthcare, protective clothing, filtration, sports and outdoor equipment. The exhibition brings together suppliers and end users seeking innovative materials and manufacturing technologies capable of meeting evolving performance, sustainability and production requirements. Techtextil North America forms part of Messe Frankfurt’s international Techtextil exhibition portfolio, which includes the flagship Techtextil event in Frankfurt, Germany. articles.o: WTRLSS makes commercial debut with Triarchy denim collection
articles.s: Digital dyeing technology developer WTRLSS has entered commercial production, with Los Angeles-based denim brand Triarchy launching the first collection made using its water-saving technology. articles.x: Digital dyeing technology developer WTRLSS has entered commercial production, with Los Angeles-based denim brand Triarchy launching the first collection made using its water-saving technology. Triarchy’s Autumn/Winter 2026 collection comprises five pieces in three colourways, all produced from a single roll of undyed organic cotton fabric. WTRLSS estimates that its technology can reduce water consumption by up to 99.9% and energy use and emissions by up to 97% compared with conventional denim dyeing and finishing processes. It claims that the approximately 75 litres of water typically required to dye and finish a pair of jeans can be reduced to just 20ml. Unlike conventional denim manufacturing, which relies on repeated dye baths and wet finishing processes, WTRLSS bonds colour directly into the fibres in a single pass, without subsequent washing or other wet treatments. Wash effects, fades and design details are created digitally and applied to woven fabric before cutting and sewing. By removing the need for large volumes of water, the technology could also enable more localised denim manufacturing. For Triarchy, it has made it possible to produce denim in Los Angeles again, providing an early example of how production could move closer to brands and their customers. Flexibility The collection demonstrates the creative flexibility of the process, with vintage indigo and black washes alongside a photographic cowhide pattern applied to matching jeans and a jacket. All three finishes were created from the same base fabric, illustrating how a single fabric can be used to produce distinctly different products. articles.s: Taiwan’s Far Eastern New Century (FENC) supplied a new moisture-management polyester fibre for football shirts worn during the 2026 FIFA World Cup, held in the USA, Canada and Mexico this summer. articles.x: Taiwan’s Far Eastern New Century (FENC) supplied a new moisture-management polyester fibre for football shirts worn during the 2026 FIFA World Cup, held in the USA, Canada and Mexico this summer. The company’s TopCool Petal fibre features a distinctive petal-shaped cross-section designed to improve moisture transport and accelerate drying, while providing a softer handle and greater opacity when fabrics become wet with perspiration. The latter characteristic addresses a particular challenge in high-performance sportswear, where lightweight fabrics must combine effective moisture management with sufficient coverage, even under demanding playing conditions. FENC says the technology was adopted by a leading international sportswear brand for World Cup team jerseys, although it has not identified the brand or national teams involved. The development was among a range of textile technologies presented by the company at the Taipei Innovative Textile Application Show (TITAS), held from October 6-8. FENC is already an established supplier of performance textiles to international sportswear brands, with its materials also used in competition apparel worn by leading professional tennis players. Circular poyester Alongside its latest sportswear developments, the company is expanding its textile-to-textile recycling activities as part of a broader strategy to establish a circular polyester manufacturing system. Building on its established production of recycled polyester from post-consumer PET bottles, FENC is developing technologies enabling polyester-based products to be recycled into new materials without requiring the separation of multiple incompatible polymers. articles.o: Committed by tradition at Merz
articles.s: German circular knitting machinery manufacturer Merz highlighted its long history of innovation in the production of medical compression stockings and other specialist knitted products, at the recent The Loop – Chapter One: Medical Textiles event at Groz-Beckert in Albstadt, as the company celebrate
articles.x: German circular knitting machinery manufacturer Merz highlighted its long history of innovation in the production of medical compression stockings and other specialist knitted products, at the recent The Loop – Chapter One: Medical Textiles event at Groz-Beckert in Albstadt, as the company celebrates 126 years of manufacturing expertise. Based in Hechingen, Germany, Merz specialises in circular knitting machines for the production of graduated medical compression stockings, combining precision engineering with a range of machine configurations designed to meet the requirements of the medical hosiery industry. The company’s origins date back to 1900, when Carl Merz founded a mechanical workshop in Hechingen, initially producing sewing machines and bicycles. In 1948, the company developed its first circular knitting machine for socks, followed by the introduction of circular knitting machines for nylon stockings in 1957. Further expansion followed in 1962 with a move to a new production site in Hechingen, which employed 210 people at the time. By 1970, Merz was developing and manufacturing circular knitting machines specifically for medical stockings, establishing the technological specialisation that remains central to its business today. Current operations Merz currently operates from a production and office facility covering approximately 6,400 square metres, employing around 70 people. More than 3,000 of its machines are in use across over 30 countries, with the company offering three principal machine types. The company’s circular knitting machinery portfolio includes models with four different cylinder diameters, allowing manufacturers to produce a variety of medical compression hosiery products. articles.s: 무신사가 글로벌 브랜드의 유통 파트너로서 수도권을 넘어 지방 핵심 상권까지 오프라인 접점을 확대한다. 무신사는 국내 공식 유통을 맡고 있는 하이엔드 스포츠웨어 브랜드 ‘Y-3(와이쓰리)’의 부산 팝업스토어를 5개월간 운영하며 글로벌 브랜드의 지방 오프라인 유통을 확대한다. 지난해 서울에 국내 첫 공식 매장을 연 데 이어 부산에서 두 번째 팝업을 열고 영남권 고객 확보에 나섰다.무신사는 19일 신세계백화점 센텀시티점 5층에 Y-3 팝업스토어를 열었다고 밝혔다. 내년 3월까지 운영하는 이번 팝업은 지난 4월 같은 백화점 2층에서 열린

Figure 01: Md. articles.o: Toray develops composite yarn with 93% recycled content
articles.s: Japan’s Toray Industries has developed a polyester-nylon composite fibre containing at least 93% recycled material by weight, overcoming some of the technical difficulties associated with combining recycled polymers in high-performance textile yarns. The development will form the basis of a new fabr
articles.x: Japan’s Toray Industries has developed a polyester-nylon composite fibre containing at least 93% recycled material by weight, overcoming some of the technical difficulties associated with combining recycled polymers in high-performance textile yarns. The development will form the basis of a new fabric collection, Artirosa CX, aimed at premium outerwear, urban outdoor clothing and casual apparel, with commercial introduction planned for Autumn/Winter 2027. Both the polyester and nylon components of the new fibre incorporate recycled raw materials, building on technologies developed through Toray’s &+ recycled fibre programme. Producing composite fibres with high recycled content presents particular challenges because the different polymers must be processed together while maintaining consistent yarn quality and performance. Toray says it has addressed these difficulties through advances in polymer design and composite spinning technology. The company emphasises that the 93% figure applies specifically to the raw yarn, rather than the finished fabric or garment, where recycled content will vary according to construction and the incorporation of other materials. Toray is now evaluating the technology’s suitability for mass production while continuing research into increasing recycled content in composite fibres. The new Artirosa CX collection combines the composite yarn with fabric design, weaving, knitting, dyeing and finishing expertise from Japan’s established textile manufacturing regions. The resulting fabrics have a dense, finely textured surface and a crisp handle, with finishing processes allowing additional properties including waterproofing, durable water repellency and wind resistance. articles.o: Jeanologia extends its EIM system
articles.s: Jeanologia introduced a new generation of its Environmental Impact Measurement (EIM) system at Kingpins Amsterdam from October 14-15, extending the technology beyond garment finishing to cover yarn and fabric production. The development builds on more than 15 years of experience in measuring the env
articles.x: Jeanologia introduced a new generation of its Environmental Impact Measurement (EIM) system at Kingpins Amsterdam from October 14-15, extending the technology beyond garment finishing to cover yarn and fabric production. The development builds on more than 15 years of experience in measuring the environmental impact of denim finishing processes and aims to provide manufacturers and brands with a more complete picture of the resources used throughout textile production. The expanded EIM system incorporates independent modules for yarn production, fabric manufacturing and garment finishing, allowing each stage to be assessed separately. A new EIM+ platform then brings the results together to provide an overall assessment of the finished product. Using primary production data, the system measures water and energy consumption and chemical use, as well as worker impact at the garment-finishing stage. Environmental performance is classified as low, medium or high impact. By connecting information from different stages of manufacturing, Jeanologia aims to address the difficulties brands face in obtaining consistent and comparable environmental data from their supply chains. © Jeanologia The resulting information is traceable and structured for use in applications including Digital Product Passports (DPPs) and Life Cycle Assessments (LCAs). Although originally developed for denim finishing, the expanded system can be applied to other textile products. articles.s: AIKEN, S.C. — October 14, 2026 — AGY, a manufacturer of advanced specialty glass fibers, announced that its glass fiber yarn serves as the base reinforcement for the Serge Ferrari Group Tenseo Xtrem GF 7000 composite membrane used in the newly installed roof at Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg, Flo
articles.x: AIKEN, S.C. — October 14, 2026 — AGY, a manufacturer of advanced specialty glass fibers, announced that its glass fiber yarn serves as the base reinforcement for the Serge Ferrari Group Tenseo Xtrem GF 7000 composite membrane used in the newly installed roof at Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg, Florida. The new permanent roof replaces the stadium’s previous membrane, which was destroyed by Hurricane Milton in October 2024. The replacement allowed the Tampa Bay Rays to return to Tropicana Field for the opening of the 2026 Major League Baseball season. The roof consists of 24 translucent composite membrane panels covering approximately 45,000 square meters, or nearly 485,000 square feet. Each panel is approximately 330 feet long and weighs roughly 5,000 pounds (2,268 kilograms). Serge Ferrari Group’s Tenseo Xtrem GF 7000 is a high-performance architectural membrane constructed from woven glass fiber fabric coated with polytetrafluoroethylene, or PTFE. The membrane is then sealed with Serge Ferrari’s Pro Shield Max fluorinated ethylene propylene, or FEP, surface treatment. AGY’s specialty glass fiber yarn forms the structural foundation of the woven fabric, providing the strength, dimensional stability and durability required for large-scale permanent tensile structures. “We are proud that AGY glass fiber yarn was selected as the base reinforcement for the Tenseo Xtrem GF 7000 membrane used in this landmark project,” said Patrick Hunter, Chief Commercial Officer and President of AGY. “The Tropicana Field roof demonstrates how advanced glass fiber yarns enable composite systems that must perform reliably under demanding structural, environmental and weather conditions.” The project required an unusually compressed engineering, manufacturing and installation schedule.
