articles.o: Jute sector eyes Chinese know-how as JDPC partners with Jiangnan University
articles.s: Bangladesh is pursuing advanced Chinese technology and research partnerships to modernize its jute sector and boost productivity. Khandakar Abdul Muktadir, Minister of Textiles and Jute emphasized the...
articles.x: Bangladesh is pursuing advanced Chinese technology and research partnerships to modernize its jute sector and boost productivity. Khandakar Abdul Muktadir, Minister of Textiles and Jute emphasized the goal of developing high‑value jute products through innovation and cooperation. The government aims to move beyond exporting raw jute and yarn towards producing processed and value-added products for international markets, with a focus on improved seeds, higher fiber yields, advanced fabrics and diversified applications of jute. Figure: Khandakar Abdul Muktadir, Minister of Textiles and Jute and State Minister Md. Shariful Alam meet with the delegation from China's Jiangnan University. The minister made the remarks at a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) signing ceremony between the Jute Diversification Promotion Centre (JDPC) and China’s Jiangnan University on October 18, 2026. Md. Shariful Alam, State Minister for Textiles and Jute, attended the event. The MoU was signed by Md. Zahid Hossain, Joint Secretary at the Ministry of Textiles and Jute, on behalf of Bangladesh, and Professor Ma Pibo, Dean of Jiangnan University, on behalf of the Chinese institution. According to the minister, Bangladesh has its own investment capacity, but fully realizing the potential of jute requires stronger technological capabilities throughout the value chain, from seed development and fiber production to advanced textiles and innovative products. He said the government wants to ensure the use of modern technologies at every stage of jute processing and value addition to improve the competitiveness of Bangladeshi products in international markets. articles.s: Key insights Non-knitted apparel exports: up 8.5% to €696.5 million Vietnam-bound exports: up 88.2% to €20.5 million Man-made staple fiber exports: down 26.4% to €112.8 million Portugal’s textile an...
articles.x: Key insights Non-knitted apparel exports: up 8.5% to €696.5 million Vietnam-bound exports: up 88.2% to €20.5 million Man-made staple fiber exports: down 26.4% to €112.8 million Portugal’s textile and clothing exports rose 2.4% year over year to €3.78 billion in the first eight months of 2026. It was supported by growth in technical fabrics, non-knitted apparel and non-EU markets. Courtesy: Collected Data from the Portuguese National Statistics Institute (INE) showed that exports to markets outside the European Union increased 5% to €1.09 billion. Exports to EU countries grew 1.3% to €2.69 billion, accounting for around 71% of total exports. Technical textiles and non-knitted apparel led product growth. Exports of coated, laminated and other treated fabrics rose 13.8% to €259.2 million, while non-knitted clothing exports increased 8.5% to €696.5 million. Knitted clothing remained the largest category, with exports of €1.46 billion, up 1.3%. However, man-made staple fiber exports fell 26.4% to €112.8 million, while man-made filament exports declined 11.2% to €53.6 million. These drops offset some gains in other product categories. Spain remained the largest export destination at €873.3 million, although sales slipped 0.1%. Exports to France rose 4.1% to €559.2 million, while shipments to the Netherlands increased 10.2% to €230.1 million. Exports to the United States grew 3.1% to €300.9 million. Emerging markets recorded faster growth. Exports to Vietnam surged 88.2% to €20.5 million, while shipments to Mexico rose 71.7% to €43.4 million. The figures show that technical fabrics and selected apparel categories are supporting Portugal’s export growth as demand varies across traditional markets. articles.x: PUTNEY, VT — September 30, 2026 — Nestled near the banks of the Connecticut River, Green Mountain Spinnery’s colorful yarn covers the entrance to its historic woolen mill headquarters in Putney, Vermont, a cheerful welcome to fiber artists and crafters alike. Green Mountain meticulously transforms raw wool into exquisite, finished skeins through a time-honored process. But that process is dependent on something else time-honored: A five-foot Davis & Furber-Whitin carding machine that is over a century old. Built right here in New England between 1908 and 1918, the carding machine sits alongside other machines dating back to the mid-1940s and early-1950s. About 10,000 pounds of wool goes through the mill a year. Imagine this machine made by two iconic Massachusetts companies has seen almost 1.1 million pounds of wool in its lifetime, and you can guess what kind of work it takes to maintain. Keeping that antique machinery running smoothly is the job of Scott Matthews, carding operator and a nine-year veteran. For Matthews, machine maintenance and fine tuning is almost a daily devotional. And perhaps the most important part of that routine is lubrication. Going Green in the Green Mountains About a decade ago the spinnery transitioned away from traditional petroleum-based products seeking a cleaner footprint. They tried various eco-friendly solutions before finally settling on Renewable Lubricants, which exceeds performance standards. Today, the shop utilizes 1-gallon containers of Bio-Slide Way Lubricant—an ISO 68 lubricant—for transfer cases, sliding parts, and other moving surfaces. articles.s: Following news reports published in several national dailies on 17 October 2026 regarding the withdrawal of bonded warehouse facilities for imports of 10–30 count cotton yarn, the Bangladesh Textile Mills Association (BTMA) wishes to clarify that any policy assessment on this issue should give equal
articles.x: Following news reports published in several national dailies on 17 October 2026 regarding the withdrawal of bonded warehouse facilities for imports of 10–30 count cotton yarn, the Bangladesh Textile Mills Association (BTMA) wishes to clarify that any policy assessment on this issue should give equal importance to the USD 32 billion investment, production capacity and employment in the primary textile industry, particularly the spinning sector, as well as the availability of raw materials and international competitiveness of the export-oriented apparel industry. The withdrawal of bonded warehouse facilities does not mean a ban on yarn imports, nor does it introduce any new customs duty. Following the decision of an inter-ministerial committee, the relevant order issued by the National Board of Revenue (NBR) allows imports against bank guarantees equivalent to the applicable duties and taxes, without imposing any new duties or taxes. articles.o: Toray develops composite fiber with 93% recycled content
articles.s: Japanese materials manufacturer Toray Industries has developed a polyester-nylon composite fiber containing at least 93% recycled material by weight. The company has also introduced ARTIROSA® CX, a fa...
articles.x: Japanese materials manufacturer Toray Industries has developed a polyester-nylon composite fiber containing at least 93% recycled material by weight. The company has also introduced ARTIROSA® CX, a fabric designed for premium apparel markets, with commercial launch planned for the Autumn/Winter 2027 season. Figure: Toray develops composite fiber with 93% recycled content. The recycled content figure applies to the raw fiber, not the finished fabric or garment. The final percentage will depend on the material composition. Toray used its proprietary polymer design and composite spinning technologies to incorporate recycled materials into both the polyester and nylon components. The challenge is to increase recycled content while maintaining consistent quality and the performance required for premium textiles. ARTIROSA® CX features a dense, fine texture and a crisp feel. It targets men's and women's outerwear, urban outdoor clothing and high-end casual wear. Depending on the fabric construction and finishing process, it can be designed to provide properties such as water resistance and wind resistance. Toray said the water-repellent agents used for the fabric are not intentionally formulated with per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS). The company plans to verify the technology's suitability for mass production and explore further increases in recycled content. It will also develop additional fabric options using nylon blends, natural fibers and different finishing techniques. Toray is targeting first-year sales of 200,000 meters for ARTIROSA® CX. The development aims to expand the use of recycled materials in premium textiles, where appearance, durability and functional performance are key requirements.

articles.o: Euratex calls for EU budget support for textile sustainability
articles.s: The European Apparel and Textile Confederation (Euratex) has urged European Union (EU) member states to protect funding for cleaner textile production, recycling and innovation under the bloc’s next l...
articles.x: The European Apparel and Textile Confederation (Euratex) has urged European Union (EU) member states to protect funding for cleaner textile production, recycling and innovation under the bloc’s next long-term budget. The trade body wants the EU’s 2028–2034 Multiannual Financial Framework (MFF) to help textile manufacturers invest in decarbonization, circular infrastructure and digitalization. The funding would support the industry in meeting the EU’s growing sustainability requirements. Euratex raised the issue as EU member states negotiate the next long-term budget. The organization stressed the need to ensure that textile businesses can access financial support as they adapt to new environmental and digital requirements. Cleaner production and recycling require investment in technology, infrastructure and industrial processes. Financial support could help manufacturers reduce emissions, improve resource efficiency and expand textile recycling. The proposed budget period covers seven years, from 2028 to 2034. Decisions on funding priorities will influence how European industries finance their transition toward more sustainable production. Euratex also wants policymakers to ensure that the transition does not leave established textile businesses behind. Supporting existing manufacturers alongside new technologies and circular business models will be important for maintaining the industry’s production base.

articles.s: Textile-to-textile recycling has made significant technological progress but the industry still faces major economic and infrastructure barriers to achieving commercial scale, according to a 19-page report called “Textile-to-textile recycling: the business case”, from the global business information
articles.x: Textile-to-textile recycling has made significant technological progress but the industry still faces major economic and infrastructure barriers to achieving commercial scale, according to a 19-page report called “Textile-to-textile recycling: the business case”, from the global business information company Textiles Intelligence. Executive attention to sustainability has declined as companies focus more closely on margins, budgets and investment returns. At the same time, climate change is affecting supply chains, raw material prices remain volatile, and regulations relating to textile waste and circularity are becoming more stringent. Consequently, sustainability is increasingly being viewed as a financial and strategic issue rather than solely an environmental one. Textile-to-textile recycling can provide three main business benefits, namely: creating new revenue opportunities through circular products; reducing exposure to supply chain risks; and helping companies to comply with emerging regulations. However, the business case remains challenging because recycled fibres are generally more expensive than virgin alternatives and the infrastructure needed to collect, sort and process textile waste is still developing. Less than 1% of global fibre production comes from recycled pre-consumer and post-consumer textiles. Most recycled fibre is derived from other sources, particularly plastic bottles. Furthermore, only around 11% of post-consumer textile waste was collected and sorted into streams suitable for recycling last year. This limits the availability of suitable feedstock for textile-to-textile recycling. Nevertheless, technological developments in textile-to-textile recycling are continuing. articles.x: SINGAPORE/ MUNICH — October 12, 2026 — Niber Technologies unveils NUSPUN®, its next-generation ingredient brand of laminates purpose-built for the functional apparel industry. Rooted in the company’s electrospun nanofiber technology, NUSPUN laminates enable a new category of Active Comfort to give performance apparel both ultra-breathability and tunable weather protection. Weather shouldn’t dictate comfort For the performance textiles industry, weather protection has long come at the cost of comfort. PFAS (Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances) has traditionally given garments an extra layer of waterproof protection, but as regulations against PFAS tighten, brands are under pressure to find alternatives. However, most PFAS-free options force a compromise between water protection and breathability. While some waterproof garments succeed at repelling water, comfort suffers during intense activity as trapped heat, built-up sweat, and humidity, leaving an uncomfortable feeling despite protection from the elements. That trade-off is exactly what NUSPUN® laminates are built to solve through ultra-breathable materials that protect from the elements, without sacrificing comfort. Electrospinning is the innovation behind NUSPUN® materials NUSPUN® laminates start with an electrospun 3D nanofiber web — built fiber by fiber, not cast or stretched like conventional membranes. That’s what lets moisture escape while keeping water out, delivering ultra-breathable performance with tunable weather protection. PFAS-free by design, NUSPUN membranes and laminates are manufactured without intentionally added PFAS materials. articles.x: BALLY, Pa. — October 15, 2026 — Bally Ribbon Mills (BRM), a designer, developer, and manufacturer of highly specialized engineered woven fabrics, will exhibit at Advanced Textiles Expo 2026, November 3–5 in Orlando, Florida. At Booth #805, BRM will showcase advanced narrow fabrics, webbings, high-performance materials, and custom textile designs for demanding applications. BRM develops standard and custom textile solutions using a range of high-performance fibers, including Zylon®, Vectran®, Kevlar® 29, Nomex®, Kevlar® EXO , Spectra®, Dyneema®, and Teflon . The company’s precision weaving capabilities support application-specific designs for markets requiring durable, high-performance textile components. BRM’s woven materials also support next-generation exploration initiatives. Bally Ribbon Mills provided high-strength specialty tapes and webbing utilized in the parachute and landing systems that successfully deployed the Curiosity and Perseverance rovers on the Martian surface. The company is also developing materials for future Moon and deep-space missions. With more than 50 years of medical textile experience, Fetterman will discuss BRM’s work in the medical device market, lessons learned, and factors shaping the future of medical textiles. Advanced Textiles Expo attendees are invited to visit Booth #805 to learn how BRM combines advanced materials with precision weaving to create custom textile solutions. articles.x: At Kingpins Amsterdam, on 14 th and 15 th October , Gold Girl Co. and Officina39 unveil RENEGADE RENAISSANCE , an experimental collaboration exploring the relationship between material and meaning through two conceptual garments: Marble Dreams and Midnight Journey . Conceived creatively by Marta and Glenda Goldschmied, founders of Gold Girl Co., the project asks how unconventional materials can move beyond their original purpose to express ideas of permanence, identity, ambition, and the paths we create through life. Officina39 acts as the project’s technical engine and creative enabler, translating the sisters’ vision into physical garments through chemistry, textile know-how, and material experimentation. Photo: Andrea Venier, Managing Director, Officina39, with Marta and Glenda Goldschmied, founders of Gold Girl Co. MARBLE DREAMS – What if fashion were made to endure? Created using marble dust, Marble Dreams explores permanence, longevity and identity in a culture increasingly defined by disposability. Inspired by the enduring presence of classical sculpture, it transforms a material associated with strength and monumentality into something intimately connected to the body. The piece asks whether beauty can be separated from durability – and whether an object that survives trends can become an extension of the person who wears it. articles.t: Karl Mayer, Changzhou 기계 혁신 공개
articles.o: Karl Mayer unveils Changzhou machine innovations
articles.s: Karl Mayer will stage a major product show at its Changzhou facility in China during ITMA Asia 2026, presenting new warp knitting, warp preparation and technical textile technologies, including several machine premieres aimed at apparel, footwear and composite manufacturers. The event, taking place
articles.x: Karl Mayer will stage a major product show at its Changzhou facility in China during ITMA Asia 2026, presenting new warp knitting, warp preparation and technical textile technologies, including several machine premieres aimed at apparel, footwear and composite manufacturers. The event, taking place from 19 to 21 November and on 23 November, will complement the company’s exhibition presence in Shanghai, where ITMA Asia + CITME 2026 runs from 20 to 24 November. Visitors to Changzhou will be able to see new machinery operating under production conditions, explore textile developments and discuss manufacturing challenges with Karl Mayer specialists. Warp knitting highlights Among the warp knitting highlights is the HKS 4-S EL in a 290-inch working width and E 36 gauge, the finest four-guide-bar warp knitting machine in Karl Mayer’s portfolio. Designed for high-speed production and flexibility, the machine produces fine fabrics with a premium appearance and handle for lingerie, sportswear and athleisure applications. The company will also demonstrate its Rascheltronic RJ 4/2 EL in E 32 gauge, combining efficient production with versatile patterning capabilities. The resulting fabrics offer a clean appearance and cool touch, targeting functional lingerie and performance sportswear markets. A further development is an upgraded TM Weft warp knitting machine with weft insertion. Featuring a finer gauge, electronic pattern drive and intelligent yarn tension control, the machine is designed to improve fabric quality and extend application possibilities in fashion textiles. Footwear solutions Footwear manufacturers will see two new double-raschel machines making their public world premieres. articles.t: The Loop는 Albstadt의 뜨개질 업계 혁신가를 연결합니다.
articles.o: The Loop connects knitting industry innovators in Albstadt
articles.s: Leading knitting technology manufacturers, component suppliers and academic researchers gathered at Groz-Beckert’s global headquarters in Albstadt, Germany, on 7 and 8 October 2026 for The Loop – Chapter One: Medical Textiles, a two-day seminar exploring technological innovation, digitalisation and
articles.x: Leading knitting technology manufacturers, component suppliers and academic researchers gathered at Groz-Beckert’s global headquarters in Albstadt, Germany, on 7 and 8 October 2026 for The Loop – Chapter One: Medical Textiles , a two-day seminar exploring technological innovation, digitalisation and new opportunities for knitted textiles in healthcare and other technically demanding applications. Hosted by Groz-Beckert, the event brought together presentations from the company itself, researchers from Pisa and Albstadt-Sigmaringen universities, and knitting technology specialists Shima Seiki, Merz, Memminger-Iro and Lonati. Together, they provided a broad overview of developments ranging from specialist knitting needles and soft robotics to artificial intelligence, precision yarn feeding and digitally connected manufacturing. The audience included many specialists from Europe’s leading manufacturers of compression hosiery, knitted orthopaedic products and other medical textiles, as well as experts from the knitting technology community and academia. © Groz-Beckert “The requirements for the knitting industry are becoming increasingly complex – from new materials and application areas to digital development and production processes,” said Marco Riecher, Head of Sales Knitting at Groz-Beckert. “The Loop offers participants the opportunity to learn about specific technological approaches, exchange experiences from research and practice, and draw inspiration for their own work.” Matthias Häckel, Head of Brand at Groz-Beckert Group, said the initiative was designed to encourage closer cooperation across the international knitting industry. “With The Loop, we are creating an international platform designed to strengthen dialogue within the knitting industry over the long term.

articles.o: Recycled yarn platform for seamless activewear
articles.s: Germany’s Suedwolle Group has collaborated with Chinese seamless garment specialist UTO and The Lycra Company to develop a collection of performance activewear incorporating polyester fibre made entirely from recycled textile waste. Presented at Performance Days in Munich from October 13-14, the col
articles.x: Germany’s Suedwolle Group has collaborated with Chinese seamless garment specialist UTO and The Lycra Company to develop a collection of performance activewear incorporating polyester fibre made entirely from recycled textile waste. Presented at Performance Days in Munich from October 13-14, the collection is based on a new yarn combining ultrafine Merino wool, Coolmax EcoMade recycled polyester fibre and a fine polyamide filament. The Coolmax EcoMade fibre, produced through a textile-to-textile recycling process using 100% textile waste as its feedstock, provides moisture management and quick-drying properties. These complement the natural thermoregulating and moisture-buffering characteristics of Merino wool, while the polyamide filament contributes durability and stability during processing. Developed through Suedwolle’s Suedwebs Innovation Hub, the yarn has been designed as a common material platform for a range of performance applications, combining next-to-skin comfort with the functionality required for active sportswear. UTO has used seamless knitting technology to turn the yarn into a collection spanning base layers, yoga, tennis and golf garments. The approach enables fit, movement and functional properties to be incorporated directly into the knitted structures, reducing the need for conventional cut-and-sew construction. Each application places different demands on the material. Base layers prioritise moisture management and thermoregulation, while yoga garments require flexibility and close-fitting comfort. Tennis apparel must accommodate more intensive movement and perspiration, while golf clothing needs to maintain comfort over extended periods and in changing weather conditions. articles.s: 글로벌 스포츠 브랜드 '데상트(DESCENTE)'가 컨템포러리 브랜드 '이스트로그(EASTLOGUE)'와 두 번째 협업 컬렉션 ‘키네틱 컨투어(KINETIC CONTOUR)’를 오늘(16일) 선보인다. 지난해 첫 협업에 이어 데상트의 스포츠웨어 기술력과 이스트로그의 밀리터리·워크웨어 헤리티지를 결합해 간절기부터 한겨울까지 아우르는 제품군으로 구성했다.이번 컬렉션명 ‘키네틱 컨투어’는 인체의 움직임과 의복의 형태가 만들어내는 선을 의미한다. 데상트 빈티지 아카이브 특유의 곡선 라인에 이스트로그의 구조적인 밀리터리 디테일을 접목했다.

articles.o: 더일마, 한남동에 신규 플래그십 스토어 오픈
articles.s: 컨템포러리 브랜드 더일마(THEILMA)가 지난 16일 서울 용산구 한남동에 새로운 플래그십 스토어를 열었다. 브랜드가 추구하는 미적 가치와 라이프스타일을 공간에 구현하고, 시즌 컬렉션과 단독 제품을 중심으로 고객 접점을 확대한다는 구상이다.한남동의 조용한 언덕에 자리한 이번 플래그십 스토어는 더일마 특유의 분위기와 취향을 공간 전반에 반영했다. 패션과 일상의 감각이 자연스럽게 어우러지는 공간으로 구성해 브랜드의 디자인 철학과 미학을 입체적으로 전달하는 데 초점을 맞췄다.매장에서는 더일마의 윈터 컬렉션을 비롯해 남성복 라인과 한남

articles.s: 한세실업 자회사이자 원단 전문 기업인 '칼라앤터치'가 효성티앤씨와 손잡고, 시즌 트렌드 및 최신 원단·가먼트 컬렉션 교육을 진행했다.칼라앤터치는 지난 14일 서울 여의도 한세실업 안원빌딩 7층 교육장에서 효성티앤씨 패션디자인센터(Fashion Design Center, FDC)와 함께 칼라앤터치 영업팀을 대상으로 시즌 트렌드 및 개발 원단·가먼트 소개 교육을 진행했다. 이번 교육에는 칼라앤터치 서울 오피스 임직원을 비롯해 과테말라와 베트남 오피스 임직원 등 80여 명이 온·오프라인으로 참석했다.이날 교육은 효성 패션디자인팀 윤인제

articles.o: 효성티앤씨, 바이오 스판덱스 글로벌 공략
articles.s: 효성티앤씨가 베트남에 구축한 바이오 스판덱스 일관생산체계를 기반으로 글로벌 친환경 섬유 시장 공략에 나섰다. 연산 5만톤 규모의 바이오-BDO 상업생산을 본격화한 데 이어 캐나다와 독일에서 열리는 국제 섬유전시회에서 바이오 소재 기술과 관련 제품을 소개했다.영국 섬유 전문매체 에코텍스타일 뉴스(Ecotextile News)가 지난 12일 보도한 내용에 따르면 효성티앤씨는 베트남에서 사탕수수 유래 원료를 바이오-BDO와 바이오-PTMG로 전환해 최종적으로 ‘리젠 바이오(regen Bio)’ 스판덱스를 생산하는 수직계열화 체계를 구축했

articles.o: Toray develops polyester-nylon fibre with almost 93% recycled content
articles.s: New ARTIROSA® CX textile combines high recycled-material content with premium aesthetics and functional performance, targeting outerwear and urban outdoor applications from Autumn/Winter 2027. Toray Industries, Inc. has developed a polyester-nylon… The post Toray develops polyester-nylon fibre with
articles.x: New ARTIROSA® CX textile combines high recycled-material content with premium aesthetics and functional performance, targeting outerwear and urban outdoor applications from Autumn/Winter 2027. Toray Industries, Inc. has developed a polyester-nylon composite fibre containing at least 93% recycled material by mass, marking a significant step towards incorporating higher levels of recycled raw materials into sophisticated textile products. The development builds on the company’s expertise in polymer design and composite spinning, drawing on technologies cultivated through its recycled fibre brand. The 93% recycled-content figure applies to the newly developed raw yarn, calculated against its total weight. It does not represent the recycled content of the finished fabric or garment, which will vary according to the material composition. Overcoming Challenges in Composite Fibre Development Composite fibres are valued for their ability to deliver enhanced functionality, sophisticated textures and distinctive visual effects. However, incorporating different polymers into a single fibre presents challenges when manufacturers seek to maximise recycled-material content while maintaining consistent quality. Toray has addressed this challenge through its proprietary polymer design and composite spinning technologies, incorporating recycled raw materials into both the polyester and nylon components of the newly developed fibre. The company plans to verify the technology’s viability for mass production while continuing research to increase the recycled-material content of composite fibres. articles.o: Andritz to supply PTFE filter line to China
articles.s: Shandong Huazhe has placed an order with Andritz for a high-speed needlepunch line to produce advanced filtration materials. The line will be installed at the company’s headquarters in Jinan, Shandong Province, China. This order builds on the cooperation between the two companies that began in 2023
articles.x: Shandong Huazhe has placed an order with Andritz for a high-speed needlepunch line to produce advanced filtration materials. The line will be installed at the company’s headquarters in Jinan, Shandong Province, China. This order builds on the cooperation between the two companies that began in 2023 with the contract for an Andritz batt forming line, which was successfully delivered in 2024. The new line will expand Shandong Huazhe’s production capacity for high-performance filtration materials made from polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) fibres, addressing the growing demand in this market. It is designed for high-speed, stable operation and the gentle handling of fibres, ensuring consistently high product quality. The line will feature the first commercial application of the A-Type needleloom, a new addition to the Andritz needleloom portfolio, combining cost-efficient operation, production flexibility and high product quality. Its random needle pattern capability helps improve material uniformity and performance. It will also be the first PTFE filtration material production line supplied by Andritz. “The production of advanced filtration materials requires reliable equipment and gentle fibre processing,” says Shandong Huazhe CEO Han Fuhe. “Based on our positive experience with Andritz, we are confident that the new needlepunch line will provide the quality, efficiency and process stability we need for our future growth.” Founded in 2015, Shandong Huazhe is a leading provider of filtration solutions, specialising in materials and equipment for solid-liquid separation and industrial dust collection. www.andritz.com The post Andritz to supply PTFE filter line to China appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .

articles.s: The Textile Innovation Awards 2026, a prestigious recognition platform celebrating innovation and excellence in Bangladesh’s textile and apparel industry, was officially launched today through a p...
articles.x: The Textile Innovation Awards 2026 , a prestigious recognition platform celebrating innovation and excellence in Bangladesh’s textile and apparel industry, was officially launched today through a press conference held today at the Dongyi Sourcing Limited (DSL) Multipurpose Hall in Dhaka. The second edition of the Textile Innovation Awards is designed to recognize organizations and individuals whose innovations create measurable impact in factory operations, technology, product development, sustainability, market development and organizational transformation. The Textile Innovation Awards 2026 will be presented on 13 November 2026. Figure: The Textile Innovation Award 2026 will be evaluated by a distinguished Jury Board comprising industry leaders, academics and professionals. The Award has established itself as an important industry recognition platform following its inaugural edition in 2024, when several prominent textile and apparel manufacturers and organizations were recognized for their achievements in different areas of innovation. Award recipients included Urmi Group for Product Development, Shasha Denims for Marketing or Market Development, Masco Group for Garment Processing, and Coats Bangladesh for HR and Organizational Development. Figure 2: Prof. Dr. Engr. Ayub Nabi Khan, Vice Chancellor, BUFT Building on the success of the first edition, the 2026 Award aims to bring greater visibility to practical innovations being developed and implemented across Bangladesh’s textile and apparel value chain. This year, awards will be considered across eight categories: Process Innovation, Manufacturing Innovation, Technology, Product Development, Marketing or Market Development, Environmental Sustainability, Social Sustainability, and HR and Organizational Development. articles.o: YarnProof links polyester origin checks to regional trade compliance
articles.s: Eleven polyester filament yarn manufacturers across North and Central America have launched YarnProof, a traceability initiative that uses embedded physical markers to verify yarn origin. The system a...
articles.x: Eleven polyester filament yarn manufacturers across North and Central America have launched YarnProof, a traceability initiative that uses embedded physical markers to verify yarn origin. The system aims to strengthen compliance with regional trade agreements and help brands substantiate sourcing claims. Figure: YarnProof is designed to support the yarn-forward requirements of the Dominican Republic-Central America-United States Free Trade Agreement (CAFTA-DR) and the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA). Led by Unifi and powered by FibreTrace technology, YarnProof embeds an invisible, permanent tracer into polyester filament yarn during extrusion. A handheld scanner can detect the marker in yarn, fabric, and finished goods, providing physical evidence of material origin as products move through the supply chain. The initiative includes Aquafil O'Mara, CS America, CS Central America, Nan Ya Plastics America, Premiere Fibers, Sans Americas, Skytex México, Tecnología Textil Avanzada, Textufil, Unifi Manufacturing and United Textiles of America. Trade compliance is a key driver. YarnProof is designed to support the yarn-forward requirements of the Dominican Republic-Central America-United States Free Trade Agreement (CAFTA-DR) and the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA). These rules make the origin of yarn and other textile inputs important for determining whether qualifying goods receive preferential trade treatment. The initiative also highlights a wider industry shift toward physical verification. Unifi already uses its FiberPrint tracer in REPREVE recycled fibers, with its U-TRUST system verifying recycled-content claims across the supply chain. articles.o: Light-activated wound patch for targeted drug delivery
articles.s: Researchers at Swiss materials research institute Empa have developed a light-responsive material that could enable wound dressings to deliver precisely controlled doses of antiseptics and other therapeutic agents, potentially improving the treatment of chronic wounds. Developed at Empa’s Biomimetic
articles.x: Researchers at Swiss materials research institute Empa have developed a light-responsive material that could enable wound dressings to deliver precisely controlled doses of antiseptics and other therapeutic agents, potentially improving the treatment of chronic wounds. Developed at Empa’s Biomimetic Membranes and Textiles laboratory in St. Gallen, the technology uses nanoparticles coated with a light-sensitive polymer to release active ingredients when exposed to visible LED light. Switching off the light stops the release, allowing the timing and dosage of treatment to be controlled. The research could have particular significance for patients with diabetes, who are vulnerable to chronic wounds caused by poor circulation and nerve damage. Diabetic foot ulcers can remain open for months, requiring frequent dressing changes, specialist care and repeated hospital visits. The Empa team, led by Luciano Boesel and Giorgia Giovannini, has developed a system based on silica nanoparticles loaded with chlorhexidine, a widely used wound antiseptic. The nanoparticles are surrounded by a polymer coating containing molecular photoswitches that change their structure when exposed to specific wavelengths of visible light. This causes the polymer to swell and become more permeable to water, allowing the disinfectant to escape from the silica core. When the light is switched off, the polymer contracts and returns to its original, less permeable state, restricting further release. © Empa “When incorporated into a wound patch, this system enables controlled wound disinfection,” explains Boesel. “The timing and dose of the released active ingredient can be controlled by varying the duration or intensity of the light exposure and the wavelength of the light.” The approach could offer advant

articles.t: 동화대학교, 전자회로 내장된 세탁 가능한 섬유 개발
articles.o: Donghua University develops washable fibers with built-in electronic circuits
articles.s: Researchers at Donghua University in Shanghai, China, have developed a programmable microfluidic spinning method that integrates electronic circuits directly into soft fibers. Published in Nature Elec...
articles.x: Researchers at Donghua University in Shanghai, China, have developed a programmable microfluidic spinning method that integrates electronic circuits directly into soft fibers. Published in Nature Electronics by a team led by Professor Zhu Meifang and researcher Wang Gang, the technology enables smart garments that sense, process, and respond to data without external electronic attachments. Conventional electronic textiles rely on conductive yarns to connect separate microchips, sensors, and heating elements. These connections often degrade under mechanical stress from stretching, bending, and laundering. Donghua University addresses this weakness by building functional electronic structures inside the fiber during spinning. The research demonstrates electroluminescent fibers for light emission, resistor and capacitor fibers for signal processing, organic electrochemical transistor fibers for digital logic operations, and functional fibers for touchless sensing. The development aligns with broader advances across material and machinery sectors. Belgian supplier Bekaert manufactures Bekinox stainless steel fibers blended with cotton or polyester for data and energy transmission. German machinery builder ZSK Stickmaschinen uses its EP-30 device to position and connect circuit boards onto textile substrates during embroidery. However, while ZSK attaches components during processing, Donghua University embeds electronic functions within the core fiber structure. Potential applications span healthcare monitoring, athletic performance tracking, industrial protective wear, and soft robotics. Nevertheless, commercial adoption depends on scalable manufacturing. articles.o: TANATEX and Transfar Chemicals Bring Global Teams Together at 2026 Global Technology Conference in the Netherlands
articles.s: TANATEX Chemicals and Transfar Chemicals brought together approximately 70 colleagues representing 22 nationalities for the 2026 Global Technology Conference, held from 6 to 8 October in the Netherlands. The three-day event focused on knowledge sharing, technical expertise, market insights and inter
articles.x: TANATEX Chemicals and Transfar Chemicals brought together approximately 70 colleagues representing 22 nationalities for the 2026 Global Technology Conference, held from 6 to 8 October in the Netherlands. The three-day event focused on knowledge sharing, technical expertise, market insights and international collaboration to address the evolving challenges of the textile industry. The conference provided a platform for colleagues from different regions to exchange perspectives, discuss business priorities and explore opportunities to strengthen the companies’ global operations. Discussions covered technology and product strategies, market developments and real-life business cases, highlighting the importance of collaboration across diverse markets. A key component of the programme was a series of interactive workshops in which international teams explored new business opportunities, product globalisation, cross-market collaboration and regional product plans for 2027. Participants presented their ideas and proposals, encouraging dialogue and alignment on future business priorities. The conference also highlighted strategies to strengthen global customer engagement, enhance technical support and deliver greater value to customers across international markets. By bringing together technical knowledge and regional market experience, the event aimed to support more coordinated approaches to customer needs and industry challenges. Beyond technical sessions and strategic discussions, the gathering offered an opportunity to strengthen professional relationships among colleagues who work across different countries and regions. articles.o: Growing consumer preference for natural fibres as Woolmark launches Return to Real
articles.s: Fashion’s next premium story may be written on the fibre label. As people become more selective about what they buy and wear, the material behind a garment is taking on… The post Growing consumer preference for natural fibres as Woolmark launches Return to Real appeared first on The Textile Magazine
articles.x: Fashion’s next premium story may be written on the fibre label. As people become more selective about what they buy and wear, the material behind a garment is taking on new importance. New research commissioned to Ipsos by Woolmark across the United States, France, Germany, Italy and China found that on average, 82% of consumers would choose natural fibres over synthetic alternatives when price, style and fit are equal. Merinowool was preferred to polyester in every market surveyed, with an average preference of 65%. The findings point to a wider shift in fashion. Worldwide Google search interest in “Merinowool” has more than doubled over the past five years, with momentum continuing to build over the past 12 months. Fibre is no longer simply a technical or sourcing decision. It is becoming part of how consumers understand quality, performance and value. “Consumers want to know what a garment is made from, what that means in everyday use and whether the claims can be trusted,” said Woolmark Managing Director Bryan Fry. “That puts fibre, and the evidence behind it, back at the centre of the conversation.” Merino wool’s strongest distinction is its association with premium quality. In the latest Ipsos research, it ranked first for both premium and high quality in four of the five markets surveyed. The survey also reveals that citizens are prepared to pay for the difference. On average across the five markets, 67% say they would pay more for clothing made mainly from natural fibres. Merino wool’s premium perception is increasingly supported by its performance credentials. Brands are taking the fibre beyond traditional tailoring and knitwear into technical sportswear and elevated essentials for a more refined material story. articles.o: From textile waste to spinning-grade fiber: STADLER Group engineers integrated sorting solution for IGERS in Italy
articles.s: As technology partner, STADLER worked alongside IGERS on its new plant in San Pietro Mosezzo, Novara, from the first process discussions to the final layout – integrating key treatment equipment… The post From textile waste to spinning-grade fiber: STADLER Group engineers integrated sorting solution
articles.x: As technology partner, STADLER worked alongside IGERS on its new plant in San Pietro Mosezzo, Novara, from the first process discussions to the final layout – integrating key treatment equipment into one system and supplying the fully automated sorting line. Together, the two companies have taken IGERS’ patented textile recycling process from vision to industrial reality STADLER Group, the globally active German company specialized in the planning, production and assembly of turnkey sorting plants, has acted as technology partner to IGERS s.r.l. in the development of its new textile recycling plant in San Pietro Mosezzo, in the province of Novara, Piedmont. STADLER supported IGERS throughout the design phase, from the earliest discussions on process requirements through to a plant layout designed to fit the existing building. It integrated key treatment equipment purchased by IGERS so that the individual process steps work together as one system, and designed and supplied the fully automated sorting line. “STADLER worked with us not simply as a supplier, but as a technology partner, understanding the specific requirements of a project that is both new and ambitious within the Italian context,” says Gian Luca Miceli, CEO of IGERS. Inaugurated on 21 September 2026, the San Pietro Mosezzo facility is the first plant in Italy to include all treatment phases of textile recycling, producing high-quality flakes and frayed material from post-consumer and post-industrial textile waste, with full traceability throughout the process. It has a capacity of 4 t/h and is authorized to process up to 19,200 tonnes of textile waste per year. The total investment amounts to approximately €8 million, including €1.3 million in co-financing from Italy’s National Recovery and Resilience Plan

articles.o: Italian textile machinery manufacturers target Brazil
articles.s: A delegation of 22 Italian companies will visit Brazil from 19 to 24 October 2026 as part of a trade mission aimed at strengthening commercial and industrial cooperation between the two countries’ textile sectors. Organised by the Italian Trade Agency in collaboration with ACIMIT, the Association of
articles.x: A delegation of 22 Italian companies will visit Brazil from 19 to 24 October 2026 as part of a trade mission aimed at strengthening commercial and industrial cooperation between the two countries’ textile sectors. Organised by the Italian Trade Agency in collaboration with ACIMIT, the Association of Italian Textile Machinery Manufacturers, and Confindustria Moda, the initiative will include workshops on 20 October in Santa Catarina and 22 October in São Paulo. The delegation comprises 18 textile machinery manufacturers alongside companies specialising in yarns, fabrics and clothing accessories, representing expertise across the Italian textile supply chain. The programme will feature technical presentations, business-to-business meetings with Brazilian manufacturers and visits to local production facilities. Activities in Santa Catarina will cover the textile manufacturing centres of Blumenau, Joinville and Brusque, while the São Paulo programme will include Americana and Denim City São Paulo, an important hub for textile and denim innovation. Brazil remains a strategically important market for Italian textile machinery manufacturers. Exports to the country reached €48 million in 2025, with a further €20 million recorded during the first half of 2026. Brazil currently ranks tenth among the industry’s leading export destinations. Finishing machinery accounts for the largest share of Italian textile machinery exports to Brazil at 57%, followed by accessories and other machinery, each representing 11%. Knitting machinery accounts for 10%, highlighting opportunities for Italian technology suppliers serving Brazil’s established knitwear and textile manufacturing industries. articles.t: Polestar가 시그니처 위브를 더하다
articles.o: Polestar adds a signature weave
articles.s: Bcomp has partnered with Polestar to bring its lightweight bio-based materials into the new Polestar 5 four-door electric grand tourer (GT). The vehicle features Bcomp’s ampliTex and powerRibs technologies in the front seatbacks and tailgate structure, reducing the use of virgin plastics. The collab
articles.x: Bcomp has partnered with Polestar to bring its lightweight bio-based materials into the new Polestar 5 four-door electric grand tourer (GT). The vehicle features Bcomp’s ampliTex and powerRibs technologies in the front seatbacks and tailgate structure, reducing the use of virgin plastics. The collaboration between the two companies began during the development of the Polestar Precept, a concept car, and evolved into large-scale production for the Polestar 5. Together, the companies developed a bespoke ampliTex flax fabric known as the ‘Polestar Signature Weave’, designed to serve both structural and aesthetic functions in the interior cabin. This material has since become a defining feature of Polestar’s minimalist and transparent design approach, engineered and tested for durability and performance across thousands of cars in global markets. Polestar credits Bcomp’s flax-based composites with using 50% less fossil-based material and being up to 40% lighter than the traditional plastics they replace. Depending on the application, Bcomp’s natural fibre composites can also reduce the cradle-to-gate CO2 footprint of components by up to 60%. All Bcomp components used in the vehicle have been validated to meet stringent automotive standards for durability, safety, UV resistance, scratch resistance and long-term ageing performance. © Bcomp “Working with Polestar over a number of years has given us the opportunity to show that the path from a material concept to a series-production component can be long and rigorous but is ultimately worth it,” says Per Martensson, chief revenue officer at Bcomp. “The Polestar 5 seatbacks have a combination of lightweighting performance, reduced carbon footprint and design for end-of-life that conventional composites cannot offer. articles.x: This year’s program adds an honorarium for three students who performed well in SSC TEAM Group has awarded the Wahid-Kohinoor Memorial Scholarship 2026 to 36 meritorious students of Hazi Piar Ali School, the school located adjacent to its 4A Yarn Dyeing Ltd. facility in Savar. The annual ceremony was graced by the presence of Managing Director Afroza Shaheen and Deputy Managing Director Abdullah Hil Nakib. This year, 18 primary-level students (KG to Class 5), 15 high-school students (Classes 6 to 10) and 3 SSC graduates were recognized. At both the primary and high-school levels, the scholarship was awarded on merit by position, with the first, second, and third position-holders of each class from KG to Class 10 receiving the award. New this year: Three students who achieved good results in the SSC examination also received an honorarium, extending the program’s recognition beyond the school’s regular classes. A high-level delegation from the Kingdom of the Netherlands – Mr. Steven Collet, Vice Minister for International Cooperation; Ms. Wampie Libon, Ambassador for Sustainable Development; and Ambassador Joris van Bommel – visited 4A Yarn Dyeing Ltd., TEAM Group’s LEED Platinum-certified facility, to see how investments and Dutch-Bangladesh partnerships are advancing sustainability in the textile sector. The delegation briefly joined the scholarship event as the program began, before departing. Addressing the students, Managing Director Afroza Shaheen urged them to carry their values as far as their grades. “You have already proven yourselves through your merit and achievements. articles.o: MAXXAM and ApparelTASKER return to Cannes
articles.s: British textile innovator MAXXAM Textiles and East London-based garment manufacturer ApparelTASKER will return to Cannes later this month for Mare di Moda 2026, the international exhibition for swimwear, lingerie and athleisure fabrics, with an expanded collection of stretch textiles and garments fo
articles.x: British textile innovator MAXXAM Textiles and East London-based garment manufacturer ApparelTASKER will return to Cannes later this month for Mare di Moda 2026, the international exhibition for swimwear, lingerie and athleisure fabrics, with an expanded collection of stretch textiles and garments for Summer 2027. The event, taking place from 27-29 October, will provide a European showcase for the British partnership, which was formed at Mare di Moda just one year ago and has since developed new garment applications for MAXXAM’s distinctive crinkle-textured stretch fabric. Created by textile designer Rosemary Moore in the early 1980s, MAXXAM is a seamless, four-way stretch textile with a three-dimensional crinkled surface that expands and contracts to accommodate different body shapes. The innovation is represented in the permanent collection of London’s Victoria and Albert Museum. MAXXAM founder and textile designer Rosemary Moore. © MAXXAM Textiles For Summer 2027, the companies will present new garment silhouettes and a vibrant colour palette featuring citrus orange, lime green and bright red, demonstrating the textile’s versatility in contemporary fashion applications. The collaboration began when Moore met ApparelTASKER founder Zack Sartor at Mare di Moda in 2025. Their shared interest in textile innovation, responsible manufacturing and garment development has since evolved into an ongoing partnership. “What started with a conversation between Zack and me has developed into something really creative, and we’re continuing to discover new possibilities for MAXXAM textiles through colour, shape and garment design,” said Moore. “I’ve always believed that heritage and innovation should sit side by side. articles.t: Welspun Living, WelVisionAi를 통해 AI 기반 제조 발전
articles.o: Welspun Living advances AI-Powered Manufacturing with WelVisionAi
articles.s: Welspun Living is taking another step towards intelligent manufacturing with the launch of WelVisionAi, an AI-powered computer vision initiative designed to bring artificial intelligence directly to the shop floor. Developed… The post Welspun Living advances AI-Powered Manufacturing with WelVisionAi
articles.x: Welspun Living is taking another step towards intelligent manufacturing with the launch of WelVisionAi, an AI-powered computer vision initiative designed to bring artificial intelligence directly to the shop floor. Developed through the Welspun USA Operations and IT teams, WelVisionAi transforms live manufacturing activity into continuous, actionable intelligence. By using computer vision to observe and analyse shop-floor operations, the system can see, measure and identify patterns across manufacturing processes. The initiative is designed to provide greater visibility into key operational parameters, including production output, machine utilisation, throughput, efficiency and safety. By converting real-time factory activity into meaningful intelligence, WelVisionAi can help manufacturing teams identify patterns, respond faster and continuously improve operations. The initiative reflects Welspun Living’s broader ambition to build a more visible, connected, intelligent and responsive manufacturing environment, where people, data and technology work together to strengthen operational capabilities. Brand-Promotion According to Mr. Keyur Parekh, the initiative represents the next phase of Welspun’s manufacturing journey, bringing AI “from the screen to the shop floor.” The broader vision of Welspun Living, under Dipali Goenka, Managing Director & CEO, is to continually evolve the organisation by harnessing technology, innovation and human ingenuity to build stronger capabilities and unlock new possibilities. WelVisionAi marks the beginning of this journey, with AI moving beyond a technology concept to become an integral layer of intelligence within manufacturing operations. articles.x: Lalmonirhat Textile Institute organized its first industrial visit of 2026 to Arunima Sportswear Limited, part of Arunima Group, on October 3, 2026, at its facility on Dewan Idris Road, Pukurpar, Zirabo, Savar, Dhaka. The visit was led by the institute’s Principal, Engr. Md. Moynul Hassan Shibly , whose leadership supported the initiative to connect students’ theoretical knowledge with practical industrial experience. The visit aimed to bridge the gap between classroom learning and real-world industrial practices. Through this initiative, students explored the industrial working environment, developed a better understanding of manufacturing operations, and gained insights into the practical applications of their academic knowledge. Industrial visits play an important role in textile education by allowing students to observe industry practices beyond textbooks and laboratory sessions. Such experiences help them understand production processes, workplace requirements, and the professional skills needed to build successful careers in the textile and apparel sector. The joint initiative by Textile Club and Lalmonirhat Textile Institute reflects their commitment to enhancing students’ practical knowledge and strengthening connections between academic institutions and the industry. The visit to Arunima Sportswear Limited offered participating students a valuable learning opportunity, encouraging them to connect theoretical concepts with industrial experience and prepare for future professional challenges in the textile and apparel industry. articles.t: Cyclothe는 재활용 과정에서 누락된 고리를 겨냥합니다.
articles.o: Cyclothe targets missing links in recycling
articles.s: Swedish technology company Cyclothe is developing an integrated system for collecting, identifying and sorting discarded textiles, with the aim of addressing one of the biggest obstacles to Europe’s emerging circular textile economy – the lack of infrastructure connecting waste collection with comme
articles.x: Swedish technology company Cyclothe is developing an integrated system for collecting, identifying and sorting discarded textiles, with the aim of addressing one of the biggest obstacles to Europe’s emerging circular textile economy – the lack of infrastructure connecting waste collection with commercially viable reuse and recycling operations. The company’s approach combines smart collection points, automated material identification, AI-supported sorting decisions and digital traceability to direct discarded textiles towards their most appropriate destinations. Rather than concentrating exclusively on recycling, Cyclothe aims to prioritise reuse, repair and resale wherever possible, before directing materials that cannot be recovered in these ways towards textile recycling operations. The intention is to connect consumers, retailers, municipalities, logistics providers and recycling companies through a common physical and digital infrastructure, enabling collected materials to be identified, tracked and channelled into appropriate markets. The mandatory separate collection of textiles was introduced in Europe at the beginning of 2025, but the infrastructure needed to process the resulting material streams remains fragmented. The introduction of extended producer responsibility (EPR) requirements is expected to increase pressure on brands and retailers to participate in more effective systems for recovering discarded products. Cyclothe is now preparing to expand its technology across the Nordic countries and wider Europe, appointing Calvin Woolley, formerly sustainable business manager for textiles at Inter Ikea, as co-founder and CEO to lead the next stage of its development. articles.o: Consumers favour natural fibres, says Woolmark
articles.s: Woolmark, the global authority on wool fibre certification and promotion, is putting Merino wool’s natural performance credentials at the centre of a new international campaign, backed by consumer research showing a strong preference for natural fibres over synthetics. The Australian wool industry’s
articles.x: Woolmark, the global authority on wool fibre certification and promotion, is putting Merino wool’s natural performance credentials at the centre of a new international campaign, backed by consumer research showing a strong preference for natural fibres over synthetics. The Australian wool industry’s marketing and certification organisation has launched Return to Real following an Ipsos study across the United States, France, Germany, Italy and China, which found that 82% of consumers would choose natural fibres over synthetics when price, style and fit are equal. Merino wool was preferred to polyester in all five markets, with an average preference of 65%, while 67% of respondents said they would pay more for clothing made mainly from natural fibres. “Consumers want to know what a garment is made from, what that means in everyday use and whether the claims can be trusted,” said Woolmark Managing Director Bryan Fry. “That puts fibre, and the evidence behind it, back at the centre of the conversation.” Merino wool ranked first for both premium and high quality perceptions in four of the five markets surveyed. Meanwhile, 71% of respondents considered independent certification or verification of fibre content and quality important, while 45% said fibre composition had become more important in their purchasing decisions. Beyond traditional Woolmark says growing interest in natural materials is creating opportunities for Merino wool beyond traditional knitwear and tailoring, particularly in technical sportswear, performance apparel and premium everyday clothing. Global Google search interest in Merino wool has more than doubled over the past five years. articles.o: Over 95% efficiency on meltblown lines with new PLA
articles.s: TotalEnergies Corbion, headquartered in Gorinchem, the Netherlands, has commercially launched a new polylactic acid (PLA) grade specifically developed for meltblown nonwoven filter media, following industrial trials demonstrating filtration efficiencies exceeding 95%. The new Luminy L040 grade can b
articles.x: TotalEnergies Corbion, headquartered in Gorinchem, the Netherlands, has commercially launched a new polylactic acid (PLA) grade specifically developed for meltblown nonwoven filter media, following industrial trials demonstrating filtration efficiencies exceeding 95%. The new Luminy L040 grade can be processed on existing meltblown production lines without major equipment modifications, enabling manufacturers to produce ultra-fine fibres with diameters of one micron or less from a biobased alternative to conventional polypropylene (PP). A key characteristic of the material is its ability to retain an electrostatic charge, which is essential for capturing fine airborne particles without creating excessive resistance to airflow. The combination of ultra-low viscosity and electrostatic properties enables high-efficiency filter media to be produced without the degrading agents or electrostatic additives that would otherwise be required. “During the early-access programme, industrial partners including Hansae in South Korea successfully processed Luminy L040 on commercial meltblown lines, demonstrating stable production, ultra-fine fibre formation and filtration efficiencies exceeding 95%,” says Bert Clymans, EMEA senior business development and nonwovens market segment leader at TotalEnergies Corbion. The launch also follows independent research by the University of Michigan indicating that PLA-based meltblown media can achieve filtration performance comparable to conventional PP materials. Made from annually renewable feedstocks, the new PLA grade is said to have a carbon footprint more than 80% lower than PP, offering filter manufacturers a potential route to reducing the embodied emissions of their products. articles.x: Starting from the upcoming Spring Edition of Intertextile Shanghai Apparel Fabrics – set to take place from 10 to 12 March 2027 – the organisers have signalled their intention to anchor the show’s evolving positioning with a new slogan: Shape the Movement. Equipped with its refined focus, Intertextile Apparel is set to showcase its continued importance for defining the industry’s future – from creating and implementing new trends, to exchanging cultural ideas, functional utility and eco-innovation, to enabling business deals with far-reaching economic benefits. Several high-potential areas have been earmarked for further development next spring. New slogan ‘Shape the Movement’ and key visual for Intertextile Shanghai Apparel Fabrics – Spring Edition 2027 (second from right) alongside other textile fairs’ wallscapes at NECC this autumn (Source: Messe Frankfurt) The fair’s key themes Fashion Forward, Textile Future, Performance Textiles, and Sustainability will again reflect the demands of the global textile market, with the latter two showing especially strong potential in the current landscape. Ms Wilmet Shea, General Manager of Messe Frankfurt (HK) Ltd , commented: “Shaping the industry’s movement is exactly what this fair does, at every edition. The new slogan is a nod to Intertextile Apparel’s unmatched influence in determining what vast numbers of global consumers want to wear, how they want to wear it, and how industry players can make that happen. articles.o: Spinning a good yarn
articles.s: Fiber Extrusion Technology Limited (FET) took a major role at the Dornbirn Global Fiber Congress in Austria in September, with Dr Jonny Hunter presenting “Spinning a good yarn.” The exhibition brought together over 100 expert speakers, leading innovators, and global stakeholders for a focused progra
articles.x: Fiber Extrusion Technology Limited (FET) took a major role at the Dornbirn Global Fiber Congress in Austria in September, with Dr Jonny Hunter presenting “Spinning a good yarn.” The exhibition brought together over 100 expert speakers, leading innovators, and global stakeholders for a focused program of events. Over 400 attendees came from a range of industrial and academic organizations. Industrial examples included Barmag, Sembis, and Fraunhofer, while from the academic world CETI (France), Aachen (Germany), Fibernamics (Portugal), and many others were present. As global challenges mount – from decarbonization pressures to shifting markets – this year’s congress reaffirmed its role as a key platform for forward-looking solutions and collaborative progress. Hunter’s presentation took a broad view of the immense challenges and innovations that have emerged in the fiber industry over recent years. FET has been at the forefront of many of these innovations – designing, developing, and manufacturing bespoke fiber equipment, thus enabling customers in a wide range of industries to find solutions to their individual challenges. FET’s reputation has been founded predominantly on melt spinning solutions – in multifilament, monofilament and nonwoven formats – and the first part of the presentation highlighted this aspect. However, FET’s more recent success has been grounded in further niche developments and technological variations: Meltblown systems for non-continuous nonwoven fibers. Spunbond equipment for continuous nonwovens. Wet spinning systems, where melt spinning solutions are not possible. articles.x: Mayer & Cie. Global will focus on mattress ticking production and fine-gauge double-face fabrics at ITMA Asia + CITME 2026, taking place in Shanghai from 20-24 November. The German circular knitting machine manufacturer will showcase two established models, introduce its new portfolio strategy and provide an update on machinery development at its Albstadt headquarters. Taking centre stage will be the OVJA 2.4 EM, a high-productivity circular knitting machine designed for mattress ticking, alongside the OV 3.2 QCe, configured to produce double-face fabrics in the exceptionally fine E40 gauge. The OVJA 2.4 EM. © Mayer & Cie. Global “Around 70 per cent of the world’s mattress fabric production takes place in China,” said Alton Xu, CEO of Mayer & Cie. Global. “Our OVJA family offers excellent solutions for this application. The OVJA 2.4 EM in particular combines maximum output with extensive patterning options.” The OVJA 2.4 EM produces up to 30kg of fabric per hour, supported by a feeder density of 2.4 feeders per inch. Its horizontal weft yarn guide facilitates operation and rapid changeovers, while improved yarn guidance and a pneumatic cross-flow nozzle maintain consistent yarn tension at high speeds, minimising vibration and ensuring reliable yarn feeding. Electronic individual needle selection in the cylinder provides extensive patterning possibilities and enables rapid design changes, making the machine particularly suitable for the demanding mattress ticking market. The OVJA 2.4 EM offers a wide variety of patterns. © Mayer & Cie. articles.o: Better Cotton Initiative becomes a regenerative standard system
articles.s: The Better Cotton Initiative (BCI) today announced that it is now officially operating as a regenerative standard system – marking a major milestone for the world’s largest cotton sustainability scheme, which has over 20% of the world’s cotton production aligned to its standard. Building on more tha
articles.x: The Better Cotton Initiative (BCI) today announced that it is now officially operating as a regenerative standard system – marking a major milestone for the world’s largest cotton sustainability scheme, which has over 20% of the world’s cotton production aligned to its standard. Building on more than 15 years of supporting locally relevant regenerative practices across cotton-growing communities, the move marks the next stage in BCI’s effort to drive healthier soils, more resilient ecosystems and stronger farmer livelihoods at scale. As the industry increasingly looks to regeneratively farmed cotton as a foundation for sustainable sourcing, BCI is helping to bridge the gap between regenerative ambitions and farming realities, ensuring that progress is driven through genuine partnership with farmers and backed by measurable outcomes. The move to a regenerative standard system reinforces farmer support through stronger requirements, targeted capacity strengthening and improved impact measurement. For retailers, brands and suppliers, it provides a reliable means of setting and meeting corporate regenerative sourcing targets, while BCI’s traceable offering opens the door to product-level claims. Nick Weatherill, Chief Executive Officer of BCI, said: “ Our transition to a regenerative standard system is about unlocking a triple win for nature, farmers and industry. When nature thrives, farmers thrive. And when retailers and brands support those conditions through their sourcing and investment, they help build more resilient supply chains and future-proof the supply of cotton. “As the world’s largest cotton sustainability organisation, we are uniquely positioned to drive change across the entire cotton supply chain. articles.o: China tightens textile wastewater regulations
articles.s: China has introduced new wastewater regulations requiring textile dyeing and finishing plants to demonstrate that their treated effluent does not cause unacceptable toxicity to fish embryos, marking a significant shift in environmental compliance for the country’s textile industry. The new national
articles.x: China has introduced new wastewater regulations requiring textile dyeing and finishing plants to demonstrate that their treated effluent does not cause unacceptable toxicity to fish embryos, marking a significant shift in environmental compliance for the country’s textile industry. The new national standard, GB 4287-2026, came into effect on 1 September 2026 for new, rebuilt and expanded facilities, with existing plants required to comply from 1 January 2028. It introduces fish egg toxicity testing alongside conventional chemical discharge limits, placing greater emphasis on the combined environmental impact of textile wastewater. According to Swiss textile sustainability specialist bluesign, the change represents an important development in wastewater management, moving beyond measuring individual pollutants to assessing the biological effects of treated effluent. The standard, published by China’s Ministry of Ecology and Environment and State Administration for Market Regulation in June, replaces four earlier standards covering dyeing and finishing, silk reeling, wool and hemp processing. It also extends regulatory coverage to chemical fibre weaving and industrial textile products. The new toxicity requirement applies to dyeing and finishing operations discharging treated wastewater directly into rivers, lakes or other water bodies, as well as dedicated textile industry wastewater treatment plants. Purely physical finishing operations are excluded. Under the test procedure, newly fertilised zebrafish embryos are exposed to a solution containing one part treated wastewater to five parts dilution water for 48 hours at 26°C. articles.o: Bhilosa Industries proposes ₹2,500-Crore investment in Madhya Pradesh
articles.s: Proposed polyester manufacturing hub at Dhar’s PM MITRA Park could create 3,750 direct jobs and strengthen the state’s man-made fibre ecosystem. Bhilosa Industries Private Limited (BIPL), one of India’s leading… The post Bhilosa Industries proposes ₹2,500-Crore investment in Madhya Pradesh appeared
articles.x: Proposed polyester manufacturing hub at Dhar’s PM MITRA Park could create 3,750 direct jobs and strengthen the state’s man-made fibre ecosystem. Bhilosa Industries Private Limited (BIPL), one of India’s leading polyester yarn manufacturers, has proposed a phased investment of ₹2,500 crore in Madhya Pradesh to establish an integrated polyester manufacturing facility at the PM MITRA Park in Dhar district. According to media reports, the project will begin with an initial investment of ₹2,500 crore, with commercial production targeted to commence in 2028. The proposed development is expected to generate approximately 3,750 direct employment opportunities. The company is in the final stages of selecting around 300 acres at the park, including 200 acres for textile manufacturing and another 100 acres for supporting industrial units. Building an Integrated Polyester Ecosystem The proposed facility is expected to manufacture polyester yarn, fibres, knitted fabrics and man-made fibre-based non-garment textiles. The project could also encourage the development of ancillary industries, strengthening the regional textile supply chain and creating opportunities for smaller manufacturers and suppliers. Located within the Dhar–Indore industrial belt, the proposed facility would add to Madhya Pradesh’s ambitions to develop an integrated textile manufacturing ecosystem through the PM MITRA initiative. Strengthening Bhilosa’s Manufacturing Footprint Bhilosa Industries has established a strong presence in India’s polyester value chain through continuous capacity expansion and backward and forward integration. Barmag is a leading provider of man-made fiber filament spinning systems, texturing machines, BCF systems, staple fiber systems, and solutions for producing nonwovens. Together with its range of polycondensation and extrusion systems and their key components, Barmag caters to the entire manufacturing process – from the monomer all the way through to the textured yarn – and supports it with customer-oriented engineering services. The product portfolio is rounded off with automation and digital solutions. Barmag also offers high-precision gear metering pumps for the textile industry and other sectors, including automotive, chemical, and paint. Manufacturers worldwide are facing increasing pressure from energy costs, sustainability requirements, labor shortages, and the need to remain competitive in highly dynamic markets. At the same time, demand for high-quality man-made fibers continues to create opportunities, particularly in applications where performance, consistency, and cost efficiency are critical. We at Barmag see potential in advanced polyester and polyamide production, recycled materials, technical textiles and increasingly automated manufacturing processes. articles.t: BEZAKTIV Salt Advisor, CHT 섬유 염료 앱 강화
articles.o: BEZAKTIV Salt Advisor Enhances CHT Textile Dyes App
articles.s: New digital solution optimizes salt usage in reactive dyeing and unlocks cost-saving potential. The CHT Group continues to expand its digital service offering for textile finishers. With the new BEZAKTIV Salt Advisor, the company enhances its successful CHT Textile Dyes App with an innovative calcul
articles.x: New digital solution optimizes salt usage in reactive dyeing and unlocks cost-saving potential. The CHT Group continues to expand its digital service offering for textile finishers. With the new BEZAKTIV Salt Advisor, the company enhances its successful CHT Textile Dyes App with an innovative calculation tool that supports users in achieving cost-effective and resource-efficient cotton dyeing with BEZAKTIV reactive dyes. Over the past years, the CHT Textile Dyes App has established itself as a valuable tool for textile finishing companies. In addition to providing access to the comprehensive range of dyes and pigments offered by the CHT Group, the app includes various digital tools designed to optimize production processes while reducing water, energy, time, and operating costs. The BEZAKTIV Salt Advisor now adds another practical solution to this portfolio. In reactive cotton dyeing, salt concentration plays a crucial role. Salt increases the substantivity of the dye for the fiber, thereby increasing dye uptake. At the same time, the amount of salt used influences not only dye consumption but also overall process costs. In practice, standard tables are often used to provide general recommendations for different shade depths. However, these recommendations do not take into account the specific conditions of an individual dye recipe, leaving significant optimization potential untapped. The new BEZAKTIV Salt Advisor offers an intelligent solution to this challenge. It is based on a mathematical model developed by the CHT Group that considers the salt-dependent dye uptake behavior of all BEZAKTIV dyes under various dyeing conditions. articles.o: Wulcea introduces graphene-heated jackets for winter wear
articles.s: Flexible graphene heating elements are at the centre of a new range of electrically heated jackets being introduced by New York-based apparel brand Wulcea, aimed at reducing the need for bulky winter clothing. The company’s proprietary GrapheneNano technology offers an alternative to conventional he
articles.x: Flexible graphene heating elements are at the centre of a new range of electrically heated jackets being introduced by New York-based apparel brand Wulcea, aimed at reducing the need for bulky winter clothing. The company’s proprietary GrapheneNano technology offers an alternative to conventional heated garments, which typically use embedded electrical wires to generate warmth. These can restrict flexibility, create uneven heating and complicate garment care. Wulcea’s new range instead incorporates flexible graphene-based heating elements designed to distribute warmth across targeted areas of the body without compromising freedom of movement. The technology uses far-infrared heating, with three adjustable temperature settings allowing wearers to control the level of warmth according to conditions and activity. The jackets can begin generating heat within three seconds and provide up to ten hours of continuous heating on the lowest setting, using an 18,400mAh rechargeable battery pack. The heating system operates at 12V and incorporates intelligent thermal control, automatically interrupting heating if internal temperatures exceed 55°C. The new collection includes hardshell jackets for outdoor work and winter sports, softshell garments for everyday use and heated vests that can be worn beneath other outerwear. The men’s hardshell jacket incorporates six heating zones positioned around the neck, upper back, lower waist and front pockets. A women’s ski jacket also features six zones, with heating extended to the upper arms as well as the neck, back and pockets.
