articles.o: Primark signs long-term deal for Circ recycled polyester
articles.s: Primark has signed a multi-year offtake agreement with US textile recycler Circ for recycled polyester produced from textile waste, with the material expected to enter the retailer’s clothing ranges from 2029. The agreement is Primark’s first long-term offtake commitment with a textile-to-textile re
articles.x: Primark has signed a multi-year offtake agreement with US textile recycler Circ for recycled polyester produced from textile waste, with the material expected to enter the retailer’s clothing ranges from 2029. The agreement is Primark’s first long-term offtake commitment with a textile-to-textile recycler and is intended to support Circ as it moves its polycotton recycling technology to industrial scale. Circ, headquartered in Danville, Virginia, is currently developing its first industrial-scale recycling facility in France. The plant will process textile feedstock sourced internationally, including post-consumer and post-industrial waste from Europe, and will supply the recycled polyester covered by the Primark agreement. The volumes involved and financial terms of the agreement have not been disclosed. Circ’s patented process addresses one of the persistent problems in textile recycling – separating the polyester and cellulosic components of blended polycotton fabrics so that both can be recovered as raw materials for new textiles. The company produces two main outputs, Circ Polyester and Circ Lyocell, and has already worked with fashion brands on applications for the materials. The Primark agreement, however, represents a longer-term commitment to future commercial volumes as Circ builds up its production capacity. Peter Majeranowski, CEO of Circ, said long-term commitments from major fashion retailers would be important in moving textile-to-textile recycling from demonstration and early commercial projects towards large-scale production. For Primark, the agreement forms part of efforts to increase its use of recycled fibres and reduce its dependence on virgin polyester. Known as Plant Armor, the textile is draped over strawberry plants to create a physical barrier against insects. Its three-dimensional porous structure prevents pests from reaching the plants while allowing sunlight, rain and airflow to pass through. Field trials found that strawberry plants protected by Plant Armor produced up to 3.56 times more harvestable fruit than uncovered plants. Researchers also found no negative impact on relative humidity, light availability or vegetative plant biomass. The results are significant because researchers had initially expected the apparently opaque textile to reduce the amount of light reaching the plants, potentially encouraging leaf and stem growth at the expense of fruit production. “We expected that Plant Armor’s seemingly opaque fabric would lead to an increase in vegetative biomass at the expense of fruiting,” said Gabriel Olawuyi, graduate research assistant at NC State and lead author of the research paper. “However, we found the fabric did not impede access to light at all, and fruit production increased significantly.” Strawberries grown with and without the Plant Armor textile cover. The new technology raised berry yields by as much as 3.56 times in tunnel field tests. © Gabriel Olawuyi The knitted cover also provided a consistent warming effect during the strawberry growing seasons. articles.s: Fulgar, The Lycra Company and CSP International Fashion Group have joined forces to launch an Oroblù tights collection made entirely with bio-derived yarns. The new Bio-Derived Sneakers Tights capsule combines Fulgar’s Q-GEO bio-based polyamide with Renewable Lycra EcoMade fibre, The Lycra Company’s
articles.x: Fulgar, The Lycra Company and CSP International Fashion Group have joined forces to launch an Oroblù tights collection made entirely with bio-derived yarns. The new Bio-Derived Sneakers Tights capsule combines Fulgar’s Q-GEO bio-based polyamide with Renewable Lycra EcoMade fibre, The Lycra Company’s bio-based elastane. The collaboration brings together technologies from different stages of the textile supply chain to create hosiery in which both principal yarn components incorporate renewable-source raw materials. According to the companies, the project marks the first time an Oroblù tights style has used bio-derived yarns for both its polyamide and elastomeric components. At the heart of the development is Fulgar’s Q-GEO polyamide, in which almost half of the raw material is bio-based. The renewable component is derived from industrial corn grown on land not intended for rice, wheat or other traditional food crops. Fulgar says 40% of the corn kernel is used to produce the bio-based component, while the remaining material is allocated to other applications, including food and animal feed production. Developed as part of Fulgar’s research into next-generation fibres, Q-GEO is designed to combine renewable-source content with the performance required for demanding textile applications. The company says the yarn provides softness, breathability and moisture management, including 50% higher moisture absorption than standard polyamide. It also retains the strength and durability associated with polyamide and offers fast drying and flame-retardant properties without the addition of additives. “Our collaboration with CSP and The Lycra Company is a concrete example of how material innovation can translate into real-world, high-value applications,” said Daniela Antunes, Marketin

articles.s: Uzbekistan is expanding knitted fabric production as its textile industry moves toward higher-value products and deeper domestic processing. Figure: Uzbekistan’s government has set a $4 billion texti...
articles.x: Uzbekistan is expanding knitted fabric production as its textile industry moves toward higher-value products and deeper domestic processing. Figure: Uzbekistan’s government has set a $4 billion textile export target for 2026, including $700 million through e-commerce platforms. Courtesy: Collected Large textile enterprises produced 70,100 tons of knitted fabric in 2025, up 32.5% from the previous year. The strategy focuses on processing more cotton into yarn, fabric, knitted products, and finished garments instead of relying mainly on raw cotton exports. Uzbekistan’s broader textile industry recorded strong growth in 2025. Textile exports reached $2.6 billion, with products shipped to 75 countries. The number of textile-exporting companies increased to 1,409, including 502 new exporters. Exports of finished textile products rose 18.5% from 2024. The growth continued in 2026. During January–June, large enterprises produced UZS 54.4 trillion (~$4.27 billion) worth of textile products, marking 10.1% growth year-on-year. Textile exports reached $1.6 billion, up 24.1%. Finished textile products accounted for 53% of exports, while yarn represented 31% and knitted fabrics 9%. The government has set a $4 billion textile export target for 2026, including $700 million through e-commerce platforms. It also plans to expand capacity for 397 million square meters of fabrics, 224 million garments and knitwear products, and 108 million square meters of dyed textiles. This expansion indicates a continued shift toward higher-value textile manufacturing, with knitted fabric becoming an important part of Uzbekistan’s export-oriented supply chain.

Gopalakrishnan Advanced finishing, coating and dyeing technologies are enabling Indian textile manufacturers to move beyond volume-driven production towards higher-value, specialised and more sustainable fabrics, says Daniel Rütten, Area Sales Manager – Asia, Monforts. India’s textile industry is entering a phase in which competitiveness will increasingly depend not only on manufacturing scale, but on the ability to produce differentiated, functional and higher-value fabrics with greater efficiency and consistency. For Monforts, one of Germany’s established names in textile finishing technology, this evolution is creating significant opportunities in India, particularly across advanced finishing, coating, dyeing and drying. Daniel Rütten, Area Sales Manager – Asia, Monforts With more than six decades of presence in India, Monforts continues to see the country as one of its most important markets. The company is witnessing continued investment in conventional woven and knitted apparel and home-textile applications, while demand is expanding into technical textiles, activewear, sportswear, filtration and automotive fabrics. At the same time, manufacturers are placing greater emphasis on energy, water and chemical consumption, automation and consistent quality. According to Daniel Rütten, Area Sales Manager – Asia, Monforts , this changing investment landscape is shifting the emphasis from productivity alone towards a broader equation combining productivity, lower operating costs, flexibility and the capability to manufacture increasingly sophisticated products. articles.o: Carbios turns complex textile waste into recycled polyester T-shirts
articles.s: Carbios has demonstrated a complete European fiber-to-fiber production chain that converts complex textile and plastic waste into finished polyester T-shirts. This marks a step from laboratory recycli...
articles.x: Carbios has demonstrated a complete European fiber-to-fiber production chain that converts complex textile and plastic waste into finished polyester T-shirts. This marks a step from laboratory recycling toward industrial textile applications. The French biotechnology company worked with Patagonia, PUMA and Salomon through its Fiber-to-Fiber Consortium to process difficult waste streams containing polyester blends such as cotton and elastane, as well as dyes, finishes and silicones. These materials are among the more challenging textile waste streams for conventional recycling. The latest demonstration builds on significant process data generated at Carbios’ Clermont-Ferrand facility. In July 2026, the company reported more than 95% conversion within 24 hours when processing complex post-consumer textile waste. It had also completed its 100th production batch, demonstrating what it described as robust and reproducible performance under conditions representative of industrial operations. For the latest garment demonstration, Carbios converted complex waste into high-purity monomers. Selenis in Portugal then repolymerized them into more than 1 ton of recycled PET, branded EnzyTex. The material was spun into yarn by ANTEX in Spain, knitted into Interlock fabric by Henitex in France, dyed by TAD, and finally made into T-shirts by ToptexCube of Chamatex Group. Carbios is now moving from technology validation toward commercial deployment. The company has expanded its licensing offering to the textile market, while its planned Longlaville industrial facility in France targets production startup in the first half of 2028, subject to project financing and finalization.

articles.t: 쉬인, 상장 후 첫 성적표 어쩌나…매출 1% 늘 때 이익은 반토막
articles.o: 쉬인, 상장 후 첫 성적표 어쩌나…매출 1% 늘 때 이익은 반토막
articles.s: 쉬인이 홍콩 증시 상장 후 처음 공개한 실적에서 성장 둔화와 수익성 악화라는 과제를 동시에 드러냈다. 주문량과 고객 기반은 계속 확대됐지만 상반기 매출 증가율은 1%에 그쳤고 영업이익과 조정 순이익은 절반 이상 감소했다. 특히 미국에 이어 유럽까지 저가 직구에 대한 관세 장벽을 높이면서 중국 등 생산지에서 소비자에게 상품을 직접 보내는 쉬인의 기존 사업모델이 비용 압박을 받고 있다. 이에 쉬인은 유럽 현지 재고 확대와 물류 자동화, 고가 브랜드 육성을 통해 ‘초저가·초고속 성장’에서 수익성 중심으로 사업구조를 전환하는 전략을 본격화

articles.t: [유통]아트몰링 추석 매출 터졌다
articles.o: [유통]아트몰링 추석 매출 터졌다
articles.s: 서부산 대표 복합쇼핑몰 '아트몰링'이 10주년 기념 리뉴얼 효과를 제대로 누리고 있다.패션그룹형지는 지난 추석 황금연휴 기간 동안 아트몰링의 매출 목표를 150% 늘어난 실적을 기록했다고 알렸다.아트몰링은 이번 추석 연휴 기간(지난 9월 24일부터 27일까지 나흘간) 동안 당초 수립했던 매출 목표 대비 약 150%를 달성, 지난해 추석 연휴 실적과 비교해서도 약 50% 신장한 것으로 나타났다고 밝혔다.개점 10주년을 맞아 추진한 공간 및 MD(상품기획) 리뉴얼과 신규 대형 테넌트 유치가 명절 특수와 맞물리면서 고객 유입과 매출 증가

articles.t: TBH글로벌, 175년 역사 英 명품 ‘아쿠아스큐텀’ 성장
articles.o: TBH글로벌, 175년 역사 英 명품 ‘아쿠아스큐텀’ 성장
articles.s: TBH글로벌이 라이선스를 보유한 175년 역사의 영국계 글로벌 브랜드 ‘아쿠아스큐텀(Aquascutum)’이 국내 시장에서 본격적인 성장을 위한 성과가 가시화되고 있다. K-패션 전문기업 TBH글로벌은 올해 8월 말 기준 아쿠아스큐텀의 누적 매출이 전년 동기 대비 11% 증가했다고 30일 밝혔다.아쿠아스큐텀은 버버리(Burberry)와 함께 1850년대 출범한 영국의 대표적인 클래식 패션 브랜드다. 영국의 클래식 헤리티지와 프리미엄 이미지를 동시에 갖추고 있으며, 대표 상품인 트렌치코트를 비롯해 니트, 재킷 등 시즌별 다양한 주력

articles.o: 링탭 “좋은 성분보다 계속할 수 있는 방식…패치형 웰니스 넓힌다”
articles.s: 피부의 결점을 가리던 패치가 자기관리의 수단으로 영역을 넓히고 있다. 여드름 패치에서 출발한 시장은 최근 글루타치온과 수분, 수면, 에너지 등 뷰티·웰니스 영역으로 확장되는 모습이다. 단순히 성분을 담는 것을 넘어 피부에 붙여 사용하는 방식 자체를 제품 경쟁력으로 내세우는 브랜드도 늘고 있다.뉴셀렉트의 패치형 웰니스 브랜드 링탭은 이러한 변화의 배경으로 ‘지속 가능한 자기관리’와 ‘보여주는 관리 문화’를 꼽았다.링탭 관계자는 “소비자들은 아무리 좋은 성분이라도 매일 챙기지 못하면 의미가 없다는 것을 경험을 통해 알고 있다”며 “효과

articles.t: 풀리, 중국 도우인 라이브커머스 확대…6월 매출 전월 대비 약 15배
articles.o: 풀리, 중국 도우인 라이브커머스 확대…6월 매출 전월 대비 약 15배
articles.s: 어댑트가 운영하는 스킨케어 브랜드 풀리(FULLY)는 중국 도우인을 중심으로 라이브커머스 판매를 확대하고 있다.풀리는 지난 6월부터 중국 뷰티 인플루언서 ‘따따(搭搭)’와 도우인 라이브 방송을 진행했다. 회사 측에 따르면 협업이 진행된 6월 도우인 매출은 전월 대비 약 15배 증가했다.6월 진행한 방송에서는 ‘레드 토마토 잼 팩 클렌저’ 준비 물량이 방송 시작 약 1시간 만에 소진됐다. 회사 측 집계 기준 해당 방송의 누적 시청자 수는 약 102만명이다. 레드 토마토 잼 팩 클렌저는 워시오프 팩과 클렌저 두 가지 방식으로 사용할 수

articles.s: Long John Group has become the first customer to put Karl Mayer’s new RDJ 7/3 Jacquard Double Needle Bar Raschel Machine into operation, strengthening its capabilities in the development and production of performance footwear fabrics. The machine was officially launched at Long John’s manufacturing
articles.x: Long John Group has become the first customer to put Karl Mayer’s new RDJ 7/3 Jacquard Double Needle Bar Raschel Machine into operation, strengthening its capabilities in the development and production of performance footwear fabrics. The machine was officially launched at Long John’s manufacturing plant in Indonesia on 20 August, with representatives from leading global athletic footwear brands and Karl Mayer management attending the event. The RDJ 7/3 features three wireless Jacquard bars and has been developed to offer increased flexibility in the production of sophisticated footwear textiles. The technology enables manufacturers to create complex patterns, precisely positioned functional zones, three-dimensional structures and distinctive design effects. Long John Group is one of Taiwan’s leading suppliers of footwear fabrics and an established manufacturer serving the international athletic footwear industry. Founded by Jeff Wen in 1983, the company now operates facilities in Taiwan, China, Vietnam and Indonesia, together with a sales office in the United States. Karl Josef Mayer, grandson of the founder of Karl Mayer, in conversation with Kevin Wen (back left), son of the founder and Chairman of Long John, Jeff Wen, about the latest textile innovations. © Karl Mayer Its vertically integrated manufacturing operations encompass spinning, weaving, knitting, warp knitting, dyeing and finishing. According to Karl Mayer, Long John has already produced fabrics for more than 313 million pairs of shoes using Jacquard double needle bar raschel technology. Warp knitting plays an important role in the group’s product development activities. articles.o: Fibroline technology fully operational at Howa
articles.s: Fibroline’s dry powder impregnation technology is now fully operational in automotive headliner production at Howa Europe, marking the latest step in the industrialisation of the solvent-free manufacturing process. The project has been implemented with support from engineering companies Ingecal and
articles.x: Fibroline’s dry powder impregnation technology is now fully operational in automotive headliner production at Howa Europe, marking the latest step in the industrialisation of the solvent-free manufacturing process. The project has been implemented with support from engineering companies Ingecal and Reliant. Fibroline’s patented technology uses high-intensity alternating electric fields to distribute and impregnate dry powders throughout porous materials. For automotive headliners, it provides an alternative to conventional liquid impregnation and eliminates the use of solvents during this stage of production. It also removes the liquid effluent associated with wet impregnation and the subsequent drying stage, potentially reducing both energy consumption and the production footprint. Fibroline and Howa have been working together on the application for several years, with the technology developed specifically for the production requirements of automotive interior components. Headliners are typically multi-layer structures combining reinforcement, core and surface materials and must meet demanding requirements for weight, mechanical properties, acoustics and appearance. Fibroline’s technology can distribute functional powders through such porous structures and impregnate several layers in a single operation. The process also offers scope for incorporating powders providing specific acoustic, thermal or structural properties and for developing mono-material constructions designed to simplify end-of-life recycling. articles.o: Primark expands textile-to-textile recycling partnership with Circ
articles.s: Primark has signed a long-term purchase agreement with recycling technology company Circ to increase its use of recycled polyester made from textile waste. Figure: Primark expands textile-to-textile...
articles.x: Primark has signed a long-term purchase agreement with recycling technology company Circ to increase its use of recycled polyester made from textile waste. Figure: Primark expands textile-to-textile recycling partnership with Circ. The deal could help move textile-to-textile recycling from technology development toward larger-scale commercial use. Circ’s technology can separate polyester and cellulose fibers from blended textile waste, addressing one of the industry's biggest recycling challenges. “This partnership with Primark represents exactly the kind of long-term commercial commitment needed to move textile-to-textile recycling from innovation to industry standard,” said Peter Majeranowski, CEO of Circ . “When a global fashion retailer commits to integrating recycled materials into future collections, it sends a powerful signal across the industry: the demand is here, the materials are ready, and the opportunity to scale circular material supply chains is real.” Lynne Walker, Director of Primark Cares, said, "We launched Primark Cares with a focus on improving the quality and longevity of our clothing, and in the process show that clothes made to last longer don't have to come at a higher price. Since then, we've delivered tangible progress, including increasing the use of recycled fibres, introducing products designed to be recycled and enhancing traceability across our supply chain. This partnership is an important milestone in accelerating our ambitions to further embed circularity in our business and help scale innovative textile-to-textile recycling solutions that could play a transformational role in the future of fashion." The Apparel Recovery Coalition (ARC), launched in Accra, Ghana, will spend the next two
articles.x: ACCRA – Adidas, H&M Group, Inditex and Bestseller have joined a new coalition to test how fashion brands could help fund the management of used clothing in countries that receive large volumes of textile exports. The Apparel Recovery Coalition (ARC), launched in Accra, Ghana, will spend the next two years developing and testing a model for producer responsibility that reflects where clothes end up after use. Its first project will focus on strengthening Ghana’s existing systems for reuse, repair, upcycling, recycling and waste management. articles.o: Automation handles World Cup surge for CSF
articles.s: Manchester, UK-based retailer Classic Football Shirts (CFS) automated almost two-thirds of its order packing during this summer’s FIFA World Cup, helping it handle the busiest trading period in its 20-year history. Orders dispatched during June and July increased by 101% compared with the same perio
articles.x: Manchester, UK-based retailer Classic Football Shirts (CFS) automated almost two-thirds of its order packing during this summer’s FIFA World Cup, helping it handle the busiest trading period in its 20-year history. Orders dispatched during June and July increased by 101% compared with the same period in 2025, surpassing the retailer’s previous peaks during Black Friday and Christmas. Ahead of the tournament, CFS worked with fellow Manchester shipping software specialist Shipster to integrate a Logopak/Adpak Ecommerce Auto Bagger into its fulfilment operation. The system automates packing and shipping label application, with Shipster supplying the shipment and label data to the Logopak equipment. For orders suitable for automated handling, the company says packing times have been reduced from minutes to seconds. During the World Cup, the machine automatically packed 64% of all CFS orders. The installation builds on a five-year partnership between CFS and Shipster which has seen the retailer more than triple warehouse productivity as its international business has expanded. Founded by Matt Dale and Douglas Bierton in 2006, CFS has grown from a student-house start-up into a business with annual revenues of more than £30 million, serving customers in more than 130 countries. It holds an inventory of more than one million authenticated football shirts and memorabilia items. The CSF Manchester team. © CSF World Cup demand was particularly strong for the company’s Away Days Mystery Box range, with 23,830 Mystery Box products ordered between May and August, including almost 10,000 England versions. articles.o: LAWER S.p.A. signs definitive agreement with Graco Inc.
articles.s: LAWER S.p.A. announces that it has signed a definitive agreement for the sale of 100% of its shares to Graco Inc., a US industrial group listed on the New York… The post LAWER S.p.A. signs definitive agreement with Graco Inc. appeared first on The Textile Magazine .
articles.x: LAWER S.p.A. announces that it has signed a definitive agreement for the sale of 100% of its shares to Graco Inc., a US industrial group listed on the New York Stock Exchange. The transaction is a strategic choice designed to ensure continuity in LAWER’s journey, strengthen its international presence and create the conditions for a new phase of sustainable development, for the benefit of the company, its people and the community in which it was born and has grown. Founded and developed in Italy, LAWER is today a global benchmark in the design and manufacture of automatic dosing systems for a range of industrial sectors, including textiles, rubber, tyres, cosmetics, plastics and food. From its headquarters in Cossato, in the province of Biella, the company serves customers worldwide with solutions for high value-added processes in which precision, traceability and micro-dosing automation are essential requirements. Graco Inc., founded in 1926 and headquartered in Minneapolis, Minnesota, is a global industrial group listed on the New York Stock Exchange since 1969. The company designs, manufactures and markets technologies and equipment to move, measure, control, dispense and spray fluids, coatings and powder materials. With approximately 4,000 employees, operations in 12 countries and products sold in more than 100 countries, Graco Inc. serves thousands of customers in the manufacturing, processing, construction and maintenance industries. articles.o: Shima Seiki brings DPC to Bengaluru
articles.s: Shima Seiki will showcase its latest digital textile solutions at Apparel Sourcing Week 2026 in Bengaluru, India, from 7-8 October. The Japanese flat knitting technology specialist will focus on efficient and sustainable product development workflows enabled by Digital Product Creation (DPC), as man
articles.x: Shima Seiki will showcase its latest digital textile solutions at Apparel Sourcing Week 2026 in Bengaluru, India, from 7-8 October. The Japanese flat knitting technology specialist will focus on efficient and sustainable product development workflows enabled by Digital Product Creation (DPC), as manufacturers and brands seek to reduce development times, physical sampling and material waste. At the centre of Shima Seiki’s presentation will be its APEXFiz Design subscription-based software, which supports fashion product development from planning and design through to realistic textile simulation and 3D virtual sampling. Using scanned data from actual yarns, APEXFiz can create highly realistic digital representations of knitted products that can be used as 3D prototypes. Shima Seiki says this enables companies to replace or reduce physical samples, helping to save time, cost and materials during product development. Once a knitted design is approved for production, automatically generated knitting data can be converted into machine data for manufacture, providing a digital workflow from initial development through to finished product. The software is not limited to flat knitting. APEXFiz can also simulate woven and circular knitted fabrics, as well as printing and embroidery, and can be used alongside other 3D design software. According to Shima Seiki, this approach can increase automation and reduce labour requirements across product development, prototyping and production, while supporting the wider digitalisation and sustainability of textile and apparel supply chains. Apparel Sourcing Week brings together manufacturers, brands, suppliers and technology providers from across the apparel value chain. articles.o: Further brands opt for Nuyarn’s Strong Wool
articles.s: Nuyarn, based in Levin, New Zealand, is expanding the commercial reach of its wool spinning technology in performance socks, adding Falke, Courier, Radio and Kathmandu to its brand partners. The four companies join existing partners Kuiu and Trew in using Nuyarn Merino and Strong Wool technologies f
articles.x: Nuyarn, based in Levin, New Zealand, is expanding the commercial reach of its wool spinning technology in performance socks, adding Falke, Courier, Radio and Kathmandu to its brand partners. The four companies join existing partners Kuiu and Trew in using Nuyarn Merino and Strong Wool technologies for socks designed to combine durability, moisture management and reduced weight. Nuyarn’s approach differs from conventional ring spinning, which twists wool fibres together to form the yarn. Its technology instead drafts merino wool around a performance filament, creating a structure intended to retain more of the fibre’s natural loft. The company claims yarns produced using the technology dry five times faster than conventional merino and provide 35% greater loft and aeration. It also reports abrasion resistance of up to 8.8 times that of conventional merino, although these figures are based on Nuyarn’s own comparative testing. The company’s Strong Wool technology is designed to use coarser wool more commonly associated with interior textile applications than next-to-skin apparel. Nuyarn says the process enables the fibre to be incorporated into lightweight yarns capable of withstanding high levels of abrasion, opening another potential outlet for wool grades facing limited demand from the apparel sector. “The objective was never just to improve wool but to unlock the performance potential already present within the fibre,” says Nuyarn CEO Andy Wynne. “We are bringing a level of durability and thermoregulation to the sock market that simply hasn’t been possible with traditional yarn structures.” The merino used in the products is Responsible Wool Standard certified, while the technology is also Oeko-Tex Standard 100 accredited. www.nuyarn.com The post Further brands opt for

articles.o: Putting a number on how textiles feel
articles.s: German testing technology specialist emtec will demonstrate how subjective assessments of textile handle can be converted into measurable and digitally transferable data at TITAS 2026 in Taipei from October 6-8th. Working with its Taiwanese representative GOIN International, the company will demonst
articles.x: German testing technology specialist emtec will demonstrate how subjective assessments of textile handle can be converted into measurable and digitally transferable data at TITAS 2026 in Taipei from October 6-8 th . Working with its Taiwanese representative GOIN International, the company will demonstrate its TSA – tactile sensation analyzer – measuring properties including softness, smoothness, flexibility, stretch and recovery, thermal haptics and insulation. Hand feel and wearing comfort can be decisive in determining whether a fabric is suitable for an application, but assessments have traditionally relied heavily on people touching samples and describing what they experience. Terms such as ‘soft’, ‘smooth’ or ‘comfortable’ are inherently subjective, and perceptions can vary between individuals. The problem becomes greater when fabrics are being developed by teams working across different companies and countries. The TSA is designed to put numerical values against these characteristics, allowing samples to be compared on a reproducible basis. Measurements can also be combined to calculate a specific ‘hand feel’ value. The latest system can be equipped with different modules, including a camera for capturing a high-resolution image of the sample alongside its measured properties. The resulting information can also be connected under licence to emtec’s cloud-based Virtual Haptic Library. This enables measurements and sample images to be stored and compared remotely, potentially allowing a mill in one country, a sourcing operation in another and a brand development team elsewhere to work from the same data rather than exchanging physical samples simply to assess handle. articles.o: Good Earth Cotton puts proof behind environmental claims
articles.s: From September 27th, new measures implementing the European Union’s Empowering Consumers for the Green Transition Directive (known as EmpCo) began to apply across EU Member States. The rules raise the evidentiary threshold for environmental claims, including restricting generic environmental claims
articles.x: From September 27th, new measures implementing the European Union’s Empowering Consumers for the Green Transition Directive (known as EmpCo) began to apply across EU Member States. The rules raise the evidentiary threshold for environmental claims, including restricting generic environmental claims that cannot demonstrate recognised environmental performance. For Australian regenerative cotton programme and traceable fibre brand Good Earth Cotton (GEC), this regulatory shift reflects the direction of its evidence-led model – moving beyond practice-based assumptions and broad environmental claims towards measured outcomes, primary farm-level data, independent verification and fibre that is physically verified at source. European Commission analysis has found that 53% of green claims examined in the EU market provide vague, misleading or unfounded information, 40% have no supporting evidence, and half of green labels offer weak or non-existent verification. The significance of EmpCo extends beyond its individual prohibitions. It reflects a broader shift from environmental claims toward substantiation – placing greater emphasis on what can be proved before a claim is made. Cotton accounted for approximately 19% of global fibre production in 2024, representing around 24.5 million tons, while recycled cotton accounted for approximately 1% of global cotton production, at around 300,000 tons. The environmental evidence associated with cotton already in production therefore matters alongside continued innovation in recycled and next-generation materials. articles.o: Automation moves into spinning plant maintenance
articles.s: Barmag is extending automation beyond the production process itself with three retrofit systems designed to take repetitive and potentially hazardous maintenance work out of the hands of operators at manmade fibre spinning plants. The new solutions automate spinneret cleaning and knife sharpening, w
articles.x: Barmag is extending automation beyond the production process itself with three retrofit systems designed to take repetitive and potentially hazardous maintenance work out of the hands of operators at manmade fibre spinning plants. The new solutions automate spinneret cleaning and knife sharpening, while a motor-assisted system tackles the handling of heavy, hot spinpacks. All three can be retrofitted to existing production equipment without major modifications. For spinning plant operators, Barmag says the benefits can extend beyond reducing manual intervention. Experience with its automatic knife sharpening technology has recorded increases of up to 12% in the full-bobbin rate and up to 28% in take-up efficiency, along with increases of up to 51% in spinneret service life. Cleaning cycles have meanwhile been reduced by as much as 53%. The machine automatically sharpens the knives used in spinneret cleaning, replacing a manual process in which variations in grinding can subsequently affect cleaning quality. Standardising the operation is intended to reduce those variations while extending the working life of the components. Barmag is taking the automation a stage further with a wiping robot that carries out spinneret cleaning automatically in both filament and staple fibre spinning. Its rotating scraper blades are resharpened automatically when the robot returns to its parking station, maintaining consistent cleaning performance without operator intervention. Barmag says the system can also reduce the consumption of silicone oil and the exposure of operators to oil-containing aerosols around the spinning line. The deal is Primark’s first multi-year offtake agreement with a textile-to-textile recycler. It is intended to help the retai
articles.x: DUBLIN – Primark has signed a long-term purchase agreement with US textile recycler Circ, with clothing containing its recycled polyester expected to reach customers in 2029. The deal is Primark’s first multi-year offtake agreement with a textile-to-textile recycler. It is intended to help the retailer reduce its reliance on virgin polyester while supporting Circ’s expansion into industrial production. articles.t: Modern Syntex, 폴리에스터 칩 생산 확대를 위해 5천만 달러 ADB 대출 확보
articles.o: Modern Syntex secures $50mn ADB loan to expand polyester chips production
articles.s: The Asian Development Bank (ADB) and Modern Syntex Limited (MSL) have signed a $50 million loan agreement to expand energy-efficient polyester chips production in Bangladesh. The agreement for the Mod...
articles.x: The Asian Development Bank (ADB) and Modern Syntex Limited (MSL) have signed a $50 million loan agreement to expand energy-efficient polyester chips production in Bangladesh. The agreement for the Modern Energy-Efficient Polyester Chips Manufacturing Project was signed on 29 September, according to an ADB press release. The financing will support MSL’s expansion of its polyester chips production capacity from 107 tons to 407 tons per day. Part of the financing will also be used to refinance the company’s short-term local working capital loans. The expanded facility will produce high-intrinsic-viscosity polyester chips, which are used in higher-value textile and apparel products. The increased production is expected to strengthen domestic availability of synthetic inputs and reduce Bangladesh’s reliance on imports. “Bangladesh’s textile and ready-made garment industry is a key driver of the economy, but it continues to rely heavily on imported synthetic inputs,” said Qingfeng Zhang, ADB Country Director for Bangladesh. Notably, the financing would help MSL increase domestic production , strengthen local supply chains and support higher-value textile manufacturing. The project will introduce energy-efficient machinery and technologies expected to save around 4,840 megawatt-hours of electricity annually and reduce approximately 2,222 tons of carbon dioxide equivalent emissions each year. As part of the project, Modern Syntex will also pursue Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design (LEED) Platinum certification for its building and factory, further supporting the facility’s environmental performance. articles.t: TEXCELLENCE 3.0은 Southeast University의 섬유 재능과 창의성을 기념합니다.
articles.o: TEXCELLENCE 3.0 celebrates textile talent and creativity at Southeast University
articles.s: The Southeast Textile Club of Southeast University organized TEXCELLENCE 3.0, a day-long celebration of textile talent, creativity, craftsmanship, and innovation, at the university’s Multipurpose Hal...
articles.x: The Southeast Textile Club of Southeast University organized TEXCELLENCE 3.0, a day-long celebration of textile talent, creativity, craftsmanship, and innovation, at the university’s Multipurpose Hall on Sunday. The program began with a recitation from the Holy Quran, followed by a welcome address by Prof. Engr. Mashud Ahmed, Chairman, Department of Textile Engineering, Southeast University. Distinguished representatives from academia and industry attended the event. A.S.M. Hafizur Rahman (Nixon), Executive Director of RH Corporation, attended as the Chief Guest, while Md. Al-Amin Mian, Head of Textile, Esquire Knit Composite PLC, delivered the keynote address. Prof. Dr. Abdul Kader Muhammad Masum, Dean, School of Engineering and Director, IQAC, Southeast University, attended as the Special Guest. The session was chaired by Prof. Dr. Md. Mofazzal Hossain, Pro Vice Chancellor, Southeast University. In their speeches, the guests highlighted the importance of creativity, innovation, practical industry knowledge, continuous learning, and professional development for students aspiring to build careers in the textile and fashion sectors. They also shared their professional experiences and encouraged students to develop skills beyond academic learning. The main attraction of TEXCELLENCE 3.0 was a fashion show based on the theme “Reborn in Retro: 90s.” The segment showcased the creativity of participating students through 1990s-inspired designs, styling, and presentations. The program also featured Wall Magazine and Hand Craft Display segments, where students presented their artistic skills, creative ideas, and craftsmanship through various works. articles.o: Performance Days expands knowledge programme
articles.s: Performance Days will place education and industry exchange alongside material sourcing when the functional fabrics exhibition returns to Munich on 13-14 October 2026. The show’s expanded education programme will span its established Expert Talks, a new Breakout Stage and the Sustainability Exchange
articles.x: Performance Days will place education and industry exchange alongside material sourcing when the functional fabrics exhibition returns to Munich on 13-14 October 2026. The show’s expanded education programme will span its established Expert Talks, a new Breakout Stage and the Sustainability Exchange, bringing together specialists to examine new technologies, regulatory developments and emerging trends affecting the functional textile industry. A central theme of the Expert Talks will be this season’s Focus Topic, Bio-Based Materials – From Fiber to Fabric. Discussions will examine bio-synthetic materials across the value chain, the transition from fossil-based to plant-based alternatives and the challenges involved in developing fossil-free performance textiles. Other sessions will address the future of waterproof performance beyond PFAS, the growing potential of cellulosic materials, repairability at scale and the future of European fine wool. Expert Talks For the first time, Performance Days CEO and founder Marco Weichert will participate in an Expert Talks panel. In The Road to Fossil Free Performance, he will join Dominik Fuss of The Natural Laboratory and Satish Tailor of Vollebak to discuss the sources of future material innovation and what will be required to move performance textiles away from fossil-based resources. Weichert brings more than two decades of experience in functional textiles and collaboration with textile, yarn and finishing manufacturers worldwide. Trend and design content will also feature prominently, including Forum Insights for Autumn/Winter 2028/29, Performance Colors by Nora Kühner, Bodywear Trend Intelligence and digital colour communication. The latest Performance Award winners and their products will also be presented on 13 October. © P

articles.o: Embossed polyester market to reach $2.47 billion by 2036 as tech advances
articles.s: Textured fabrics are moving beyond aesthetics as buyers look for design flexibility, durability, and verified sustainability. The global embossed polyester fabric market is expected to reach $1.74 bil...
articles.x: Textured fabrics are moving beyond aesthetics as buyers look for design flexibility, durability, and verified sustainability. The global embossed polyester fabric market is expected to reach $1.74 billion in 2026, up from $1.68 billion in 2025, and grow to $2.47 billion by 2036 at a 3.6% CAGR. The numbers show a steady market rather than a sudden boom. But the more important story is how technology and recycled materials are changing what embossed polyester can offer. Figure: The global embossed polyester fabric market is expected to reach $1.74 billion in 2026, up from $1.68 billion in 2025, and grow to $2.47 billion by 2036 at a 3.6% CAGR. Courtesy: Collected Thermal embossing remains the dominant technology, holding a 55% market share in 2026. Its cost advantage, pattern durability, and dimensional stability make it widely used in clothing, bedding, and home furnishings. Clothing accounts for 28% of market demand, supported by apparel linings, textured outerwear, and activewear. The global production map also explains where this market is heading. China is projected to record the fastest growth among the profiled countries at 4.9% CAGR through 2036, followed by India at 4.5% and Germany at 4.1%. China added 3.03 million tons per year of polyester filament capacity in 2025. Its polyester filament exports also reached 4.35 million tons in 2025, up 10.6% year over year. From January to April 2026, exports increased another 15.3% to 1.57 million tons. Sustainability is becoming another competitive layer. Recycled polyester embossed fabrics with Global Recycled Standard certification are gaining attention as brands seek traceable materials and stronger sustainability compliance. articles.o: Silver Fleece invests in seam free knitwear production
articles.s: Australian knitwear and textile manufacturer Silver Fleece is investing in advanced Shima Seiki WHOLEGARMENT technology as it builds its capabilities in seamless, digitally driven garment production at its mill in Bowden, Adelaide. The company recently welcomed Steve Georganas, Federal Member for Ad
articles.x: Australian knitwear and textile manufacturer Silver Fleece is investing in advanced Shima Seiki WHOLEGARMENT technology as it builds its capabilities in seamless, digitally driven garment production at its mill in Bowden, Adelaide. The company recently welcomed Steve Georganas, Federal Member for Adelaide, to the facility, where co-owner and creative director Melanie Flintoft demonstrated how new technology is supporting the next stage of the manufacturer’s development. Georganas was at Parliament House in Canberra in March for the launch of Australia’s first National Manufacturing Strategy for Fashion and Textiles. His visit to Silver Fleece provided an opportunity to see how investment in advanced knitting technology and skills is being applied at manufacturing level. Central to the company’s strategy are Shima Seiki computerised WHOLEGARMENT flat knitting machines. The technology enables garments to be knitted three-dimensionally and to shape, reducing the cutting and material waste associated with conventional garment production. Silver Fleece is also developing the programming expertise required to operate the machines in-house. According to Flintoft, bringing design, programming and manufacturing together within the mill will allow the business to develop products from the initial concept rather than simply manufacture existing designs. The company’s team is currently being trained in the technology, with Silver Fleece viewing the development of local technical skills as an important part of its investment. The WHOLEGARMENT capability complements an existing manufacturing chain that includes circular knitting, dyeing, cutting, sewing, linking and finishing. articles.x: Globally, the textile industry has witnessed a decisive shift toward Man-Made Fibers (MMF), which today account for nearly 70% of total staple fibre consumption, compared to about 30% for cotton. Polyester Staple Fiber (PSF) alone contributes nearly 75–80% of the total MMF staple segment, highlighting its importance in modern spinning. In contrast, India continues to remain predominantly cotton-centric, with cotton still accounting for nearly 60-65% of staple fibre consumption. However, changing consumer preferences, rising demand for performance and value-added textiles, sustainability considerations, and the growing global preference for MMF based products are steadily driving India toward a more balanced fiber mix. Moving ahead, PSF is expected to play a pivotal role owing to its versatility, cost competitiveness, durability, and wide applicability across apparel, home textiles, and technical textile segments. In this evolving textile landscape, LMW Limited with decades of engineering excellence and continuous technological innovation, offers complete range of smart state-of-the-art machinery, highly versatile in processing all types of fibres and blends, including cotton, synthetic fibres, regenerated fibres, and specialty materials. Particularly in Polyester Staple Fiber processing, LMW’s integrated spinning solutions ensure optimized fiber handling, controlled drafting, enhanced yarn formation, improved productivity, and superior yarn quality consistency throughout the spinning process. articles.x: RALEIGH, N.C.— September 29, 2026 — A new textile used to cover strawberry plants more than tripled strawberry yields in tunnel field tests, without negatively impacting plant health. The technology could also significantly reduce water and pesticide usage in strawberry fields. The cover, known as Plant Armor, is a carefully designed fabric that is draped over strawberry plants. The material’s three-dimensional structure prevents insects from reaching the plants beneath. But its multiple layers allow sunlight, rain and airflow to reach the plant. Strawberries grown with and without the Plant Armor textile cover. The new technology raised berry yields by as much as 3.56 times in tunnel field tests. Photo credit: Gabriel Olawuyi Tunnel field tests found that Plant Armor increased strawberry yields by as much as 3.56 times, without negatively impacting relative humidity or light access. “To produce fruit, plants need sunlight,” said Gabriel Olawuyi, a graduate research assistant at North Carolina State University and lead author of a paper on Plant Armor. “We expected that Plant Armor’s seemingly opaque fabric would lead to an increase in vegetative biomass at the expense of fruiting — because reduced sunlight would trigger a ‘shade-avoidance’ response, making the plant divert energy toward stem and leaf growth rather than fruit production. articles.x: Prof. Ma Pibo is Dean of the School of Textile Science and Engineering at Jiangnan University, a Zhishan Post Professor and a doctoral supervisor. His research focuses on the design and performance of flexible textile structural materials. articles.o: Odour control for Ortovox trailwear
articles.s: Microban International has partnered with mountain sports specialist Ortovox to introduce odour-capture technology into the brand’s first mountain biking collection, the Sequence Series. The Sequence Trail Line uses 100% textile-to-textile recycled polyester and a closed-loop recycling concept that
articles.x: Microban International has partnered with mountain sports specialist Ortovox to introduce odour-capture technology into the brand’s first mountain biking collection, the Sequence Series. The Sequence Trail Line uses 100% textile-to-textile recycled polyester and a closed-loop recycling concept that turns used textiles into new apparel. With synthetic fibres prone to retaining sweat-related odours, Ortovox identified durable odour control as an important requirement for the range. “Because this new collection features our first synthetic T-shirts made entirely without wool, finding a reliable, high-performance odour control solution was critical,” said Christian Morgenroth, senior product manager at Ortovox. “We selected Microban because its technology integrates seamlessly into our overall product concept, allowing riders to keep their gear fresher for longer.” Microban’s Scentry Revive technology is incorporated directly into the fabric during manufacturing and is designed to capture and neutralise odour molecules before they settle into the material. Its performance is claimed to last for up to 50 domestic washes. Microban says the technology can reduce persistent sweat-related odours in synthetic garments and lessen the need for frequent washing, potentially extending garment life. © Microban International Scentry Revive has achieved Eco Passport by Oeko-Tex and bluesign certification. Microban also says the technology does not require biocidal registration. “At the core of our partnership with Ortovox is our mutual commitment to advancing innovation in mountain biking apparel,” said Shermon McMillan, president at Microban International. “We are proud to partner with Ortovox to give mountain bikers the freedom to worry less, explore more and rely on gear that lasts.”

articles.x: EFI and Agfa are to combine their industrial inkjet operations in a new company expected to generate annual sales of around €540 million. Under an agreement announced on September 28th, Agfa’s Digital Printing Solutions (DPS) business will be merged with EFI, bringing together two substantial portfolios of industrial printing equipment, inks, software and workflow technologies. An affiliate of EFI owner Siris Capital will hold 60% of the new company, with Agfa retaining 40%. Despite the difference in shareholdings, Siris and Agfa will operate as equal partners under the proposed governance structure. The transaction is expected to close by the end of 2026, subject to regulatory approvals, employee consultation and other customary conditions. The move significantly consolidates the industrial inkjet market and follows a commercial partnership established between EFI and Agfa in 2024, under which the companies began offering complementary technologies from each other’s portfolios. EFI has particular strengths in corrugated packaging, wide-format roll-to-roll and hybrid printing and textiles through its Nozomi, Vutek and Reggiani platforms. Agfa DPS adds equipment for display graphics, décor and packaging, including its Jeti Tauro, Onset Panthera and SpeedSet Orca systems. Together, the businesses expect pro forma revenues of approximately €540 million ($625 million) in 2026 and will serve thousands of customers in more than 100 countries. The combination also gives the new company a substantial presence on both sides of the Atlantic, with EFI particularly strong in North America and Agfa bringing an established European customer and service base. articles.o: Single-step dyeing advances to bedlinen
articles.s: A single-step dyeing process developed by Archroma has moved into commercial production at Portuguese home textiles manufacturer Lameirinho, with the first bedlinen collection produced using the technology now being sold worldwide. InOneGO combines coloration, fixation and softening in a single pad-
articles.x: A single-step dyeing process developed by Archroma has moved into commercial production at Portuguese home textiles manufacturer Lameirinho, with the first bedlinen collection produced using the technology now being sold worldwide. InOneGO combines coloration, fixation and softening in a single pad-dry application, eliminating a number of the separate processing and washing stages normally required to achieve washed-down and vintage effects on woven cellulosic fabrics. Archroma says assessments of the process using its Diresul RDT dyes have demonstrated reductions of up to 97% in water consumption, 65% in energy use and 75% in CO2 emissions, while cutting processing time by as much as 81%. The figures were calculated using Archroma’s One Way Impact Calculator, with InOneGO benchmarked against conventional cold pad-batch reactive dyeing followed by a pigment top-dye finish. Tests covered woven fabrics and incorporated the additional processing required to produce an easy wash-down effect. Lameirinho has now taken the technology beyond trials and sampling into commercial home textile production. It is using InOneGO to produce bedlinen in a range of shades and finishes, including indigo denim appearances, washed-down effects and vintage-style surfaces. Such effects conventionally involve several wet-processing stages, with additional water and energy consumed during successive washing operations. InOneGO is designed to create the required coloration and character during a single continuous application while retaining the necessary colour fastness. The process operates on existing stenter and thermosol lines, potentially allowing mills to introduce it without investment in dedicated processing machinery. The company plans to bring customers, suppliers and other textile industry specialists to Obertshausen in September
articles.x: Karl Mayer will mark its 90th anniversary in 2027 with a major week-long technology event at its headquarters in Obertshausen, Germany, rather than exhibiting at ITMA 2027 in Hanover. The company plans to bring customers, suppliers and other textile industry specialists to Obertshausen in September for demonstrations of new machinery and textile developments spanning warp knitting, technical textiles and warp preparation. The programme will make use of Karl Mayer’s Textile Innovation Center and Product Innovation Center, providing more than 5,000 square metres for machinery demonstrations, textile development and application work. New machine generations will be shown in live operation alongside textile applications and fabric concepts currently being developed by the company. Karl Mayer says specialists covering its different machine and technology areas will also be available throughout the week for technical discussions with customers. “Our anniversary activities are about much more than individual machines or new features,” says Karl Mayer CEO Lutz Wolf. “They are about the next major technical breakthrough developments and true textile innovations across warp knitting, technical textiles and warp preparation.” He adds that the company currently has a strong pipeline of developments across all three areas which will be presented during 2027. The decision means Karl Mayer will not exhibit at ITMA 2027, which takes place in Hanover from September 16-22. Instead, it will concentrate its activities around the anniversary programme at Obertshausen, close to Frankfurt. The approach builds on the company’s expertise in warp-knitted stretch textiles and its continuing research into advanced fibres, constructions and finishing technologies. Carvico says its technical fabrics are developed around resistance, comfort, protection, innovation and durability, with extensive internal testing supporting product development. At unspun, she will lead operations as the company moves OneWeave into commercial deployment. Previously, he held senior brand and marketing leadership positions with Hanesbrands and Kayser-Roth, gaining extensive experience in textile and apparel supply chains. He began his career serving mission-driven organizations, including the American Cancer Society and the National Multiple Sclerosis Society. Tony Fragnito, INDA’s current president and CEO, will transition to an executive consultant role in January 2027 to support the leadership transition and focus on projects and initiatives designed to expand the reach and participation of the Global Nonwovens Alliance (GNA). His planned retirement will occur in December 2027. articles.t: Nuyarn, 기능성 양말의 범위 확장
articles.o: Nuyarn expands performance sock reach
articles.s: Nuyarn is expanding its presence in the endurance and outdoor sock market, with Falke, Courier, Radio and Kathmandu joining existing partners KUIU and Trew in using its performance wool technologies. The New Zealand-based textile technology company says the growing adoption reflects increasing deman
articles.x: Nuyarn is expanding its presence in the endurance and outdoor sock market, with Falke, Courier, Radio and Kathmandu joining existing partners KUIU and Trew in using its performance wool technologies. The New Zealand-based textile technology company says the growing adoption reflects increasing demand for lightweight, durable and fast-drying natural fibre solutions for applications including running, cycling, hiking and hunting. Nuyarn has developed a twist-free spinning technology designed to preserve more of wool’s natural performance characteristics. Instead of tightly twisting fibres together using conventional ring-spinning methods, the process drafts superfine merino wool around a high-performance filament, creating what the company describes as a loftier and more resilient yarn structure. The objective was never just to improve wool; it was to unlock the performance potential already present within the fibre The company has also developed its Strong Wool technology, which is designed to transform coarser wool grades traditionally associated with interior textile applications into yarns suitable for performance apparel and accessories. According to Nuyarn, the technology enables these stronger wool fibres to deliver increased abrasion resistance while retaining the comfort, moisture management and thermal properties required for active applications. The latest sock programmes use both Nuyarn Merino and Strong Wool technologies, with products designed to deliver durability, moisture management, comfort and lightweight performance. Nuyarn says testing has shown its yarns can achieve up to 8.8 times greater abrasion resistance than conventional merino constructions, while drying up to five times faster. articles.t: Riopele의 플루오로카본 프리 패브릭 마감
articles.o: Fluorocarbon-free fabric finish from Riopele
articles.s: Portuguese textile manufacturer Riopele has developed a new fluorocarbon-free finish designed to provide durable water repellency without the long-chain PFC chemistry traditionally used for protective fabrics. The new FCF (Fluoro Carbon Free) finish is based on a modified resin formulation and provi
articles.x: Portuguese textile manufacturer Riopele has developed a new fluorocarbon-free finish designed to provide durable water repellency without the long-chain PFC chemistry traditionally used for protective fabrics. The new FCF (Fluoro Carbon Free) finish is based on a modified resin formulation and provides repellency against water and other aqueous liquids. According to Riopele, the treatment retains its effectiveness through repeated washing cycles. The development reflects the wider textile industry’s move away from fluorinated treatments as brands seek alternatives that can provide weather protection while reducing the environmental impact associated with conventional durable water-repellent finishes. Riopele says durability was a particular focus during development, both in maintaining fabric performance and potentially extending the useful life of garments. “Durability is no longer just a matter of performance but has become part of the sustainability equation,” says Ângela Teles, sustainable product and R&D project manager at Riopele. The company also says the finish can make treated garments easier to maintain and potentially reduce the frequency with which they need to be washed, while retaining their protective properties over time. www.riopele.pt The post Fluorocarbon-free fabric finish from Riopele appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .

articles.o: NITER Textile Club to host Textile Fest Bangladesh 1.0 on October 8–9
articles.s: The National Institute of Textile Engineering and Research (NITER) will host Textile Fest Bangladesh 1.0, a two-day textile-focused festival that aims to strengthen connections among students, indust...
articles.x: The National Institute of Textile Engineering and Research (NITER) will host Textile Fest Bangladesh 1.0, a two-day textile-focused festival that aims to strengthen connections among students, industry leaders, brands, and aspiring professionals in Bangladesh’s textile and apparel sector. Organized by the NITER Textile Club, the festival is scheduled for October 8 and 9, 2026, at the NITER campus. Textile Today is the media partner of the event. Positioned as a platform for textile innovation, technical learning, career development, and industry-academia collaboration, the festival will feature a range of activities designed to engage students, industry, and stakeholders. One of the key attractions of Textile Fest Bangladesh 1.0 is its total prize pool of BDT 2,50,000, which will be distributed across the festival’s competitive segments. The program is expected to attract more than 3,000 student participants and industry representatives, creating opportunities for professional networking, knowledge exchange, and talent engagement. Two-Day program featuring technical competitions, seminars, and industry engagement The first day of Textile Fest Bangladesh 1.0 will focus on technical learning, career development, and industry interaction. The proposed program includes an opening session, a job fest, seminars, a podcast, and industry-oriented discussions, alongside a series of competitions. The competition segments include Case Study, Creative Exhibition, Fashion Show, 300-Seconds Innovation Pitch, Mock Interview, Photography Competition and Textile Olympiad. articles.o: ITMF Awards highlight gains through collaboration
articles.s: The Zurich-headquartered International Textile Manufacturers Federation (ITMF) has announced the two winners of its 2026 International Collaboration Awards which recognise how collaboration can move textile innovation beyond individual companies and into commercial applications. The awards have gone
articles.x: The Zurich-headquartered International Textile Manufacturers Federation (ITMF) has announced the two winners of its 2026 International Collaboration Awards which recognise how collaboration can move textile innovation beyond individual companies and into commercial applications. The awards have gone to Swiss textile technology companies HeiQ and Archroma for their work to accelerate the global adoption of functional textile finishes, and to Austria’s Lenzing and German fashion brand Armedangels for a project that has challenged the reliance of performance outerwear on synthetic fibres. Both projects will be presented at the ITMF and IAF Conference in Fortaleza, Brazil, on October 14-15. HeiQ and Archroma’s winning project, Alone we Innovate, Together we Scale, stems from a co-marketing agreement announced by the two Swiss companies in January this year. It brings together HeiQ’s development of functional textile technologies with Archroma’s much larger global manufacturing, application and commercial network. The initial focus is on antimicrobial and odour-control technologies, with the partners offering textile mills, brands and retailers access to an expanded portfolio of functional finishes. HeiQ has built its business around developing specialist material and finishing technologies, while Archroma has more than 4,000 employees in 42 countries and over 30 production sites, along with established technical and customer networks serving textile manufacturers worldwide. As India’s premier retail technology forum, the event brought together CEOs, CIOs, technology partners, and industry leader
articles.x: The Retailers Association of India (RAI) successfully hosted the 20th edition of the Retail Technology Conclave, ReTechCon 2026, on September 23–24 at JW Marriott Mumbai Sahar. As India’s premier retail technology forum, the event brought together CEOs, CIOs, technology partners, and industry leaders to explore how intelligence, automation, and unified commerce are transforming retail, while driving smarter decision-making, seamless customer experiences, and a more connected, future-ready retail ecosystem. ReTechCon 2026 offered an immersive experience that brought together the depth of expert-led discussions with the scale and diversity of a premier industry conclave. Participants gained valuable insights into emerging technologies, evolving global trends, and innovative solutions shaping the future of retail, with a focus on driving smarter, more connected, and future-ready businesses. Speaking about ReTechCon 2026, Kumar Rajagopalan, CEO, Retailers Association of India (RAI), said, “Retail has spent 50years organising itself around five Ps — people, product, place, promotion, price. Technology has quietly added two more: pace and personalisation. AI is no longer a pilot project sitting in some retailers’ innovation labs — it is already reshaping how customers are found, how products are tracked, and how every transaction becomes a data point. ReTechCon 2026 exists to have that conversation honestly, not as a sales pitch, but as an industry working out together what comes next.” Saloni Khosla, Vice President, Pepperfry: “In a category like furniture, technology has to solve for a very specific problem — the customer can’t just add it to cart the way they would a t-shirt. articles.x: Mr. Md. Mejba Uddin Ali, Chairman of Wega Group, has been appointed Chairman of the newly constituted Board of Trustees (BoT) of BGMEA University of Fashion & Technology (BUFT). The appointment was made at the board’s inaugural meeting on September 28, where members discussed key matters relating to the university’s governance, administration and future development. The newly constituted Board of Trustees reaffirmed its commitment to strengthening BUFT’s academic and institutional capabilities and advancing the university’s continued growth and development. The meeting also underscored the importance of enhancing BUFT’s contribution to education and professional skills development in Bangladesh’s textile, apparel and fashion industries. In this context, the board discussed strategic initiatives to further align the university’s academic programs and skills development efforts with the evolving needs of the industry. The post Md. articles.s: STOCKHOLM, Sweden — September 22, 2026 — The little black dress may be one of fashion’s simplest and most enduring garments, but achieving its characteristic clean lines depends on manufacturing precision of the kind supplied by Swedish textile machinery specialist and TMAS member Svegea. Ever since
articles.x: STOCKHOLM, Sweden — September 22, 2026 — The little black dress may be one of fashion’s simplest and most enduring garments, but achieving its characteristic clean lines depends on manufacturing precision of the kind supplied by Swedish textile machinery specialist and TMAS member Svegea. Ever since Audrey Hepburn appeared in Givenchy’s celebrated creation in Breakfast at Tiffany’s, the LBD has become a wardrobe staple across generations. Its appeal lies partly in its apparent simplicity, but producing a dress that retains its shape, sits cleanly around the neckline and withstands repeated wear requires considerable attention to details that are largely invisible to the wearer. Bias binding begins with Svegea’s Tube Sewing Unit, which joins open-width fabric to create a continuous tube. One of those details is bias binding. Bias binding is produced from strips of fabric cut diagonally across the material rather than along its straight grain. Cutting on the bias gives the strip greater flexibility, allowing it to follow curved necklines, armholes and other edges without puckering or distorting the garment. It can be used to enclose raw edges, reinforce areas subjected to movement and provide a clean internal finish. While largely unnoticed by the wearer, accurately produced and applied binding can consequently make an important contribution to both the appearance and durability of a garment. For a home sewer, bias strips can be cut and prepared manually but in industrial garment production, where thousands of identical pieces may be required, the challenge is quite different. articles.t: ACG Kinna의 KA-195를 사용하여 베개 포장에 대한 제어력 강화
articles.o: More control over pillow packaging with ACG Kinna’s KA-195
articles.s: Sweden’s ACG Kinna is targeting greater automation and control in high-volume pillow packaging with its KA-195 system, combining programmable compression, bag forming and sealing at rates of up to 12 individually packed units per minute. Compression packaging is already widely employed by pillow man
articles.x: Sweden’s ACG Kinna is targeting greater automation and control in high-volume pillow packaging with its KA-195 system, combining programmable compression, bag forming and sealing at rates of up to 12 individually packed units per minute. Compression packaging is already widely employed by pillow manufacturers to reduce the considerable volume occupied by finished products during transport. The focus of the KA-195, however, is on integrating and controlling this established process within an automated production flow. The machine forms bags directly from roll material before compressing and sealing each pillow. A servo-controlled compression plate allows manufacturers to specify the final packed height according to the pillow, filling material and subsequent packaging and transport requirements. This is important because the objective is not necessarily to compress every product to its smallest possible dimensions. Different fillings have different recovery characteristics, making the ability to balance shipping volume against protection of the pillow’s loft and shape an important consideration. Pre-set recipes stored in the machine’s HMI allow operators to change between products and customer specifications while maintaining automated production. The KA-195 can also be configured for multi-packs and vacuum-secured sealing, along with leaflet insertion, sticker application and handle punching. For manufacturers producing pillows at high volumes, the system is designed to bring what can be a series of separate packaging operations into a controlled automated process, while enabling the degree of compression to be adjusted to individual products. articles.o: K-뷰티 유럽 진출 강화…‘수출’ 너머 ‘현지 유통’ 구축한다
articles.s: K-뷰티의 유럽 진출 방식이 온라인 수출과 단기 마케팅을 넘어 현지 소비자 체험, 상설 판매, 규제 대응, 기업간거래(B2B) 유통망 확보를 결합한 ‘현지 사업 인프라’ 구축 단계로 이동하고 있다. 보건복지부는 9월 25일 이탈리아 밀라노를 시작으로 28일 독일 슈투트가르트, 30일 프랑스 파리에 중소 화장품 기업을 위한 체험·판매 거점을 잇달아 가동한다. 시장 반응을 확인하는 팝업스토어, 실제 판매 실적을 만드는 플래그십스토어, 규제와 바이어 연결까지 담당하는 플래그십 허브를 국가별 시장 성숙도에 따라 달리 배치한 것이 핵심이다.

articles.o: Filo 66 delivers strong results
articles.s: The 66th edition of Filo, the International Yarns and Fibres Exhibition, has closed in Milan with organisers reporting strong visitor numbers and positive results despite challenging economic and geopolitical conditions. The two-day event showcased yarn and fibre collections combining style, innovat
articles.x: The 66th edition of Filo, the International Yarns and Fibres Exhibition, has closed in Milan with organisers reporting strong visitor numbers and positive results despite challenging economic and geopolitical conditions. The two-day event showcased yarn and fibre collections combining style, innovation and research, with a consistently high flow of buyers rewarding exhibitors presenting their latest developments for the international textile market. Filo 66 once again shared dates and exhibition space at Fiera Milano Rho with Lineapelle, the international exhibition for leathers, accessories, components, synthetics, fabrics and materials for footwear, leather goods, apparel and furnishings. The arrangement enabled the two fashion-related supply chains to present a more integrated offering to international buyers. Internationalisation remained a central focus for Filo, particularly in supporting small and medium-sized textile companies seeking greater access to overseas markets. The exhibition has continued to increase its international exhibitor base and attract foreign buyers through collaborations with ITA – the Italian Trade Agency – and the Piedmont Region. The partnership with ITA, which celebrates its centenary this year, brought a delegation of 20 buyers from France, Spain, Portugal, the Netherlands, the United Kingdom, Turkey and India to Filo 66. Filo’s collaboration with the Piedmont Region also supported the organisation of Buyers’ Days through the region’s Integrated Textile Supply Chain Project. Funded by the 2021–2027 ERDF Operational Programme and implemented through Ceipiemonte, the initiative attracted a significant contingent from the United Kingdom, identified as a market of particular interest for Italian textile companies. articles.o: Heberlein reinforces commitment to the Chinese market
articles.s: Advanced DTY jet technology and a new service hub bring performance and technical support closer to customers Heberlein, globally recognised as a leading provider of air interlacing and air texturing… The post Heberlein reinforces commitment to the Chinese market appeared first on The Textile Magazi
articles.x: Advanced DTY jet technology and a new service hub bring performance and technical support closer to customers Heberlein, globally recognised as a leading provider of air interlacing and air texturing jets for synthetic filament yarns, is consolidating its success in the Chinese market with its APh- and APe-series for DTY applications. Particularly in the field of Air Covering, Heberlein technologies combine excellent quality with significant savings in compressed-air consumption. A new service hub in Shengze City underlines the company’s long-term commitment in the Chinese market. Over the past 20 years, Heberlein has achieved considerable success in China. The Swiss brand stands for innovation, reliability and trust. Heberlein DTY jets are used both for the retrofitting of existing facilities and in new investments. Compressed-air consumption is an important KPI for mills, as compressed air is a cost-intensive resource. Heberlein’s compressed-air-saving technology therefore gives its solutions a major competitive advantage. Heberlein will present its successful APh- and APe-series at upcoming ITMA Asia + CITME 2026. Air Covering for required yarn qualities Demand for Air Covering has been high in the Chinese market. Air Covering combines elastane with a covering yarn by interlacing the two components at regular intervals using a controlled air jet. The resulting yarns offer good stretch, comfort and surface properties. They are widely used in leggings and sportswear, underwear, hosiery and socks. Other applications include stretch fabrics for trousers and jeans, elasticated cuffs, as well as medical and compression textiles. articles.t: Ravel의 성공적인 펀딩 라운드
articles.o: Successful funding round for Ravel
articles.s: Seattle-based textile-to-textile recycling technology company Ravel has closed an oversubscribed $8.2 million seed funding round to accelerate the commercial readiness of its Purification technology. The investment was led by One Small Planet, with significant participation from AP Ventures plus sup
articles.x: Seattle-based textile-to-textile recycling technology company Ravel has closed an oversubscribed $8.2 million seed funding round to accelerate the commercial readiness of its Purification technology. The investment was led by One Small Planet, with significant participation from AP Ventures plus support from Overlay Capital and Lichen Ventures. Existing investors At One Ventures, who led Ravel’s pre-seed round, along with Collateral Good and Betterway Ventures, also provided follow-on participation. The new capital will accelerate Ravel’s path to commercial readiness and work towards its mission to disrupt material recovery in the fashion industry. Purification recycling technology was intentionally designed to address the industry’s biggest unsolved challenges – valorising hard-to-recycle blends that make up the vast majority of modern clothing and avoiding disruption in existing supply chains. Ravel does this with feedstock flexibility and a market-based product offering that is ‘drop-in ready’. “There are countless advantages to blended fibre materials for clothing,” says Zahlen Titcomb, CEO of Ravel. “Blends are what make clothing durable, functional and affordable, but are not recyclable with existing infrastructure. That’s where Ravel comes in. articles.s: Premex Solutions, the Georgia-based digital textile fabrics business, has been acquired by Media One, marking the next phase of its growth in the US market. Premex was established to meet growing US demand for digitally printable textiles. It carries the product expertise, technical knowledge and te
articles.x: Premex Solutions, the Georgia-based digital textile fabrics business, has been acquired by Media One, marking the next phase of its growth in the US market. Premex was established to meet growing US demand for digitally printable textiles. It carries the product expertise, technical knowledge and textile heritage of its parent company, Premier Textiles Group, a Manchester-based, family-run business founded in 1981, serving customers across North West England and beyond. A key part of Premex’s success has been its focus on innovation, with the business bringing new fabric developments to the US market. This combination of textile expertise, technical knowledge and commitment to innovation has helped establish Premex as a strong and respected supplier in the digital textile market. Nick Smith, Director, Premier Textiles Group, said: “Premex has developed into an exciting business with real potential in the US market. This acquisition puts it in the best position to reach that potential, with an owner able to give it the focus, resource and investment it needs. “Media One is exactly that owner. We’re excited to see what the business achieves as it enters this next chapter.” Premex joins Media One’s existing portfolio alongside Fisher Textiles and Hyperflex Vinyls, bringing print-ready fabrics together with printing equipment, inks, finishing solutions and nationwide technical service under one roof. Premex customers will continue working with the same people and products, now backed by Media One’s wider capabilities.
