articles.o: Alkegen expands needlefelt capacity in Germany
articles.s: Alkegen has invested approximately €1.5 million in new needlefelt equipment at its Fulda plant in Germany, increasing production speeds while extending the weight range of technical nonwovens the site can manufacture. At the centre of the investment is a new elliptical pre-needle loom installed on a
articles.x: Alkegen has invested approximately €1.5 million in new needlefelt equipment at its Fulda plant in Germany, increasing production speeds while extending the weight range of technical nonwovens the site can manufacture. At the centre of the investment is a new elliptical pre-needle loom installed on an existing needlepunching line. Alkegen says initial production results indicate an increase in line performance of around 20%, alongside a two-to-three percentage point improvement in yield and an estimated 15% reduction in energy consumption per kilogramme of fibre processed. Significantly, the equipment also allows Fulda to produce much heavier needlefelt constructions than previously possible, with weights now reaching approximately 4,000gsm. This opens up additional applications in the steel industry and other demanding industrial markets requiring high-basis-weight technical felts. The elliptical pre-needling process provides tighter control of web elongation in both the machine and cross directions, enabling more isotropic felt structures with more consistent properties. Alkegen also reports improved process stability and reduced downtime compared with the previous hydraulic equipment, including a lower risk of contamination from hydraulic oil leakage. Fulda manufactures needlepunched nonwovens from a wide range of staple fibres, including conventional polyester and polypropylene as well as higher-performance preox, polyimide, PTFE and aramid fibres. The upgraded line can accommodate different fibre types, lengths and constructions, allowing materials to be engineered for industrial filtration, fire protection, acoustics, construction and architecture, white goods and PPE, among other applications. articles.x: With more than 20 years of experience in textile automation, a strong engineering infrastructure, and innovative technologies, ENMOS is strengthening its operations in Egypt with a new strategic step. The appointment of Nobeltex, one of the well-established and experienced companies in the Egyptian textile industry, as an ENMOS dealer brings together the complementary strengths of both companies. ENMOS’s advanced automation technologies and engineering expertise are supported by Nobeltex’s extensive market knowledge, strong customer relationships, and well-established after-sales service capabilities. Through this new structure, ENMOS’s dyehouse automation, process control,mechnical automation systems and software solutions are being offered to textile manufacturers in Egypt with a stronger local support network. Nobeltex’s long-standing industry experience and strong after-sales service capabilities provide an important advantage in ensuring the continued performance of ENMOS technologies in the field. This new chapter represents an important step in ENMOS’s growth strategy in Egypt while creating new opportunities for both companies to undertake larger and more comprehensive projects together. Giza Project Currently Under Commissioning One of the significant examples of this new cooperation is the dyehouse project being carried out for Giza , a well-known company in the Egyptian textile industry. As part of the project undertaken by ENMOS, a comprehensive dyehouse automation system is being implemented according to Giza’s specific requirements. ENMOS’s automation solutions, software infrastructure, and process control technologies are being integrated as part of a comprehensive system. Commissioning activities are currently ongoing. articles.t: Tearfil이 구조 조정에 들어가면서 Spinnova가 개입합니다.
articles.o: Spinnova steps in as Tearfil enters restructuring
articles.s: Spinnova is considering the acquisition of Portuguese yarn spinner Tearfil for €500,000 and plans to provide the financially troubled company with a €1.5 million bridge loan while its debts are restructured. The Finnish fibre technology company has signed a non-binding letter of intent to acquire al
articles.x: Spinnova is considering the acquisition of Portuguese yarn spinner Tearfil for €500,000 and plans to provide the financially troubled company with a €1.5 million bridge loan while its debts are restructured. The Finnish fibre technology company has signed a non-binding letter of intent to acquire all of Tearfil, one of its key development partners and a specialist in converting Spinnova fibre into yarn. Tearfil is currently entering a Portuguese court-supervised restructuring process after reporting a sharp deterioration in its financial performance during 2025. Turnover fell by almost 34% from €12.9 million in 2024 to €8.6 million last year, while its loss widened from €448,000 to €3.27 million. At the end of 2025, the company had short-term liabilities of €7.9 million and long-term liabilities of €5 million. Spinnova says the proposed acquisition would give it dedicated yarn development and spinning capabilities as it seeks to accelerate the commercialisation of its fibre technology. Tearfil has already played an important role in developing yarns incorporating Spinnova fibre and bringing them closer to commercial textile applications. Taking the spinner in-house would give Spinnova greater control over this stage of the supply chain and potentially shorten the time between fibre development and customer-ready yarns and fabrics. “Tearfil has been an important partner for Spinnova, playing a key role in advancing Spinnova fibre toward commercial applications,” said Spinnova CEO Janne Poranen. “Bringing these capabilities into Spinnova would strengthen our ability to support broader adoption of Spinnova fibre and advance the commercial scaling of our technology.” The proposed €500,000 purchase price would be paid through a combination of cash and Spinnova shares. The meeting focused on the development of Bangladesh’s RMG buying hou
articles.x: The Bangladesh Garment Buying House Association (BGBA), led by President Md. Abdul Hamid, along with members of the Board of Directors, paid a courtesy visit to Khandaker Abdul Muktadir, Minister of Commerce, on 21 September 2026. The meeting focused on the development of Bangladesh’s RMG buying house sector and its role in the country’s international apparel trade. The BGBA delegation highlighted the need for a strong and business-friendly environment for buying houses to support international buyer engagement, attract new export orders and expand market opportunities. The association also discussed strengthening the sector’s operational framework, improving trade facilitation, supporting new buyer and market development, and enhancing coordination between government and industry stakeholders. The meeting reflected BGBA’s continued efforts to maintain dialogue with the government and contribute to the long-term development of Bangladesh’s export-oriented buying house sector. BGBA expressed its commitment to working with the government and relevant stakeholders to strengthen international business connectivity, expand market opportunities and further enhance Bangladesh’s position in the global apparel sourcing landscape. articles.o: The true purpose of technology is to enhance human capabilities
articles.s: Engineer Md. Saiful Islam Shahin has built a distinguished career in Bangladesh’s textile and garment industry, with expertise in production management, efficiency enhancement, and transforming factor...
articles.x: Engineer Md. Saiful Islam Shahin has built a distinguished career in Bangladesh’s textile and garment industry, with expertise in production management, efficiency enhancement, and transforming factories into profitable enterprises. Starting his career as a production engineer, he gradually advanced into senior leadership roles, eventually taking responsibility for multiple factories and driving their transformation into profitable operations. He later joined New Asia Group, where he initially oversaw JM Fabrics and Knit Asia and currently serves as Group Executive Director. Under his leadership, the group has expanded across the fiber-to-fashion value chain, covering spinning, fiber, fabric, denim, knit, woven, and garments. Figure 1: Engineer Md. Saiful Islam Shahin, Group Executive Director, New Asia Group Alongside his corporate career, Saiful Islam Shahin serves as Administrator of Sirajganj District Council, where he works closely with marginalized communities. He recently spoke with Textile Today about leadership, technology, business growth, and Bangladesh’s textile industry. Textile Today: Tell us a little more about the history of the journey of New Asia Group and the scope of its current business? articles.s: Yarn Expo Autumn 2026 recently concluded in Shanghai with approximately 600 exhibitors from 14 countries and regions connecting with nearly 22,000 visitors representing 110 markets. Held from 25-27 August at the National Exhibition and Convention Center, the fair brought together fibre and yarn supp
articles.x: Yarn Expo Autumn 2026 recently concluded in Shanghai with approximately 600 exhibitors from 14 countries and regions connecting with nearly 22,000 visitors representing 110 markets. Held from 25-27 August at the National Exhibition and Convention Center, the fair brought together fibre and yarn suppliers with buyers seeking new materials, sustainable solutions and performance technologies. Running alongside Intertextile Shanghai Apparel Fabrics – Autumn Edition, CHIC and PH Value, Yarn Expo linked upstream fibre and yarn developments with fabric manufacturing, garment production and fashion-market demand. Sustainability was prominent across the exhibition, with recycled, bio-based and regenerated fibres presented alongside performance materials. Exhibitors demonstrated developments ranging from recycled PET and plant-based polyester to regenerated fibres and traceable speciality yarns. Among the international exhibitors, Indorama Ventures of Thailand presented its 100% recycled PET deja range, while Japan’s Toray Industries showcased plant-based polyester and Nanodesign technology. The UK’s Lurex Company presented traceable recycled metallic yarns. Chinese exhibitor Hangzhou Benma Chemfibre and Spinning displayed regenerated polyester produced from PET bottles and textile waste, targeting applications including fashion, activewear, home textiles and nonwovens. The returning Uzbekistan Pavilion featured eight exhibitors and highlighted the country’s vertically integrated cotton and textile industry, spanning domestic cotton cultivation through to weaving and garment manufacturing. Returning to the international fibre innovation forum as a Silver Sponsor, the company had two s
articles.x: The Lycra Company highlighted advances in textile-to-textile recycling and sweat-masking technology at the 65th Dornbirn Global Fiber Congress, which took place from 16-18 September in Dornbirn, Austria. Returning to the international fibre innovation forum as a Silver Sponsor, the company had two scientists presenting developments focused on circularity and textile performance. Alberto Ceria, technical product manager at The Lycra Company, presented the company’s textile-to-textile platform, a systemic circularity initiative designed to transform elastane from a potential barrier to recycling into a recoverable, high-value resource. The platform is based on collaboration between recyclers, textile mills, brands and technology developers and is designed to be compatible with mechanical, chemical, enzymatic and emerging recycling technologies. According to the company, the approach provides a scalable framework for advancing textile-to-textile circularity across the industry. In a second presentation, Nicholas Kurland, product development director – advanced concepts at The Lycra Company, discussed the development of Coolmax CloakFX fibre. Launched earlier this year and now commercially available, the technology is designed to minimise the appearance of sweat on fabrics while providing moisture management to help keep the wearer cool. © The Lycra Company The GRS-certified fibre is now manufactured using 100% recycled polyester. The world-class center for advancing textile innovation and fostering entrepreneurship is named in honor of the late W. Duke Kimbrell
articles.x: RALEIGH, N.C. — September 21, 2026 — The W. Duke Kimbrell Flex Factory officially opened on Sept. 11 following a ribbon-cutting ceremony to commemorate the occasion. The world-class center for advancing textile innovation and fostering entrepreneurship is named in honor of the late W. Duke Kimbrell ’49, a pioneering textile leader of the 20th century. In 1949, Kimbrell became one of the 314 students of the then School of Textiles at NC State. Within 12 years of graduating, he became the CEO of Parkdale, the largest consumer of cotton fibers and yarn manufacturers in the world. In the 1980s, Kimbrell took ownership of the company. Students, staff and faculty from the Wilson College of Textiles welcomed donors and distinguished guests to celebrate the official opening of the Flex Factory, with the state-of-the-art machinery now being fully operational. The factory offers 17,000 square feet for research and collaboration in a space formerly occupied by the Wilson College Senior Design Lab. The renovated space continues to house the Senior Design capstone program for textile engineering and textile technology students and adds a new makerspace where students can bring ideas to reality. The Flex Factory also houses a new prototype lab where industry partners and entrepreneurs can create novel textile products. According to Brownley King, a W. Duke Kimbrell Centennial Scholar and textile technology student, spaces like this that connect the academic experience to the real world make the Wilson College student experience unique. “There is truly no place quite like the Wilson College. articles.o: Mario Crosta sees strong potential in supporting Bangladesh’s transition toward premium, high-value textile finishing
articles.s: Latest innovative technology to boost the Bangladesh textile sectorBangladesh has built a world-class reputation in knitwear and denim, and the next step in that journey is finishing — the stage where a fabric gains its real character. The most valuable technology today is the one that gives produce
articles.x: Latest innovative technology to boost the Bangladesh textile sector Bangladesh has built a world-class reputation in knitwear and denim, and the next step in that journey is finishing — the stage where a fabric gains its real character. The most valuable technology today is the one that gives producers precise, repeatable control over the hand of the fabric: raising, sueding and shearing machines that can turn a simple knit into a warm performance fleece, a peach-soft touch, or a refined brushed denim. At Mario Crosta, we’ve built our POLARIS 28 around exactly this — a double-drum raising machine that delivers an even finish selvedge to selvedge, meter after meter. For a country producing large volumes for demanding global brands, this consistency is what turns good fabric into premium fabric, and lets local manufacturers move further up the value chain. Reducing production cost & saving energy In finishing, energy is one of the largest costs — which makes it one of the biggest opportunities. At Mario Crosta, we engineer our machines to do more with less. Drawing on our long experience with inverter drives, we developed our own Energy Saving System (ESS): instead of losing the energy produced by the motor, we recover it, so it’s reused rather than wasted. The result is a significant reduction in energy consumption — and a lower cost per kilo of fabric, shift after shift, for the entire life of the machine. Precision matters just as much: when a machine applies exactly the right finish the first time, producers gain consistent, first-pass quality and a better yield from every meter. articles.o: SwitchDye takes top innovation award at Dornbirn
articles.s: University of Leeds spin-off SwitchDye took the top award at the Dornbirn GFC Innovation Days 2026 for a technology that could significantly reduce the chemical and water demands of polyester dyeing while making garments easier to recycle. Professor Richard Blackburn, one of the technology’s invento
articles.x: University of Leeds spin-off SwitchDye took the top award at the Dornbirn GFC Innovation Days 2026 for a technology that could significantly reduce the chemical and water demands of polyester dyeing while making garments easier to recycle. Professor Richard Blackburn, one of the technology’s inventors and a co-founder of SwitchDye, claimed the award following the Innovation Day presentations at the 65th Dornbirn GFC in Austria on Thursday September 17th. SwitchDye was one of ten innovations selected for the dedicated Innovation Day, where Blackburn presented Polyester Infinity: CO2-switchable dyeing and decoloration for fully circular polyester . The other finalists covered developments ranging from new fibres and textile-to-textile recycling to biodegradable polymers and filtration technologies. Switching behaviour The Leeds technology addresses one of the less visible environmental problems associated with polyester. Conventional disperse dyeing relies on significant quantities of auxiliary chemicals, followed by washing and clearing stages to remove residual dye and achieve the required colour fastness. SwitchDye instead employs specially designed CO₂-responsive dyes which change their behaviour when a small amount of carbon dioxide is introduced into the dyebath, effectively using carbonised water to trigger the process. “Our technology makes it easier to dye the fibre without other auxiliaries by injecting a small amount of carbonated water into the dyebath,” Blackburn explained. “This triggers the unique switching behaviour of the dyes within the polyester fibres.” Tests carried out during the technology’s development indicate that SwitchDye can reduce chemical use by around 90% and water consumption by approximately 40%, while maintaining conventional standards o

articles.x: The latest edition of Texworld Apparel Sourcing Paris confirms the global reshaping of sourcing strategies. The offer is evolving to meet more selective buyers seeking responsiveness, innovation, and diversification in their sourcing options. The 59th edition of Texworld Apparel Sourcing Paris , which took place from 31 August to 2 September at the Paris-Le Bourget Exhibition Center, ended in a still-tense market environment. Compared with previous editions, attendance at the show was affected by an early calendar and an uncertain political and economic environment. An offer that adapts to the context Nevertheless, these three days confirmed the platform’s ability to generate business contacts and highlight new sourcing opportunities. With 1,054 exhibitors, including 146 first-time exhibitors, the offering continues to evolve, reflecting a market that now favors partner quality, flexibility, and sourcing choice. The major production hubs – China, India, Türkiye, South Korea, Taiwan, Bangladesh, Pakistan – still strongly represented, now stand alongside a growing number of emerging or nearby countries. Up to 35 countries were represented this year, notably Bulgaria, Armenia, Estonia, Kyrgyzstan, Uzbekistan, Mongolia, Myanmar and Ghana. Looking for new directions For some buyers, diversification is now as much a question of competitiveness as of securing flows. Longer transport times and disruptions to maritime routes are indeed increasing interest in these alternative production areas, particularly in West Africa. The example of Andreas Eickelmann, from SVAN International Import-Export, illustrates these concerns. Previously sourcing his Denim collections (finished products) from Bangladesh, Vietnam, and Pakistan, he has explored alternatives in Africa for several years

articles.s: WRAP’s Durability Accelerator Initiative unites leading brands and retailers to define durability standards, prepare for regulation, and meet growing consumer demand for quality and value. Environmental action NGO, WRAP, highlights the urgent need for clearer, evidence‑based approaches to garment du
articles.x: WRAP’s Durability Accelerator Initiative unites leading brands and retailers to define durability standards, prepare for regulation, and meet growing consumer demand for quality and value. Environmental action NGO, WRAP, highlights the urgent need for clearer, evidence‑based approaches to garment durability, as more than a decade of their research shows that consumers and many industry experts cannot reliably identify durable clothing. Durability is consistently ranked among the top three drivers of consumer purchasing decisions. New insights from WRAP show that more than half of consumers would be much more likely to buy clothing described as durable, while most would respond positively to brands that can prove they design garments to last — by choosing to buy from them, continuing to do so, and being more likely to trust and recommend them. Yet WRAP’s research demonstrates that commonly held assumptions about what makes clothing last simply do not hold up under testing. The fashion industry contributes 8 – 10% of global greenhouse gas emissions. WRAP has shown that increasing a products’ active lifetime is the single most effective intervention that can be made to reduce the environmental impact of clothing, and durability is fundamental to this. Measuring, improving, and communicating product durability will help businesses reduce their overall environmental impacts and deliver on their climate commitments, as well as the requirements of the Science Based Targets Initiative (SBTi) and other voluntary initiatives. Rokonuzzaman, FCA, President of BGCCI, presided over the meeting. In his address, he emphasized the importance of deepening trade, investment and
articles.x: The Bangladesh-German Chamber of Commerce and Industry (BGCCI) held its 24th Annual General Meeting (AGM) today at 11:00 a.m. at The Westin Dhaka. Mr. Md. Rokonuzzaman, FCA, President of BGCCI , presided over the meeting. In his address, he emphasized the importance of deepening trade, investment and industrial cooperation between Bangladesh and Germany. He also reaffirmed BGCCI’s commitment to connecting German investors with credible Bangladeshi partners, supporting market entry and creating meaningful business opportunities for its members. The AGM reviewed the Chamber’s activities, key initiatives and financial performance during the year. Members also discussed BGCCI’s future priorities, with particular emphasis on strengthening member services, facilitating investment and expanding business cooperation between Bangladesh and Germany. The audited financial statements and audit report were presented by Mr. Adnan Md. Iqbal, Treasurer of BGCCI , who briefed members on the Chamber’s financial position and audited accounts. The meeting highlighted BGCCI’s continuing role as an effective bilateral business platform, bringing together companies, investors, government authorities, diplomatic missions, development partners and other stakeholders. Members underscored the importance of translating business dialogue into concrete trade, investment and industrial partnerships. The AGM concluded with a vote of thanks delivered by Mr. Md. Farooque Khan, Senior Vice President of BGCCI . He expressed his appreciation to the President, Board of Directors, members and participants for their valuable contributions and continued support to the Chamber. articles.t: AI에 관한 모든 것: 7Learnings의 Felix Hoffmann
articles.o: All About AI: Felix Hoffmann of 7Learnings
articles.s: 7Learnings' CEO & Co-founder on why AI won't replace pricing analysts and merchandisers, but free them from optimising thousands of SKUs by hand so they can focus on the strategic calls that need human expertise. The post All About AI: Felix Hoffmann of 7Learnings appeared first on The Interline .
articles.x: Originally released in The Interline’s AI Report 2026 , this executive interview with 7Learnings is one of a 17-part series that sees The Interline quiz executives from companies who have either introduced new AI solutions or added meaningful new AI capabilities into their existing platforms . For more exclusive interviews, stories and opinions from different industry perspectives, and real survey feedback from voices from every level of fashion, download The AI Report 2026 . We’re observing a big disconnect (in both our own fashion-only data and in wider benchmarks from other sources) between the increasing capability and reliability of AI, in both a general sense and in discrete applications, and the lack of trust that end users place in its outputs. What does trust in your specific applications of AI look like, and how do you achieve and measure it? The user needs to be able to understand why a recommendation for a decision was made. At 7Learnings specifically, we use predictions to help with different decision options. We have additionally implemented a few measures to build trust in our solution: Explainable AI: It is important for retail pricing optimization to avoid being a black box. As such, we explicitly show the drivers behind a recommendation, whether that’s competitor price elasticity, inventory runway, historical seasonality, or current marketing spend (important to note: it is almost always a combination of these and never one single metric). Override function: We track the human override rate. When a client first onboards, overrides might be higher as they test the solution. articles.o: European industry urges action on competitiveness
articles.s: European textile, clothing, retail and wholesale organisations have welcomed European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen’s latest commitments on competitiveness, trade and regulatory simplification, while calling for faster action to turn them into practical measures. In her State of the Unio
articles.x: European textile, clothing, retail and wholesale organisations have welcomed European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen’s latest commitments on competitiveness, trade and regulatory simplification, while calling for faster action to turn them into practical measures. In her State of the Union address on September 16th, von der Leyen said Europe needed to move more quickly to strengthen its economy, complete the Single Market and reduce the administrative burden on companies. She also proposed a pact with Member States against the “gold-plating” of EU legislation through additional national requirements. Both Euratex, representing Europe’s textile and clothing industry, and EuroCommerce, representing retail and wholesale, have welcomed these commitments but stressed the urgency of implementation. Second China shock Euratex said industrial competitiveness received comparatively limited attention in the wide-ranging address and called for manufacturing sectors such as textiles to be placed more firmly at the centre of the EU agenda. “Europe cannot build a strong defence, lead the green and digital transitions, or protect its social model on a weakening industrial base,” said Euratex director general Dirk Vantyghem. “Competitiveness is not just one chapter of the European project – it is the foundation all the others are built on.” The organisation particularly welcomed von der Leyen’s focus on trade with China. The Commission president said the EU’s trade deficit with China had reached €1 billion a day and warned that what has been described as a “second China shock” was already contributing to deindustrialisation in European manufacturing regions. articles.o: Monforts ATC: Turning New Ideas Into Industrial Reality
articles.s: MÖNCHENGLADBACH, Germany — September 21, 2026 — The Monforts Advanced Technology Centre (ATC), initially opened in 2013 and subsequently expanded, continues to be an invaluable resource to customers from around the world in achieving new standards in fabric finishing. Covering an area of 1,200 squar
articles.x: MÖNCHENGLADBACH, Germany — September 21, 2026 — The Monforts Advanced Technology Centre (ATC), initially opened in 2013 and subsequently expanded, continues to be an invaluable resource to customers from around the world in achieving new standards in fabric finishing. Covering an area of 1,200 square metres, the Monforts ATC at the company’s headquarters in Mönchengladbach houses two full MONTEX finishing lines, engineered to accommodate an extremely diverse range of processes, in addition to a THERMEX range for the continuous dyeing of denim and other woven fabrics, a full colour kitchen and a number of lab-scale systems for smaller batch trials. “The ATC allows our customers to test their own textiles and technical fabrics on Monforts dyeing and finishing machines under fully confidential, real production conditions,” says the company’s Marketing Manager Nicole Croonenbroek. “Using the results from these trials, we are also able to make recommendations for improving many fabric finishes.” Technical textiles A highly-controlled and contained environment was a key consideration when constructing the special MONTEX line for technical textiles at the ATC. articles.t: Jeanologia는 환경 절약에 대한 수치를 제시합니다.
articles.o: Jeanologia puts figures on environmental savings
articles.s: Jeanologia says the use of its textile finishing technologies worldwide prevented 21.52 million cubic metres of water from being polluted and avoided 103.53 million kg of CO2 emissions during 2025, compared with conventional processes. The figures are contained in the Spanish company’s Sustainabilit
articles.x: Jeanologia says the use of its textile finishing technologies worldwide prevented 21.52 million cubic metres of water from being polluted and avoided 103.53 million kg of CO2 emissions during 2025, compared with conventional processes. The figures are contained in the Spanish company’s Sustainability Report 2025, which also records a 13.64% reduction in the carbon footprint of its own operations. Jeanologia’s operational footprint fell from 895.79 tons of CO2 equivalent in 2024 to 773.57 tons in 2025, as the company continued to develop technologies aimed at reducing the water, chemicals and energy demands of textile finishing. The Valencia-based company has spent more than 30 years developing processes including laser, ozone and e-flow technologies, initially making a major impact in denim finishing and subsequently expanding into other areas of garment processing, dyeing and finishing. “Sustainability is not a destination or a department but a way of thinking, creating and acting,” says founder and CEO Enrique Silla. “Real transformation only happens when sustainability and business progress together.” 100,000 production processes Jeanologia has also carried out its first voluntary assessment against the EU Taxonomy – the classification system established to identify environmentally sustainable economic activities. It found that 96.37% of its turnover was associated with Taxonomy-aligned activities, along with 84.43% of capital expenditure and 34.96% of operating expenditure. These activities principally contribute to climate change mitigation and adaptation and the transition towards a circular economy. articles.s: New discontinuous dyeing technologies focus on resource efficiency, process consistency and gentle fabric handling Swiss textile machinery manufacturer Benninger has introduced its latest discontinuou...
articles.x: New discontinuous dyeing technologies focus on resource efficiency, process consistency and gentle fabric handling Swiss textile machinery manufacturer Benninger has introduced its latest discontinuous dyeing technologies, FabricMaster and SynthMaster , to the Bangladesh textile industry, highlighting new approaches to resource efficiency, process consistency and gentle fabric handling. The technologies were presented recently at a seminar in Dhaka , titled “The sustainable way of discontinuous dyeing. Fast, cost effective and zero footprints.” The event was jointly organized by Benninger and Global Hitech , Benninger’s agent for discontinuous dyeing machinery in Bangladesh. Figure 1: The event brought together more than 100 textile industry professionals to explore the capabilities of FabricMaster and SynthMaster and the future of sustainable discontinuous dyeing in Bangladesh More than 100 textile industry professionals attended the seminar, which brought together dyeing and finishing professionals to explore developments in discontinuous dyeing and the changing requirements of modern textile production. With more than 160 years of experience in textile machinery and finishing technologies, Benninger used the Dhaka event to demonstrate how its latest machine concepts are responding to the increasing complexity of fabrics, growing resource-efficiency requirements and the need for more consistent production. articles.o: Functional textiles drive Intertextile
articles.s: Intertextile Shanghai Apparel Fabrics – Autumn Edition 2026 concluded with functional textiles, sustainable fibres and digital technologies playing an increasingly prominent role in the international sourcing event. Held from 25-27 August at the National Exhibition and Convention Center in Shanghai,
articles.x: Intertextile Shanghai Apparel Fabrics – Autumn Edition 2026 concluded with functional textiles, sustainable fibres and digital technologies playing an increasingly prominent role in the international sourcing event. Held from 25-27 August at the National Exhibition and Convention Center in Shanghai, the fair attracted more than 3,500 exhibitors from 30 countries and regions and over 100,000 visitors. The exhibition occupied 240,000 square metres and was structured around four key themes – Fashion Forward, Performance Textiles, Sustainability and Textile Future. Performance Textiles gained additional visibility through the upgraded Functional Lab, where fabric developments were presented in a more application-focused environment. Central to the area was The CUBE, an enhanced display combining fabric samples, product presentations and testing demonstrations. Technical displays from IDFL Laboratory and Institute and Sunshinetex International Holdings covered airshift and waterproof testing, down proof testing and down inspection applications. Across the exhibition, functional textile suppliers focused on four principal performance areas – thermal regulation, sustainability and comfort, moisture management and protection. Prutex Nylon partnered with Invista to present high-performance materials, functional yarns and sustainable solutions for a range of applications. Among these was Prueco Ocean, a material produced by converting discarded fishing nets into nylon 6,6. Prutex also highlighted the potential to combine the recycled material platform with performance properties such as cooling and moisture movement, illustrating how sustainability and functionality are increasingly being developed together rather than treated as separate sourcing requirements. articles.o: The LYCRA Company Appoints Hua Du As Chief Executive Officer
articles.s: WILMINGTON, Del. — September 15, 2026 — The LYCRA Company, a global developer of fiber and technology solutions for the apparel and personal care industries, announced today that Hua Du has been appointed chief executive officer, effective September 14, as the company enters its next chapter followi
articles.x: WILMINGTON, Del. — September 15, 2026 — The LYCRA Company, a global developer of fiber and technology solutions for the apparel and personal care industries, announced today that Hua Du has been appointed chief executive officer, effective September 14, as the company enters its next chapter following the successful completion of its financial restructuring. The LYCRA Company Appoints Hua Du as Chief Executive Officer. With 30 years of leadership experience in the specialty chemical and biotechnology industries, Du is well positioned to lead the company into its next chapter. Du succeeds Dean Williams, who served as interim chief executive officer and will continue in his role as chief financial officer. Du brings 30 years of leadership experience in the specialty chemical and biotech-based industries, driving transformational growth across global businesses. Du most recently served as CEO of Grobest Group, a private equity-backed animal nutrition business, where he led a comprehensive operational turnaround culminating in the company’s sale. Earlier in his career, he held senior leadership roles at Rhodia (later acquired by Solvay) and managed electronic materials businesses across Asia for Rohm and Haas, later acquired by Dow Chemical. “We are pleased to welcome Hua as The LYCRA Company’s next CEO,” said Bruce Rubin, executive chairman of the company’s board of directors. “With his extensive technical expertise, operational leadership, and global customer focus, we are confident that Hua has the experience and vision to help shape a successful future for the business. articles.t: HeiQ와 Archroma, ITMF International Collaboration Award 2026 수상
articles.o: HeiQ And Archroma Win ITMF International Collaboration Award 2026
articles.s: SCHLIEREN, Switzerland/ PRATTELN, Switzerland — September 21, 2026 — HeiQ and Archroma are proud to announce that their strategic partnership has been awarded the ITMF International Collaboration Award 2026, recognizing outstanding cooperation that advances innovation, sustainability, and competitiv
articles.x: SCHLIEREN, Switzerland/ PRATTELN, Switzerland — September 21, 2026 — HeiQ and Archroma are proud to announce that their strategic partnership has been awarded the ITMF International Collaboration Award 2026, recognizing outstanding cooperation that advances innovation, sustainability, and competitiveness across the global textile industry. The award acknowledges the success of the HeiQ-Archroma collaboration in bringing next-generation antimicrobial and odor-control technologies to textile manufacturers, brands, and retailers worldwide through a unique combination of innovation, technical expertise, and global market reach. The partnership combines Archroma’s worldwide commercial and technical platform with HeiQ’s expertise in creating high-performance and sustainable material technologies. Together, the companies have established a model for scaling innovation globally, enabling textile mills and brands to access advanced functional technologies more efficiently and effectively than ever before. “Our collaboration demonstrates what can be achieved when two organizations with complementary strengths unite around a shared purpose,” said Raquel Vaz Vieira, Executive Vice President, HeiQ Advanced Materials. “This award is not only a recognition of what has been achieved so far, but also an encouragement to continue pushing the boundaries of sustainable textile innovation. We thank ITMF for this honor and our customers, partners, and teams across both organizations whose commitment made this collaboration a success.” Dhirendra Gautam, Vice President, Marketing at Archroma, said: “This recognition from ITMF validates our belief that innovation has greater impact when it is made accessible at scale. articles.t: 글로벌 섬유 연합(Global Textile Alliance), 뉴욕 기후 주간(Climate Week NYC)에서 식물성 저탄소 데님 소개
articles.o: Global Textile Alliance introduces plant-based low-carbon denim at Climate Week NYC
articles.s: A new industry collaboration showcases how plant-based and low-carbon denim can transform the textile supply chain. The project brings together key global players to create Naturalls, a sustainable d...
articles.x: A new industry collaboration showcases how plant-based and low-carbon denim can transform the textile supply chain. The project brings together key global players to create Naturalls, a sustainable denim collection. The involved companies include The Lycra Company, Avalo, Neela by Sapphire Fibers Ltd., and Soko. They presented this project during Climate Week NYC. Figure: Global Textile Alliance introduces plant-based low-carbon denim at Climate Week NYC. Courtesy: Collected Every piece of clothing begins in a field. Climate change places huge demands on modern farming. Designers and product developers need sustainable choices that deliver high performance. This collaboration proves that fashion can achieve high impact without trading off innovation. The fabrics in this collection offer exceptional softness. They feature a combination of Low-Footprint Cotton from Avalo and Renewable Lycra fiber from The Lycra Company. The cotton requires zero irrigation and uses 75 percent less fertilizer. It also generates half the carbon emissions of conventionally grown cotton. The Renewable Lycra fiber contains 70 percent renewable content. This lowers the fiber carbon footprint by up to 45 percent compared to standard spandex. Neela managed the spinning, weaving, and garment production. The mill focused on strong fabric aesthetics, comfort, and visual appeal. Soko applied its advanced Hydrogel and Rare technologies for garment finishing. Hydrogel turns water into a gel and allows multiple treatments in one bath. This process cuts water consumption by up to 85 percent, energy use by up to 68 percent, and processing time by up to 50 percent. The Rare technology uses naturally derived mineral pigments and natural binders to create rich shades.

Figure: Mohammad Ashraful Islam, Editor, Textile Focus Today, as we celebrate our 10th Anniversary , we look back with gratitude and pride- and forward with renewed determination. Over the past decade, Bangladesh’s textile and apparel industry has undergone remarkable transformation. It has navigated global disruptions, technological change, sustainability demands, evolving consumer expectations, and intensifying competition. Throughout this journey, Textile Focus has remained committed to documenting the industry, amplifying its voices, and creating meaningful connections. Our name reflects our responsibility. We believe industry media should do more than report what has happened. It should help stakeholders understand what is happening, why it matters, and where the industry is heading . That responsibility matters more than ever as the sector enters a new era. Sustainability, circularity, renewable energy, digitalization, automation, artificial intelligence, and advanced manufacturing are redefining the global textile and apparel landscape. articles.x: SHANGHAI — September 18, 2026 — Yarn Expo Autumn 2026 concluded with approximately 600 exhibitors from 14 countries and regions, connecting with nearly 22,000 visitors from 110 represented markets, bringing the textile industry’s evolving material agenda into sharper focus. Nearly 22,000 visitors gathered at Yarn Expo Autumn 2026 to explore global yarn and fibre innovations. (Photo: Messe Frankfurt) Held alongside Intertextile Shanghai Apparel Fabrics – Autumn Edition, CHIC and PH Value, the fair connected upstream fibre and yarn innovation with fabric development, garment production and fashion-market demand. Its broad product offering enabled buyers to assess recycled, bio-based and regenerated fibres alongside performance-led solutions, demonstrating how responsible choices can meet practical requirements across textile applications. Industry players from across the textile spectrum made new business connections, supporting cross-border sourcing dialogue and the commercialisation of innovation. Speaking at the fair’s conclusion, Ms Wilmet Shea, General Manager of Messe Frankfurt (HK) Ltd, commented: “This edition showed that sustainability and performance are no longer separate product categories; buyers increasingly expect credible solutions that deliver both. By bringing material innovators, processors, spinners, brands and downstream buyers together face to face, Yarn Expo Autumn 2026 has turned shared priorities into practical discussions and tangible business outcomes. articles.x: JYVÄSKYLÄ, Finland — September 17, 2026 — Spinnova Plc (“Spinnova” or the “company”), a materials technology company producing textile fibre from wood pulp and waste streams, has signed a non-binding letter of intent with Tearfil – Indústria Têxtil, S.A. (“Tearfil”) and its shareholders concerning a potential acquisition by Spinnova of all shares in Tearfil. Tearfil is a Portuguese yarn spinning company and a key development partner in Spinnova’s ecosystem. The contemplated transaction would strengthen Spinnova’s position in the textile value chain by securing dedicated yarn development and spinning capabilities for SPINNOVA® fibre. The potential acquisition is intended to shorten development cycles, provide greater control over the conversion of SPINNOVA® fibre into customer-ready yarns and textile applications, and accelerate commercialisation with brand and supply chain partners. “Tearfil has been an important partner for Spinnova, playing a key role in advancing SPINNOVA® fibre toward commercial applications,” said Janne Poranen, CEO of Spinnova. “Bringing these capabilities into Spinnova would strengthen our ability to support broader adoption of SPINNOVA® fibre and advance the commercial scaling of our technology”. The letter of intent sets out the parties’ current understanding of the framework for the potential acquisition, including an initial purchase valuation of EUR 500,000 paid in cash and Spinnova’s shares for all shares in Tearfil. Except for certain provisions expressly stated to be binding, the letter of intent is non-binding and does not create an obligation for Spinnova to proceed with or complete the acquisition. articles.o: Spinnova moves to acquire Tearfil to accelerate fiber commercialization
articles.s: Finnish textile fiber innovator Spinnova has signed a non-binding letter of intent to acquire Portuguese yarn spinning company Tearfil. The deal aims to strengthen its yarn development capabilities an...
articles.x: Finnish textile fiber innovator Spinnova has signed a non-binding letter of intent to acquire Portuguese yarn spinning company Tearfil. The deal aims to strengthen its yarn development capabilities and accelerate the commercialization of its fiber. Figure: Spinnova develops textile fiber from wood-based and waste-based raw materials. Courtesy: Collected Tearfil is an existing partner of Spinnova. The proposed acquisition would bring dedicated yarn development and spinning capabilities within Spinnova’s operations. According to Spinnova, the move would give the company greater control over the conversion of its fiber into customer-ready yarns. It also expects the integration to shorten development cycles. Spinnova develops textile fiber from wood-based and waste-based raw materials. The company has been working to scale the technology and expand its commercial applications across the textile industry. By bringing yarn development and spinning capabilities in-house, Spinnova aims to improve coordination between fiber production and yarn development. This could also help it respond more quickly to customer requirements during product development. The proposed deal is part of Spinnova’s efforts to advance its fiber technology from development toward wider commercial use. However, the letter of intent is non-binding, and the acquisition remains subject to further discussions and the completion of the required conditions. If completed, the transaction would combine Spinnova’s fibre technology with Tearfil’s yarn development and spinning expertise.

articles.o: Eurojersey launches ‘Out of Frame’ sportswear fabric concept
articles.s: Italian warp knitting specialist Eurojersey has launched its ‘Out of Frame’ concept, featuring a range of warp-knitted fabrics developed for performance sportswear. The concept focuses on fabrics desi...
articles.x: Italian warp knitting specialist Eurojersey has launched its ‘Out of Frame’ concept, featuring a range of warp-knitted fabrics developed for performance sportswear. The concept focuses on fabrics designed for movement-led applications, from everyday exercise to high-intensity training across sports and wellness. Courtesy: Collected The company says the developments address the changing needs of performance sportswear, where fabric performance and freedom of movement are key requirements. Eurojersey plans to showcase the ‘Out of Frame’ concept at Performance Days in Munich and Functional Textiles in Shanghai later this year. The collection highlights warp knitting's role in developing fabrics for activewear applications. Warp-knitted structures can be engineered to meet different performance requirements, making them suitable for garments that need flexibility and comfort in motion. The new concept also reflects the broader development of sportswear beyond traditional high-performance applications. Wellness and everyday physical activity are creating demand for fabrics that combine performance with comfort and versatility.

articles.s: Four major textile and garment trade bodies have urged the government to introduce area-based gas rationing promptly to maintain industrial production amid the ongoing gas shortage. The Bangladesh Gar...
articles.x: Four major textile and garment trade bodies have urged the government to introduce area-based gas rationing promptly to maintain industrial production amid the ongoing gas shortage. The Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA), Bangladesh Knitwear Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BKMEA), Bangladesh Textile Mills Association (BTMA) and Bangladesh Terry Towel & Linen Manufacturers & Exporters Association (BTTLMEA) requested in a letter sent to the Managing Director of Gas Transmission Company Limited (GTCL) on September 16. Figure: The organizations proposed dividing industrial establishments into separate zones. The organizations proposed dividing industrial establishments into separate zones. They suggested preparing gas rationing rosters for each area instead of uniform distribution across all zones. Under the proposed system, gas supply to one industrial area could be restricted for four to five days while other areas receive adequate supply. The restrictions would then rotate among different zones. The associations recommended that the rationing roster consider production dependency, industry type, employment, export contribution and safety to ensure gas is allocated according to industrial needs and economic importance. They also urged the government to promptly assess excess gas available in other distribution areas beyond their proportional allocation and reallocate it to the Titas Gas distribution area. Around 90% of industries are located within the Titas Gas distribution area, but inadequate gas supply has prevented the company from meeting industrial demand. articles.o: CHT Bangladesh Welcomes German Parliamentary Delegation and Ambassador
articles.s: A delegation of the German Bundestag visited CHT Bangladesh Limited at the Meghna Industrial Economic Zone to gain first-hand insights into the company’s local operations, production capabilities, and contribution to Bangladesh’s textile industry. Led by Nicklas Kappe, Chair of the German-South Asia
articles.x: A delegation of the German Bundestag visited CHT Bangladesh Limited at the Meghna Industrial Economic Zone to gain first-hand insights into the company’s local operations, production capabilities, and contribution to Bangladesh’s textile industry. Led by Nicklas Kappe, Chair of the German-South Asian Parliamentary Friendship Group, the delegation included Members of the German Bundestag Johann Saathoff, Ulle Schauws, and Gerold Otten. They were joined by Katerina Bienert from the Administration of the German Bundestag. The delegation was accompanied by Dr Rüdiger Lotz, Ambassador of the Federal Republic of Germany to Bangladesh, and representatives of the German Embassy in Dhaka, including Olga Nowikow Winnen, Economic Attaché, and Monika Reuter, Head of Political, Press and Culture. Prodip Kumar Dhar, Managing Director and Head of Production Site, welcomed the guests together with the management team of CHT Bangladesh Limited. During a tour of the plant, the visitors learned more about CHT Bangladesh’s production, technical expertise, quality standards, and approach to responsible manufacturing and environmental protection. The exchange focused on the role of German companies in Bangladesh, opportunities for sustainable industrial development, and the importance of technology, innovation, and long-term cooperation in strengthening economic relations between the two countries. “We are honored to welcome the German parliamentary delegation and representatives of the German Embassy to our site. articles.s: BGMEA participated in VisionSpring Bangladesh’s 25th Anniversary Partnership Event as an advocacy partner. Independent research, including a randomized controlled trial, found that providing reading glasses to workers increased productivity by 5.7%, generated an additional $156 in annual factory gai
articles.x: BGMEA participated in VisionSpring Bangladesh’s 25th Anniversary Partnership Event as an advocacy partner. Independent research, including a randomized controlled trial, found that providing reading glasses to workers increased productivity by 5.7%, generated an additional $156 in annual factory gains per worker, and delivered a 269% return on investment for manufacturers. BGMEA has played a significant role in advancing the initiative through sustained advocacy, advocating VisionSpring’s Clear Vision Workplaces program among its member factories. In recognition of its contribution, BGMEA received an Advocacy Partner Award from VisionSpring Bangladesh. The partnership continues to strengthen efforts to ensure access to clear vision for RMG workers nationwide. Ms. Rumana Rashid and Ms. Fahima Akter, Directors of BGMEA, received the award on behalf of the association. articles.o: Global Standards announce launch of GRTS, a new textile processing standard covering a broader range of eligible fibres
articles.s: Stuttgart, Germany, 14 September 2026 Today marks the public laurich of the Global Responsible Textile Standard (GRTS), a new standard for the processing of textiles made from fibres certified to third-party standards recognised by GRTS arid covering a broad range of plant, animal, synthetic, man-ma
articles.x: Stuttgart, Germany, 14 September 2026 Today marks the public laurich of the Global Responsible Textile Standard (GRTS), a new standard for the processing of textiles made from fibres certified to third-party standards recognised by GRTS arid covering a broad range of plant, animal, synthetic, man-made cellulosic and recycled fibres. GRTS has been developed based on decades of experience from the established Global Organic Textile Standard (GOTS). Until now, products outside GOTS’ organic fibre eligibility criteria had no equivalent certification route within the Global Standards system. GRTS meets a growing industry demand for a textile processing standard that defines environmental and human rights criteria for the processing and physical traceability of a broader range of fibres Claudia Kersten, Managing Director of Global Standards, said: “Following our mission as a non-profit Voluntary Sustainability Standard setter, we aim to ensure the highest level of social and environmental impact in textile value chains. GRTS is a strategic and exciting step for us. By offering a standard that cover fibres beyond organic and building it on the same system as GOTS, we support the inry’s business case for sustainability and enable more positive impact together.” Independent third-party certification and physical traceability GRTS sets defined environmental, chemical, human rights, business conduct, due diligence and traceability requirements. For fibres to enter the GRTS system, they must be certified to third-party fibre standards recognised by GRTS and meet social, ecological and traceability criteria, including the prohibition of highly hazardous chemicals and GMOs, chain of custody with identity preservation and the inclusion of social norms in fibre production, among others

articles.s: 중국에서 제조된 가짜 화장품과 건강기능식품이 국내 물류거점을 거쳐 온라인 오픈마켓에서 정품처럼 판매된 대규모 유통망이 적발됐다. 특히 국내 K뷰티 브랜드부터 글로벌 화장품 브랜드, 건강기능식품, 신발·골프용품까지 위조 대상이 광범위했고, 일부 기능성 화장품과 건강기능식품에서는 표시된 기능성을 뒷받침하는 성분과 지표물질이 검출되지 않았다.식품의약품안전처와 지식재산처는 17일 중국산 가짜 화장품과 건강기능식품, 정수기 필터 등을 국내에 불법 반입해 정품처럼 판매한 유통 브로커 A씨를 적발해 검찰에 송치했다고 밝혔다. 식약처와 지식재산처

articles.t: TBH글로벌, 日 판매량 성장… ‘무신사 글로벌 K-패션 효과 톡톡’
articles.o: TBH글로벌, 日 판매량 성장… ‘무신사 글로벌 K-패션 효과 톡톡’
articles.s: K-컬처에 대한 글로벌 관심이 높아지는 가운데, TBH글로벌(대표 우종완)이 일본 시장에서 빠르게 저변을 넓히고 있어 기대를 모은다.올해 8월 말 기준 ‘무신사 글로벌 스토어’를 통한 일본향 누적 판매수량이 전년 동기 대비 382% 증가했다고 18일 밝혔다. 같은 기간 주문건수와 매출액도 각각 383%, 228% 증가하며 큰 폭의 성장세를 기록한 것.무신사 글로벌 스토어는 국내 패션 브랜드의 제품을 해외 소비자에게 판매하는 온라인 쇼핑 플랫폼으로, 해외 소비자가 한국 상품을 직접 구매할 수 있는 역직구 형태로 운영되고 있다. 202

articles.t: 혁신 외면 “걱정만 하고 행동은 없었다”
articles.o: 혁신 외면 “걱정만 하고 행동은 없었다”
articles.s: 대구 섬유 산지에 암흑기가 본격 들이 닥쳤다. 시장 원리에 따른 타율의 혹독한 구조 조정 신호탄이 터지고 말았다.결국 올 것이 오고 말았다. 예상보다 2~3년 빨리 온 셈이다.불황에 장사 없듯이 코로나를 시발로 고개를 든 집단 붕괴 현상이 현실로 다가왔다. 사실상 지난 5~6년 가속된 시장 추락에 악전고투하다 결국 파탄의 불구덩이 속으로 내몰리고 있다.분초를 다투는 글로벌시장의 변곡점을 외면한 채 변화에 둔감한 천수답 경영이 몰고 온 필연적인 결과다. 중국이란 거대 공룡이 휘젓고 있는 쓰나미 상황을 빤히 바라보면서 걱정만 하고 행동

articles.s: 해피랜드 코퍼레이션(대표 임남희)이 전개하는 유아동복 브랜드 압소바가 산리오캐릭터즈의 ‘마이멜로디’와 협업한 26FW 가을 컬렉션을 18일 출시했다.이번 컬렉션은 ‘우리 아이 첫 마이멜로디’를 콘셉트로 마이멜로디의 캐릭터 요소와 압소바의 디자인을 결합했다. 따뜻한 가을 컬러를 중심으로 마이멜로디의 빨간 두건에서 가져온 레드 컬러를 포인트로 활용한 것이 특징이다.컬렉션은 의류를 비롯해 아이들의 일상에서 활용할 수 있는 다양한 아이템으로 구성했다. 마이멜로디의 디자인 요소를 제품 곳곳에 적용해 압소바의 26FW 시즌 스타일로 풀어냈다.

articles.o: BIS Invests ₹38.72 Crore Across 21 Laboratories to Strengthen Cotton Fibre Testing
articles.s: In a major boost to India’s textile and agriculture sectors, the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) has undertaken a national project to strengthen cotton fibre testing infrastructure across India. Operating… The post BIS Invests ₹38.72 Crore Across 21 Laboratories to Strengthen Cotton Fibre Testing a
articles.x: In a major boost to India’s textile and agriculture sectors, the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) has undertaken a national project to strengthen cotton fibre testing infrastructure across India. Operating as the National Standards Body of India under the Ministry of Consumer Aﬀairs, Food & Public Distribution, BIS is providing direct financial support to establish high-precision testing facilities in critical regional nodes. Under its Scheme for Supporting Other Laboratories for Creation/Augmentation of Test Facilities in Critical Areas, BIS with approval for the ₹38.72 crore initiative from the Department of Consumer Aﬀairs, GoI targets the modernization of 21 key laboratories operated by the Textiles Committee, Power Loom Service Centres, and the Cotton Corporation of India (CCI), located across key cotton-producing regions of India. ₹38.72 Crore Project Details and Upgrades Infrastructure Component Planned Deployment High Volume Instrument (HVI) Testers 22 Units Trash Analysers (TA) 44 Units Participating Laboratories 21 Network Labs Significant progress has already been achieved by BIS this year, resulting in the installation and commissioning of 14 HVI Testers and 28 Trash Analysers across 13 laboratories (comprising 11 laboratories of the Textiles Committee and 2 of the Cotton Corporation of India). These laboratories are geographically distributed across the Northern, Central, Southern, and Eastern zones. This ensures comprehensive coverage for major cotton-producing regions spanning Punjab, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, and Odisha. articles.s: 에스제이그룹(대표 이주영)이 전개하는 호주 브랜드 ‘헬렌카민스키(HELEN KAMINSKI)’가 천연소재 액세서리와 온라인 선물 판매에서 성장세를 보이고 있다.올해 상반기 액세서리 매출은 전년 동기 대비 42% 증가했고 카카오톡 선물하기 등 온라인 플랫폼의 선물 판매는 262% 늘었다.상반기 액세서리 매출 가운데 한국에서만 단독 전개하는 니트 액세서리가 60% 이상의 비중을 차지했다. 가을·겨울 시즌에는 전체 상품의 천연소재 비중이 약 86%에 달한다.대표 제품인 ‘밀란 캐시미어 니트 숄’은 100% 캐시미어로 제작했다. 3년 연속

articles.o: Dornbirn at 65 and the rise of China’s urban mines…
articles.s: Anyone attending the Dornbirn Global Fiber Congress in Austria this week (September 16-18) could be forgiven a slight sense of déjà vu. Sustainability, circularity and textile recycling have been recurring themes at the conference for well over a decade and this year’s 65th edition again put them ce
articles.x: Anyone attending the Dornbirn Global Fiber Congress in Austria this week (September 16-18) could be forgiven a slight sense of déjà vu. Sustainability, circularity and textile recycling have been recurring themes at the conference for well over a decade and this year’s 65th edition again put them centre stage. Its programme ranged from mechanical, chemical and enzymatic recycling technologies to circular workwear, fibre separation, renewable raw materials and the infrastructure needed to establish textile-to-textile recycling at industrial scale. Getting to scale There is certainly no shortage of technology, expertise or enthusiasm, but what remains much harder to identify is recycling at anything approaching the scale of Europe’s textile industry. “Having recognised the need for industry-wide change early, Europe’s competitive advantage is shrinking as its companies respond to a series of crises, one after another,” said Robert van de Kerkhof, president of the Austrian Fibers Institute during a CEO panel debate on the opening day of Dornbirn 2026. “We are losing the opportunity to pass on know-how to the next generation of leaders and China is no longer just leading in cheap production, but also in innovation. Europe is meanwhile leading in bureaucracy.” €1 trillion waste programme China is now putting a new expression at the centre of its circular economy thinking – the urban mine. Under its new Circular Economy Development Plan for the 15th Five-Year Plan period, covering 2026-2030, China increasingly regards the enormous volumes of material discarded by its cities and industries as a domestic source of raw materials. articles.s: 삼성물산 패션부문의 신규 여성복 브랜드이자, 온라인을 중심으로 전개해 온 '앙개(anggae)'가 올해 1월부터 8월까지의 누적 매출은 전년 동기 대비 129% 신장하며 신예 브랜드로서의 경쟁력을 입증했다.2024년 론칭한 앙개는 독특한 감성과 디자인, 우수한 품질을 바탕으로 여성의 실루엣을 감각적이고 유연하게 표현해 본연의 아름다움을 자연스럽게 드러내는 페미닌 컨템포러리 브랜드다. articles.t: BGMEA는 2026년 11월 18~19일에 Bangladesh 의류 및 섬유 전시회(BATEXPO)를 개최할 예정입니다.
articles.o: BGMEA set to hold Bangladesh Apparel and Textile Exhibition (BATEXPO) on 18-19 November 2026
articles.s: Bangladesh’s apparel industry is set to revive its flagship Bangladesh Apparel and Textile Exhibition (BATEXPO) after more than a decade, with the BGMEA planning a major international showcase of the sector’s transformation, innovation, sustainability and growing technological capabilities in Novemb
articles.x: Bangladesh’s apparel industry is set to revive its flagship Bangladesh Apparel and Textile Exhibition (BATEXPO) after more than a decade, with the BGMEA planning a major international showcase of the sector’s transformation, innovation, sustainability and growing technological capabilities in November this year. BGMEA President Mahmud Hasan Khan announced the programme at a press conference today, saying the 25th edition of BATEXPO will take place on November 18 and 19, 2026 at the Bangladesh-China Friendship Conference Centre in Dhaka. “After more than a decade, our largest and traditional flagship exhibition is returning to the domestic and international arena,” he said while addressing the press conference at the BGMEA Complex. BGMEA Vice President (Finance) Mijanur Rahman and Director Shah Rayeed Chowdhury were present among others. He said BATEXPO 2026 will serve as one of the BGMEA board’s major initiatives for country branding and will showcase the transformation of Bangladesh’s apparel industry before the global community. “BATEXPO is one of our board’s major initiatives for country branding on the global stage,” Mahmud Hasan Khan said. The event will highlight improvements in workplace safety and environment-friendly production alongside Bangladesh’s growing capacity to manufacture value-added and technology-driven apparel products. The exhibition will feature a Global Apparel Expo, Global Apparel Summit, AI and Innovation Hub and Sustainability and Circularity Exhibition. The programme will also cover sustainability, fashion, innovation and emerging trends in the global apparel industry. articles.t: Bangladesh 대표단, 지식교류 위해 독일 RUDOLF 본사 방문
articles.o: Bangladesh Delegation Visits RUDOLF Headquarters in Germany for Knowledge Exchange
articles.s: A delegation from Bangladesh visited the headquarters of specialty chemicals company RUDOLF in Geretsried, Germany, as part of a GIZ-supported knowledge exchange program focused on chemical management, sustainability, and industrial safety. The visit gave participants insights into product safety, c
articles.x: A delegation from Bangladesh visited the headquarters of specialty chemicals company RUDOLF in Geretsried, Germany, as part of a GIZ-supported knowledge exchange program focused on chemical management, sustainability, and industrial safety. The visit gave participants insights into product safety, chemical compliance, sustainability, certification systems, and environmental, health and safety (EHS) management in the European chemical industry. As part of the program, participants attended expert presentations and toured RUDOLF’s production facility to gain practical exposure to chemical management systems and industrial practices. The knowledge exchange also gave participants an opportunity to discuss responsible chemical management and share experiences related to sustainability and compliance. The programme was supported by the Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH. The initiative comes amid growing international expectations for stronger chemical safety, environmental compliance and sustainability across global supply chains. For Bangladesh’s export-oriented textile and apparel sector, such knowledge-sharing initiatives are increasingly relevant as manufacturers and suppliers work to meet evolving requirements for product safety, responsible chemical use, and sustainable production. The visit highlighted the importance of international collaboration and knowledge exchange in strengthening chemical management practices and supporting higher environmental, safety and sustainability standards across industries. articles.x: On September 16, HiTHIUM, a leading global energy storage technology company, officially unveiled its next-generation integrated sodium-ion energy storage solution at its “Powered Day in, Day out” launch event. The new offerings include the ∞Power N4.0MWh, a 4MWh sodium-ion energy storage system equipped with the high-capacity ∞Cell N785Ah sodium-ion battery. HiTHIUM also announced its plans to begin full-scale production and delivery in 2027. With a 30-year designed service life, the system provides an infrastructure-grade solution for sodium-ion deployment. Drawing on integrated capabilities spanning materials, cells, manufacturing, system integration, station applications and lifecycle services, HiTHIUM is moving sodium-ion technology from validation toward large-scale deployment. Photo: ∞Power N4.0MWh “Energy storage technologies must overcome two barriers to achieve large-scale deployment: affordability and availability,” said Dr. Nazar Yi, Chief Technology Officer of HiTHIUM. Sodium is abundant and widely distributed, supporting resource security and supply-chain stability. As sodium-ion material systems, manufacturing processes and supply chain continue to mature, sodium-ion batteries can move from an energy technology to infrastructure. articles.o: BUFT Students Achieve Champion and Second Runner-Up at National-Level Texillence 3.0
articles.s: Students of the Department of Fashion Studies, BGMEA University of Fashion & Technology (BUFT) have brought pride to the university by securing Champion and Second Runner-Up positions in the Fashion Runway/Ramp Show segment of Texillence 3.0, a national-level event organized by the Southeast Univers
articles.x: Students of the Department of Fashion Studies, BGMEA University of Fashion & Technology (BUFT) have brought pride to the university by securing Champion and Second Runner-Up positions in the Fashion Runway/Ramp Show segment of Texillence 3.0, a national-level event organized by the Southeast University Textile Club. Fariha Yesmen Sadia (Batch- 231) emerged as the Champion, while K.M. Mynul Hasan (Batch- 231) secured the Second Runner-Up position in the competition, demonstrating their creativity, design thinking, craftsmanship, and ability to translate meaningful concepts into distinctive fashion expressions. For the competition, which featured a 1990s-inspired theme, Fariha Yesmen Sadia presented her collection concept “Nomadic Bloom — Bold Botanical Appliqués Rooted in the Spirit of Boho Wanderlust.” Inspired by the nostalgia, simplicity, and free-spirited character of the 1990s, she incorporated Bangladesh’s traditional Kantha stitch as the primary craft technique. Through the intricate stitches, she sought to reinterpret the memories, emotions, and stories associated with a bygone era. She further incorporated patchwork and hand-painting to capture the spontaneous, nature-inspired aesthetic of Boho art. By bringing together diverse textures, colours, botanical motifs, and handcrafted elements, her design created a contemporary interpretation where 1990s nostalgia, Bangladeshi craftsmanship, and the spirit of Boho wanderlust converged. Meanwhile, K.M. Mynul Hasan presented a concept titled “Letter (চিঠি),” drawing inspiration from the emotional significance of handwritten letters during the pre-digital era. articles.s: The textile industry is entering a groundbreaking era. For a globally active textile industry, where competitiveness is closely linked to production efficie
articles.x: The textile industry is entering a groundbreaking era. Manufacturers face rising energy prices, growing sustainability demands, increasing labor shortages, and an unprecedented need for flexibility. For a globally active textile industry, where competitiveness is closely linked to production efficiency and cost leadership, this means that technology is no longer merely a means of improving operational processes – it is increasingly becoming a strategic differentiator. Against this backdrop, Barmag will present a innovation portfolio at ITMA Asia 2026 that goes far beyond incremental machine upgrades. From November 20 to 24, 2026, Barmag’s experts will be presenting next-generation spinning concepts, smart factory platforms, and groundbreaking technologies for filament, staple fibers and nonwovens at their booth D45 in Hall 6.1 at the NECC in Shanghai. In doing so, the company is laying the foundation for what it calls “A New Era” of textile production. At the center of this transformation stands one development in particular: Barmag POY 2.0. Every few years, an innovation emerges that fundamentally changes how an industry thinks about production. Barmag believes POY 2.0 represents exactly such a moment. The new spinning concept is the result of a complete re-evaluation of the entire POY process chain, from spinning and quenching to winding, parallel with a digital process control. Rather than improving isolated components, engineers reimagined the interaction between all process steps. articles.t: CiCLO는 침구에서 지속성이 낮은 합성 물질의 새로운 역할을 탐구합니다.
articles.o: CiCLO explores a new role for lower-persistence synthetics in bedding
articles.s: The bedding textile sector is seeing growing interest in materials that can deliver comfort and performance while addressing concerns around synthetic microfiber persistence. Against this backdrop, In...
articles.x: The bedding textile sector is seeing growing interest in materials that can deliver comfort and performance while addressing concerns around synthetic microfiber persistence. Against this backdrop, Intrinsic Advanced Materials is exploring new applications for its CiCLO technology in mattress ticking and other bedding textiles. The US-based materials company is working with HeiQ Materials to develop functional fiber combinations using CiCLO polyester and nylon. The latest development targets circular-knit fabrics used in mattress ticking and wider bedding applications. The fiber combinations are designed to provide several functions in one textile. These include moisture management, thermal comfort, and freshness. This makes the technology relevant for bedding products where fabric performance directly affects sleeping comfort. At the same time, the development focuses on reducing the environmental persistence of synthetic microfibers. Conventional polyester and nylon can shed microscopic fibers during textile use and washing. These fibers can persist in the environment for long periods. CiCLO technology is designed to make synthetic fibers more biodegradable under certain environmental conditions, helping address part of this concern. For circular-knit manufacturers, the development could create another material option for high-performance bedding textiles. For the wider synthetic fiber market, it highlights how environmental performance is becoming increasingly connected with the functional value of a textile.

articles.x: Shima Seiki will exhibit its latest computerised flat knitting and digital design technologies at Egypt Stitch & Tex in Cairo later this month. The Japanese flat knitting technology specialist will participate alongside its Egyptian sales representative TTS (El Masria for Trade & Technical Services) at the 24th International Exhibition for Textile & Carpet Machineries, Printing Technologies and Accessories, taking place at the Cairo International Convention Centre from 24-27 September 2026. Shima Seiki will focus on solutions for automated knitwear manufacturing and digital product development, with exhibits including its new N.SSR112 and N.SSR132 computerised flat knitting machines, SDS KnitPaint-Online software and SDS-ONE APEX4 3D design system. © Shima Seiki The N.SSR series is Shima Seiki’s global standard for shaped knitting, with the new N.SSR112 and N.SSR132 developed as more cost-effective options for knitwear manufacturers. Both machines feature a compact, lightweight carriage and the company’s R2Carriage system for quick carriage returns, designed to support increased productivity. © Shima Seiki Established Shima Seiki technologies incorporated into the machines include its Digital Stitch Control System, spring-type moveable sinker system, stitch presser, yarn gripper and cutter, and takedown comb. New features include a 52-inch, or 132cm, knitting width to accommodate larger garments, while optional sub-rollers provide additional flexibility for different products and market requirements. Shima Seiki says the machines combine competitive cost performance with Japanese manufacturing quality, reliability, safety and ease of operation. articles.o: 마텔라, 좋은 옷에 대한 높은 기준으로 고객 만족도 높여
articles.s: 여성의 아름다움을 현대적인 감각으로 풀어내는 컨템포러리 여성복 브랜드 마텔라(MATTELLA)가 소재와 제품 완성도에 대한 고객 만족도를 높여가고 있다.마텔라는 옷의 완성도를 결정하는 핵심 요소로 소재를 꼽고, 제품 기획 단계부터 디자인에 적합한 소재의 품질과 특성을 세심하게 살핀다.실크·캐시미어·밍크를 비롯해 일본에서 수입한 트리아세테이트 원단 등 제품별 디자인과 실루엣을 가장 잘 표현할 수 있는 소재를 엄선해 사용한다.좋은 소재의 선택에 그치지 않고 소재가 가진 장점을 충분히 살릴 수 있도록 디자인과 제작 방식에도 공을 들인다.

articles.o: Lycra names Hua Du as CEO
articles.s: The Lycra Company has appointed Hua Du as chief executive officer as the fibre and materials technology specialist enters a new phase following the completion of its financial restructuring. Du took up the position on 14 September 2026, succeeding Dean Williams, who served as interim chief executive
articles.x: The Lycra Company has appointed Hua Du as chief executive officer as the fibre and materials technology specialist enters a new phase following the completion of its financial restructuring. Du took up the position on 14 September 2026, succeeding Dean Williams, who served as interim chief executive officer. Williams will continue in his role as chief financial officer. The new CEO brings 30 years of leadership experience in the speciality chemicals and biotech-based industries, including responsibility for driving growth and transformation across global businesses. Most recently, Du was CEO of Grobest Group, a private equity-backed animal nutrition business, where he led an operational turnaround culminating in the sale of the company. Earlier in his career, he held senior leadership positions at Rhodia, which was subsequently acquired by Solvay, and managed electronic materials businesses across Asia for Rohm and Haas, later acquired by Dow Chemical. Bruce Rubin, executive chairman of The Lycra Company’s board of directors, said Du’s combination of technical expertise, operational leadership and international customer experience would support the company as it shapes the next stage of its development. “We are pleased to welcome Hua as The Lycra Company’s next CEO,” Rubin said. “With his extensive technical expertise, operational leadership, and global customer focus, we are confident that Hua has the experience and vision to help shape a successful future for the business.” Rubin also thanked Williams for his leadership as interim CEO during the company’s period of transition. Two hundred years ago, the single biggest leap in human productivity did not start in a laboratory, a bank, or a government ministry—it started in a cotton mill. From the spinning jenny t
articles.x: A presentation at the H&M Tech Event, August 2026. Scott Camp, Head of Engineering, Shapeshifter Technology Ltd. Two hundred years ago, the single biggest leap in human productivity did not start in a laboratory, a bank, or a government ministry—it started in a cotton mill. From the spinning jenny to the power loom, the modern manufacturing supply chain was born on the factory floors built to weave and spin fabric. Today, as artificial intelligence is hailed as the new industrial revolution, garment manufacturers are not latecomers to technology; their industry is where industrial transformation began. Speaking at H&M’s supplier conference in Shanghai, Scott Camp, Head of Engineering at Shapeshifter, framed the strategic choice facing modern apparel manufacturers. Historically, the ultimate winners of industrial revolutions were not the inventors of the machines, but the factory owners who adopted them first. When Edmund Cartwright invented the power loom in 1785, most weaving remained manual for another forty years. The factory owners who moved early—asking whether new technology delivered more fabric at lower costs—built unassailable competitive advantages, while those who delayed spent decades trying to catch up. The Core Challenge: Fabric Yield and Cutting Efficiency In modern apparel manufacturing, fabric accounts for up to 70 percent of a garment’s total production cost. The fundamental question for factory leadership remains unchanged: how to purchase only the fabric required and extract the maximum number of garments in the shortest possible time.
