articles.o: WUB textile engineering project secures 7th position at Bangladesh Innovation Fair 2026
articles.s: A research project titled “Natural Fiber Based PCB”, developed by the Department of Textile Engineering at World University of Bangladesh (WUB), has secured the 7th position at the Bangladesh Innovati...
articles.x: A research project titled “Natural Fiber Based PCB”, developed by the Department of Textile Engineering at World University of Bangladesh (WUB), has secured the 7th position at the Bangladesh Innovation Fair 2026. The project was selected from 930 submissions received during the registration period of the fair. Following a multi-stage evaluation, 50 projects were shortlisted for exhibition, with the WUB project eventually securing a place among the top 10 and being ranked seventh. The project team was led by Md Mostafizur Rahman, Associate Professor and Head of the Department of Textile Engineering at WUB. Team members included Mohammad Bellal Hoque, Assistant Professor, and Rajib Hasan, a student of the Department of Mechatronics Engineering. The project was supervised by Prof. Dr. MD Abdus Shahid, Professor, Department of Textile Engineering, Dhaka University of Engineering & Technology (DUET). Md Mostafizur Rahman said, “The Bangladesh Innovation Fair 2026 was the first-ever program in Bangladesh. Our project, Natural Fiber Based PCB" was selected to be showcased in the fair as one of the top 50 innovations.” It was a nice experience, especially networking among researchers, academics, students, professionals, and different industry leaders. Definitely, these innovations, networking, and knowledge sharing lead the country to a new era, he added. “Natural Fiber Based PCB” explores the use of natural fibre-based substrates as a sustainable alternative for printed circuit board (PCB) fabrication. The research aims to support environmentally responsible electronics while creating new value-added applications for the natural fibre sector. articles.o: BTMA seeks policy support to sustain primary textile industry capacity
articles.s: BTMA has urged policy measures to sustain production capacity and competitiveness in Bangladesh’s primary textile industry. It specifically called for retaining the facility to import 10–30 count cot...
articles.x: BTMA has urged policy measures to sustain production capacity and competitiveness in Bangladesh’s primary textile industry. It specifically called for retaining the facility to import 10–30 count cotton yarn against bank guarantees instead of under the bond system. The demands were raised at a discussion meeting on the current situation, challenges and required policy support for the primary textile sector held at Gulshan Club on Tuesday (September 15). BTMA President Showkat Aziz Russell chaired the meeting. Figure: Showkat Aziz Russell, President, BTMA. BTMA leaders said the primary textile industry is one of the major sources of raw materials for the country’s export-oriented sectors, particularly the ready-made garment (RMG) industry. They stressed that business-friendly policy support is necessary to maintain the sector’s production capacity and competitiveness. In this regard, the association called for maintaining the existing provision allowing imports of 10–30 count cotton yarn through bank guarantees instead of the bond facility. At the same time, BTMA urged the authorities to take strict legal action against those involved in misuse or irregularities related to the bond facility. The association said action against irregularities should be accompanied by efforts to ensure a simpler and more competitive business environment for legitimate and compliant industrial enterprises. The meeting also called for simplifying the processes for loan rescheduling, refinancing and restructuring for primary textile manufacturers. Entrepreneurs said appropriate policy support from the financial sector, considering production costs, banking conditions and competitiveness in international markets, would help sustain the industry’s capacity. articles.s: Ahsan Composite Limited has joined the Factory Innovation Pavilion at the TIE-ITET Textile Innovation Expo 2026, scheduled for 12–14 November at the International Convention City Bashundhara (ICCB) i...
articles.x: Ahsan Composite Limited has joined the Factory Innovation Pavilion at the TIE-ITET Textile Innovation Expo 2026 , scheduled for 12–14 November at the International Convention City Bashundhara (ICCB) in Dhaka. At the pavilion, Ahsan Composite Ltd. will showcase its innovative manufacturing practices, production technologies and diversified product portfolio. The company’s participation will offer visitors a closer look at how Bangladeshi manufacturers are improving their capabilities and responding to changing market expectations. Figure: Ishfaq Ahsan, CIP, Managing Director of Ahsan Composite Limited and Director of BKMEA welcomed the initiative. Ishfaq Ahsan, CIP, Managing Director of Ahsan Composite Limited and Director of the BKMEA, welcomed the initiative and highlighted the importance of presenting locally developed solutions to a wider industry audience. “The Textile Innovation Expo provides an important platform for Bangladesh’s textile and apparel manufacturers to demonstrate their progress, exchange practical knowledge and explore new opportunities. Through the Factory Innovation Pavilion, visitors will be able to see the technologies, practices and product developments emerging from our factories,” said Ishfaq Ahsan. He also invited textile and apparel professionals, innovators, technology providers, buyers and other industry stakeholders to visit the expo and explore the ideas and solutions that will support the next phase of Bangladesh’s textile industry. The Factory Innovation Pavilion is a dedicated segment of the TIE-ITET Textile Innovation Expo 2026. It will bring together leading manufacturers to present factory-level innovations, practical applications and measurable improvements from across the textile and apparel value chain. articles.o: Indorama Ventures presents innovative odor capturing technology at Dornbirn Global Fiber Congress
articles.s: Indorama Ventures, a global leader in fibers and nonwovens serving customers in hygiene and technical markets, will present its latest technological innovation in odor management at the Dornbirn Global Fiber… The post Indorama Ventures presents innovative odor capturing technology at Dornbirn Global
articles.x: Indorama Ventures, a global leader in fibers and nonwovens serving customers in hygiene and technical markets, will present its latest technological innovation in odor management at the Dornbirn Global Fiber Congress. The innovation has been developed to address one of the most important yet challenging performance requirements in absorbent hygiene and technical products: effective odor control. By incorporating odor-capturing functionality for a broad spectrum of odor-causing compounds directly into the fiber structure, the technology helps manufacturers create products that actively capture odor-causing molecules rather than simply masking them. This enables a more effective and long-lasting approach to odor management while maintaining the comfort and performance consumers expect, for instance from adult incontinence and feminine care products, as well as from technical products such as air conditioning systems. “Consumers don’t simply want odors to be covered up. They want products that help them feel comfortable, confident and protected throughout the day,” said Anne Louise Theut Meier, R&D Engineer for Textiles and Nonwoven Fibers at Indorama Ventures. “This is why our customers are looking for meaningful improvements to the user experience. This patented technology is a non-biocidal, and fragrance-free approach compatible with polyolefin and polyester fibers. It has undergone extensive evaluation using a combination of analytical and real-use testing methodologies. articles.s: TechnoSport, India’s largest activewear brand, has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Atal Incubation Centre (AIC) IIT Delhi, under the Atal Innovation Mission supported by NITI Aayog, to… The post TechnoSport and AIC IIT Delhi partner to Advance Made-in-India Performance Textiles f
articles.x: TechnoSport, India’s largest activewear brand, has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Atal Incubation Centre (AIC) IIT Delhi, under the Atal Innovation Mission supported by NITI Aayog, to establish T-CREST, the TechnoSport Center for Research and Entrepreneurship in Sports Textile, at IIT Delhi’s Sonipat campus. The initiative aims to build deeper scientific and engineering capabilities in India to develop world-class performance sportswear designed around the needs of Indian athletes and sporting conditions. As part of the collaboration, TechnoSport will invest ₹4.5 crore over three years towards research, prototyping and capability building in sports textiles. The partnership will combine TechnoSport’s expertise in textiles, product development, and manufacturing with IIT Delhi’s scientific and engineering know-how, creating a stronger bridge between research and high-performance product development. The MoU was signed in the presence of Prof. Vivek V. Buwa, Deputy Director (Strategic & Planning), IIT Delhi, Dr. Nikhil Agarwal, MD FITT, IIT Delhi, Mr. Alok Pandey, CEO AIC IIT Delhi, Prof. Bipin Kumar, Associate Professor, Department of Department of Textile and Fibre Engineering, IIT Delhi, and Puspen Maity, CEO, Technosport reflecting the initiative’s intersection of sport, science, manufacturing and technical textiles. Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, in his Independence Day address, referred to India’s progress across sports infrastructure, coaching, sports medicine and sports nutrition, and to the opportunities emerging within the wider support system around sport. articles.o: Portugal’s Tintex launches Digital Showroom
articles.s: Tintex Textiles has unveiled a revamped website featuring a new Digital Showroom, providing brands and textile professionals with online access to more than 500 fabric references. The Portugal-based textile manufacturer says the refreshed platform reflects the evolution of the company and strengthen
articles.x: Tintex Textiles has unveiled a revamped website featuring a new Digital Showroom, providing brands and textile professionals with online access to more than 500 fabric references. The Portugal-based textile manufacturer says the refreshed platform reflects the evolution of the company and strengthens its positioning within the international textile industry, with a more contemporary look and a reorganised content structure. The website places greater emphasis on the four principal markets for which Tintex develops fabrics – fashion, activewear, loungewear and underwear – while also highlighting sustainability and innovation, two areas that have played a central role in the company’s development. A major addition is the Digital Showroom, an online portfolio bringing together more than 500 fabric references. Existing and prospective customers can explore the company’s offering, search for individual references and filter fabrics according to different characteristics. © Tintex Textiles Detailed information is provided for each development, supported by imagery designed to give users a closer view of the fabrics. Tintex says the platform will make it easier for brands and industry professionals around the world to begin sourcing its developments remotely. The launch represents a further step in a wider communications strategy that Tintex has been developing in recent years. articles.t: Kornit은 주문형 상품에 대한 사례를 제시합니다.
articles.o: Kornit makes the case for on-demand merchandise
articles.s: Kornit Digital will demonstrate how on-demand digital textile printing can help licensed merchandise producers respond more quickly to changing demand at Brand Licensing Europe, taking place in London from October 6-8. The company will focus on production models that allow merchandise to be manufact
articles.x: Kornit Digital will demonstrate how on-demand digital textile printing can help licensed merchandise producers respond more quickly to changing demand at Brand Licensing Europe, taking place in London from October 6-8. The company will focus on production models that allow merchandise to be manufactured in response to actual orders rather than forecasts, reducing the need for large production runs and inventories. Licensed merchandise associated with films, music, sport, anime and other entertainment markets can be particularly exposed to rapidly changing consumer demand. Conventional production can require companies to decide which designs and quantities to manufacture months before products reach the market. Kornit says digital on-demand production can shorten this process, allowing new designs to be introduced quickly and successful products to be replenished as demand develops. It can also make much wider product ranges commercially practical. Rather than concentrating production on a relatively small number of designs expected to generate sufficient volumes, rights holders and licensees can make merchandise available for niche characters, artists and fan communities without manufacturing every product in advance. “Licensed merchandise is all about capturing the connection between fans and the culture they love – and those moments can happen incredibly fast,” says Guy Yaniv, president of Kornit Digital Europe. “On-demand production gives the industry the agility to respond when those moments happen, while reducing the inventory risk that has traditionally come with expanding merchandise portfolios.” Kornit customers already using the approach include Sweden’s Hybris Production, which produces licensed movie merchandise, while Basic Thinking and Fifth Column operate

articles.o: Bally Ribbon Mills To Showcase Award-Winning 3-D Woven Composite Technologies At CAMX 2026
articles.s: BALLY, Pa. — September 10, 2026 — Bally Ribbon Mills (BRM), a designer, developer, and manufacturer of highly specialized engineered woven fabrics, will showcase its high-quality, high-performance products at CAMX 2026, that will take place on September 21–24, 2026 at the Georgia World Congress Cent
articles.x: BALLY, Pa. — September 10, 2026 — Bally Ribbon Mills (BRM), a designer, developer, and manufacturer of highly specialized engineered woven fabrics, will showcase its high-quality, high-performance products at CAMX 2026, that will take place on September 21–24, 2026 at the Georgia World Congress Center (GWCC) in Atlanta, Georgia. BRM experts were on hand in booth K46 to discuss the company’s 3-D woven joints, thermal protection systems (TPS), and other 3-D structures. BRM was named a 2016 JEC Innovation Award winner in the Space category, recognizing the company’s contributions to advanced composite technology for space-related applications. The award underscores BRM’s longstanding expertise in developing engineered woven solutions that help meet critical performance requirements while supporting lightweight, efficient composite structures. Using 3-D continuous weaving, BRM creates new joint structures and improves existing designs. The company’s 3-D woven joints are available in Pi (π), double-T, H, and other complex net shapes. Designed to deliver strength, durability, and structural integrity, these woven shapes can help reduce component weight and cost without sacrificing performance. Because reinforcement is integrated throughout all three dimensions of the weave, BRM’s 3-D woven structures support load paths across joined substructures. The architecture of each woven shape can be tailored to the needs of the overall structure and its individual components. BRM’s 3D woven composites are also well suited for aerospace thermal protection systems. These mission-critical components are used in demanding heat-shield applications, including space exploration vehicles. articles.s: Mimaki Europe, a leading manufacturer of industrial inkjet printers and cutting plotters, announces the TxF330-800, its new direct-to-film (DTF) printer. Designed to support stable, high-quality garment decoration in demanding print environments, the system combines automated maintenance, expanded w
articles.x: New TxF330-800 direct-to-film (DTF) printer enhances automation and supports longer, continuous garment decoration. Mimaki Europe , a leading manufacturer of industrial inkjet printers and cutting plotters, announces the TxF330-800 , its new direct-to-film (DTF) printer. Designed to support stable, high-quality garment decoration in demanding print environments, the system combines automated maintenance, expanded white ink capacity and advanced production capabilities to streamline workflow. Photo: The TxF330-800, Mimaki’s new direct-to-film printer for high-quality garment decoration. Longer Print Runs with Greater Stability Delivering 1.5x the production speed of the previous TxF300-75 model, the TxF330-800 is equipped for long, uninterrupted production runs with an expanded 16-cartridge ink system. Up to eight white ink slots provide up to 4L of capacity, while Mimaki’s UISS (Uninterrupted Ink Supply System) allows print providers to replace cartridges without stopping production. The printer also incorporates Mimaki Feed Tension Technology (MFT), which improves film transport without applying additional tension. This reduces the risk of misalignment during high-speed and long-duration printing and supports stable, precise image quality. To extend productivity further, rotary wipers have been introduced for easier maintenance of the print heads, while minimising ink splatter during wiping. MCT2 (Mimaki Circulation Technology) helps to prevent ink blockages which can slow down production. articles.t: 직물은 고성능 가정을 부드럽게 만든다
articles.o: Textiles soften the high-performance home
articles.s: Technical performance is increasingly moving from outdoor clothing into the home, but a parallel demand for tactile, natural and understandable materials is emerging as consumers seek relief from increasingly technology-driven lives. This apparent contradiction was at the heart of the Heimtextil Tre
articles.x: Technical performance is increasingly moving from outdoor clothing into the home, but a parallel demand for tactile, natural and understandable materials is emerging as consumers seek relief from increasingly technology-driven lives. This apparent contradiction was at the heart of the Heimtextil Trends 27/28 online preview held on September 7th, ahead of next January’s Heimtextil exhibition in Frankfurt. Developed by Milan-based design studio Alcova under the theme Home-Maxxing – The Performance of Everyday Living , the trends identify the growing influence of a culture in which everything from sleep and fitness to personal wellbeing is measured and optimised. The result is a new generation of domestic products drawing on technologies and visual cues previously associated with sportswear, outdoor equipment and other high-performance applications. At the same time, however, Alcova sees consumers seeking more analogue experiences through tactile materials, visible construction and products that reveal how they are made and age naturally over time. “Textiles are a way of compensating for this technological drift that the home has undergone,” says Alcova co-founder Joseph Grima. Performance moves indoors The first of three identified directions, Staged Competence , reflects the migration of the technical language of outdoor products into interiors. Performance characteristics are increasingly being made visible rather than concealed, with technical graphics, fastenings, labels and specification-style information becoming part of the aesthetic of furniture and home textiles. articles.o: Shein dominates social media fashion haul culture
articles.s: Shein accounts for more than half of the fashion haul posts identified in a new analysis of TikTok content, highlighting the continuing influence of social media in encouraging high-volume clothing purchases. The study, carried out by UK textile waste management company Bins.co.uk, examined hashtags
articles.x: Shein accounts for more than half of the fashion haul posts identified in a new analysis of TikTok content, highlighting the continuing influence of social media in encouraging high-volume clothing purchases. The study, carried out by UK textile waste management company Bins.co.uk, examined hashtags associated with 24 fashion brands and identified more than three million posts featuring fashion hauls – videos in which consumers or influencers display multiple items purchased in a single shopping trip or online order. Shein was associated with 1.6 million of these posts – more than twice the 738,200 recorded for Zara and far ahead of the other brands examined. Primark was third with 189,100 posts, followed by Princess Polly with 128,100 and H&M with 113,900. PrettyLittleThing, ASOS, Abercrombie & Fitch, Bershka and Stradivarius completed the top ten. The figures do not represent the number of purchases made from each company, but indicate the scale of social media activity surrounding haul shopping and the extent to which the practice has become associated with some of fashion’s biggest brands. Bins.co.uk suggests Shein’s particularly strong showing may reflect a business model built around low prices, frequent purchasing and digital engagement. Features including discounts and rewards, alongside its affiliate and creator programmes, provide incentives both to continue shopping and to share purchases online. Where customer numbers were publicly available, the researchers also attempted to relate haul posts to the size of brands’ customer bases. Shein recorded 5.86 haul posts for every 1,000 customers, compared with 2.30 for ASOS, 0.51 for Marks & Spencer and 0.39 for New Look. articles.o: INDA Hires Ben Muller As Executive Director
articles.s: CARY, N.C. — September 15, 2026 — INDA, the Association of the Nonwoven Fabrics Industry, announced today that Ben Muller has joined the association as executive director. Mr. Muller brings more than 20 years of progressive leadership experience spanning nonprofit organizations, corporations and tra
articles.x: CARY, N.C. — September 15, 2026 — INDA, the Association of the Nonwoven Fabrics Industry, announced today that Ben Muller has joined the association as executive director. Mr. Muller brings more than 20 years of progressive leadership experience spanning nonprofit organizations, corporations and trade associations. Ben Muller Most recently, Mr. Muller served on the senior executive team of the High Point Market Authority, where he led marketing, public relations and educational programming for one of the world’s largest trade shows. Previously, he held senior brand and marketing leadership positions with Hanesbrands and Kayser-Roth, gaining extensive experience in textile and apparel supply chains. He began his career serving mission-driven organizations, including the American Cancer Society and the National Multiple Sclerosis Society. Tony Fragnito, INDA’s current president and CEO, will transition to an executive consultant role in January 2027 to support the leadership transition and focus on projects and initiatives designed to expand the reach and participation of the Global Nonwovens Alliance (GNA). His planned retirement will occur in December 2027. The creation of the executive director position follows the formation of the GNA by INDA and EDANA and represents the next step in the evolution of INDA’s staff leadership to support the alliance. articles.t: 인터필리에르 상하이 카운트다운
articles.o: Countdown to Interfilière Shanghai
articles.s: Interfilière Shanghai 2026 is preparing to bring together the international intimate apparel supply chain when it returns to the Shanghai Exhibition Center from 13-14 October. More than 170 exhibitors are expected to take part in the two-day event, presenting products and technologies spanning fabri
articles.x: Interfilière Shanghai 2026 is preparing to bring together the international intimate apparel supply chain when it returns to the Shanghai Exhibition Center from 13-14 October. More than 170 exhibitors are expected to take part in the two-day event, presenting products and technologies spanning fabrics, yarns, fibres, lace, embroidery, trims and accessories, as well as OEM and ODM manufacturing, textile machinery, trend forecasting and associated services. Positioned as a leading Asian sourcing and business platform for lingerie, swimwear and activewear, this year’s exhibition will take place under the theme Innovation Re:Code, exploring how materials, design, technology and changing consumer expectations are reshaping the sector. A key element of the programme will be a masterclass from fashion trend expert Jos Berry, bringing together global trend research, intimate apparel design and commercial application. The session will include selected trend directions, sample runway presentations and forward-looking forecasts aimed at brands, designers and other industry professionals. The exhibition will also introduce its Her World themed curation, which uses physical spaces across the show floor to connect materials, creativity, trends, nature, culture and commerce. According to the organisers, each area has been developed around a different aspect of the intimate fashion supply chain, enabling visitors to explore relationships between materials, design, market trends and emerging consumer demands. Interfilière Shanghai forms part of the international Interfilière exhibition network dedicated to fabrics, accessories and solutions for lingerie, swimwear and activewear. The Shanghai edition has been operating in China since 2005 and connects domestic and international suppliers

articles.t: 태국 원형 패션을 뉴욕으로 가져가다
articles.o: Taking Thai circular fashion to New York
articles.s: Indorama Ventures is supporting KH Editions, a Thai fashion brand which has developed fabrics woven from deja recycled polyester yarn for its Spring/Summer 2027 collection at New York Fashion Week. KH Editions has used the fabrics for two looks and accompanying accessories in the ten-look collection
articles.x: Indorama Ventures is supporting KH Editions, a Thai fashion brand which has developed fabrics woven from deja recycled polyester yarn for its Spring/Summer 2027 collection at New York Fashion Week. KH Editions has used the fabrics for two looks and accompanying accessories in the ten-look collection, combining recycled materials with the brand’s playful and experimental approach to streetwear. The brand reinterprets Thai craftsmanship and identity while seeking to create new value from waste and recycled materials. This year, it was selected by Thailand’s Ministry of Commerce to participate in a programme promoting Thai fashion brands and creative talent internationally. The deja yarn supplied by Indorama Ventures is produced from recycled PET, demonstrating how materials derived from sources such as used bottles can be incorporated into fashion products without compromising design or functionality. Napat Tansuwan, co-founder and art director of KH Editions, says the brand’s involvement with recycled materials dates back to participation in the RECO Young Designer Competition in 2018 and 2020, when its founders were still students. It subsequently participated in RECO Collective in 2023 and 2025. “We do not see recycled materials and fabrics as limitations on design, but as starting points for new possibilities,” he says. “These experiences helped us deepen our understanding of materials and product development while building connections with industry partners. “For this collection, we wanted to demonstrate that environmentally conscious alternative materials can be transformed into bold, playful and distinctive streetwear while still clearly expressing the identity of our brand. articles.o: RE&UP’s Next-Gen Cotton fibers power Zalando’s private-label T-shirt collection crafted from innovative recycled textiles
articles.s: The partnership demonstrates industrial-scale textile-to-textile recycling in action, enabling brands to integrate recycled fibers into commercial production. RE&UP Recycling Technologies’ Next-Gen Cotton powers a new collection from Zalando’s private labels, marking a step forward in bringing texti
articles.x: The partnership demonstrates industrial-scale textile-to-textile recycling in action, enabling brands to integrate recycled fibers into commercial production. RE&UP Recycling Technologies’ Next-Gen Cotton powers a new collection from Zalando’s private labels, marking a step forward in bringing textile-to-textile recycled fibers into commercial fashion production. Launching on Zalando in August, the collection comprises five T-shirts across YOURTURN by Zalando and Even&Odd by Zalando , made from a circular-knit fabric blending 80% organic cotton with 20% RE&UP Next-Gen Cotton — textile-to-textile recycled fiber produced from textile waste. This is the first time RE&UP’s recycled fibers feature in Zalando’s private label assortment. As the fashion industry transitions to scale textile-to-textile recycling, RE&UP is providing the essential infrastructure to move beyond the pilot phase. The initiative addresses the scaling challenge, providing a blueprint for brands to integrate next-gen fibers without compromising quality. RE&UP’s proprietary process transforms pre- and post-consumer textile waste through sorting , deconstruction , and decolorization . The result is a range of recycled materials that meet the technical , performance , and traceability standards required for commercial textile production. “ Industrial-scale circularity is no longer aspirational but operational ,” said Özgür Atsan , Chief Commercial Officer of RE&UP . “ Through collaborations like this, brands can move from pilot projects to repeatable, scalable production with confidence .” “ Zalando’s Private Label brands are where entry price points, quality and new materials come together for our customers. articles.o: Bringing movement monitoring to rehabilitation
articles.s: Researchers at RWTH Aachen University are developing a washable smart jacket with integrated textile sensors for monitoring rehabilitation exercises, targeting a healthcare application in which wearable technology could have a clearly defined role. Smartwatches, fitness trackers and experimental sen
articles.x: Researchers at RWTH Aachen University are developing a washable smart jacket with integrated textile sensors for monitoring rehabilitation exercises, targeting a healthcare application in which wearable technology could have a clearly defined role. Smartwatches, fitness trackers and experimental sensor garments have made personal health monitoring increasingly familiar, but maintaining engagement with such devices over long periods has proved challenging. Rehabilitation potentially presents a different proposition, with monitoring required for a specific purpose and usually for a limited period. Developed as part of the PhysioTaix research project by ITA – the institute for technical textiles at Aaachen – the jacket is designed to monitor patients carrying out prescribed exercises, including those performed at home between appointments with physiotherapists. Sensors are integrated directly into the garment, avoiding the need to attach multiple individual sensors to different parts of the body. The jacket tracks movement in real time and transmits the resulting data to an app, where artificial intelligence is used to analyse how exercises are being performed. Patients can receive immediate feedback to help determine whether they are carrying out movements correctly, while therapists can use the recorded data as additional objective information when assessing rehabilitation progress. This addresses a practical limitation of physiotherapy. Recovery frequently depends on patients repeating exercises regularly between appointments, when a therapist is not present to observe their movements or correct mistakes. articles.s: Md. Waliul Islam Swapon graduated from BUTEX in 2002 and started his career in yarn dyeing. His long journey began with taking charge of launching a 1.5-ton capacity yarn dyeing project of Mondol Grou...
articles.x: Md. Waliul Islam Swapon graduated from BUTEX in 2002 and started his career in yarn dyeing. His long journey began with taking charge of launching a 1.5-ton capacity yarn dyeing project of Mondol Group with just two years of experience. Later, he played an important role in managing and developing various projects of the group including dyeing, fabric dyeing, garments, all-over printing. Since taking full responsibility of the garments business in 2013, he has been working closely with the expansion and technological development of Mondol Group. He is currently serving as the Executive Director (ED) of Mondol Group. Figure 1: Md. Waliul Islam Swapon, Executive Director (ED) of Mondol Group With more than two decades of experience, Md. Waliul Islam Swapon spoke about the current challenges, innovation, sustainability, traceability, investment and future growth of the textile and apparel industry of Bangladesh. Textile Today: What factors do you think are the most important behind the rapid growth of Mondol Group? Md. Waliul Islam Swapon: Mondol Group is a fast-growing organization. Many people have contributed to the current stage. However, one policy of our founding chairman Abdul Majid Mandal has been very effective—that is, decentralization. Due to this policy, the group has been able to quickly build and manage many organizations. By giving each organization, a specific responsibility and the opportunity to make decisions, the pace of work has increased and the organizations have grown rapidly. articles.s: CUYAHOGA FALLS, Ohio — September 1, 2026 — Americhem, a global supplier of custom polymer solutions, today announced the launch of nPure™ and nZorb™, two complementary PFAS-free functional additive technologies designed to engineer performance within the polymer matrix. Developed for fiber and nonwo
articles.x: CUYAHOGA FALLS, Ohio — September 1, 2026 — Americhem, a global supplier of custom polymer solutions, today announced the launch of nPure and nZorb , two complementary PFAS-free functional additive technologies designed to engineer performance within the polymer matrix. Developed for fiber and nonwoven applications, the technologies help manufacturers address two critical performance requirements: durable odor control and moisture management. As manufacturers continue to seek more durable, material-level solutions, functional additive technologies are gaining traction for their ability to deliver consistent performance while simplifying manufacturing by reducing reliance on separate topical treatment steps. By incorporating functionality within the polymer matrix, nPure and nZorb help customers engineer odor control and moisture management into fiber and nonwoven products while supporting processing efficiency and scalable commercial manufacturing. nPure transforms odor control from a temporary surface treatment into an engineered material property. The PFAS-free, fragrance-free, and non-biocidal technology captures and reduces malodors without relying on topical finishes or antimicrobial chemistries, helping manufacturers improve freshness and consumer comfort. Independent testing demonstrates adsorption of sweat, body odor, and selected volatile organic compounds (VOCs), and the technology is compatible with PP, PE, PET, and bicomponent fiber systems. Designed for scalable commercial manufacturing, nPure supports hygiene, medical, fibers, nonwovens, textiles, automotive interiors, packaging, and recycled polymer applications. nZorb transforms hydrophilic performance from a temporary surface effect into a PFAS-free, engineered material property. articles.x: BRIDGWATER, England — September 15, 2026 — Nonwovenn and CorpAcq have announced the formation of a corporate vehicle, named Technical Materials Group (TMG), to spearhead an ambitious growth and acquisition strategy. Experienced M&A practitioner, Keith Pickering, has also been appointed as Head of Acquisitions to lead the initiative Following the partnership transaction completed between Nonwovenn and CorpAcq (a TDR Capital portfolio company) in December 2025, the businesses have established TMG as the corporate vehicle to create an international specialist materials business. Keith Pickering TMG will focus on acquiring businesses in the UK, Europe and North America manufacturing IP rich products and specialist materials, such as highly engineered textiles, films, composites, ceramics and laminated products. Keith joins the business as a highly experienced M&A practitioner, having completed over 120 transactions in a 30-year advisory career. This included jointly founding Catalyst Corporate Finance in 1998, subsequently selling the business to Alantra Partners SA in 2017. Keith retired from the Alantra partnership at the end of 2025. articles.o: Global Standards launches new benchmark for responsible textile processing
articles.s: Global Standards, the organization behind the Global Organic Textile Standard (GOTS), has launched a new standard for responsible textile processing. Called the Global Responsible Textile Standard (GR...
articles.x: Global Standards, the organization behind the Global Organic Textile Standard (GOTS), has launched a new standard for responsible textile processing. Called the Global Responsible Textile Standard (GRTS), the new standard covers a wider range of certified fibers. It applies to fibers certified under third-party standards recognized by Global Standards. The standard aims to give textile processors a common framework for responsible production. It expands the organization’s work beyond organic textiles. GRTS builds on Global Standards’ experience with GOTS. Launched in 2006, GOTS is now used by more than 15,000 certified facilities across 87 countries. The new standard comes as brands and manufacturers face growing pressure to improve sustainability across their supply chains. Many companies now use different types of certified fibers in their products. For textile manufacturers, the development could create a wider route to demonstrate responsible processing practices. Its impact will depend on how brands, suppliers and certification bodies adopt the new standard.

articles.x: Macroeconomic Overview: Recent activity in bond markets has refocused attention on inflation and interest rates ahead of the next Federal Reserve meeting on September 16. The last time the Fed cut rates was in December 2025. The last time the Fed lifted rates was in July 2023. With the rise in bond yields, expectations that the central bank will maintain or raise rates may have increased. The latest data on the labor market, which were stronger than generally expected, may have reduced concerns about weakness in the employment portion of the Fed’s dual mandate. Meanwhile, the core measure of inflation (price index based on personal consumption expenditures) that the Federal Reserve tracks to help determine policy has been near 3.3% since March. The Fed’s official target for that measure is 2.0%. Since the surge in inflation that occurred after COVID, the lowest monthly reading is 2.6% (April 2025). With the latest inflation figures above that level, there may be motivation to keep monetary policy restrictive in pursuit of price stability. Officials with the Fed have stated they believe the factors that contributed to the latest rise in inflation, including tariffs and higher energy prices, are already incorporated into inflation rates and may not be sources of significant additional price pressure. These competing considerations could support a decision not to increase rates in September and introduce uncertainty around the immediate direction of monetary policy. Tariffs are another variable that could influence both inflation and the outlook for interest rates. There were two Section 301 investigations that were launched in March. articles.x: Key insights 10–30 count yarn accounts for about 60% of Bangladesh’s total yarn imports. Bangladesh’s annual yarn import bill reached about Tk300 billion, according to recent industry and customs data. Industry leaders estimate reopening closed and partially closed textile factories could create nearly 1.5 million jobs. The government raised the incentive for RMG exporters using locally produced yarn and fabric from 1.5% to 5% for FY27. Figure: To match NBR's import penalty with a strong pull factor, Bangladesh Bank raised the export cash incentive for garments using locally produced yarn or fabric from 1.5% to 5% for FY27. Bangladesh’s latest tightening of yarn import rules puts its long-struggling domestic spinning sector back at the core of national industrial policy. The regulatory shift explicitly targets 10–30 count cotton yarn. This workhorse product accounts for roughly 60% of total yarn imports and underpins the country's massive knitwear export engine. On September 13, 2026, the Ministry of Commerce asked the National Board of Revenue (NBR) chairman to suspend its decision to withdraw the duty-free bonded warehouse facility for imports of 10–30 count cotton yarn pending further review. The initial policy aimed to protect local industries while maintaining raw material access for genuine exporters. Under that decision, export-oriented garment factories had to provide a 100% bank guarantee on the import value along with certifications from BGMEA, BKMEA, or BTMA. Banks would only release the collateral after the complete repatriation of export proceeds. This policy shift follows an unsustainable import surge. articles.o: Honour for Archroma’s new FiberColors
articles.s: Archroma has won a coveted 2026 ICIS Innovation Award for Best Product Innovation from a Large Company for its FiberColors. These high-performance sulphur dyes are synthesized from pre-consumer wool waste, reducing industry reliance on petroleum-based inputs while contributing to the circular econom
articles.x: Archroma has won a coveted 2026 ICIS Innovation Award for Best Product Innovation from a Large Company for its FiberColors. These high-performance sulphur dyes are synthesized from pre-consumer wool waste, reducing industry reliance on petroleum-based inputs while contributing to the circular economy by upcycling unwanted wool that farmers would otherwise pay to dispose of. With FiberColors, Archroma has extended its patented EarthColors method of bio-based feedstock substitution from plant residue to coarse, non-commercial wool. Using a minimum of 50% wool waste as a primary feedstock instead of conventional petroleum-derived raw materials, it produces high-quality biosynthetic dyes that deliver the same dyeing and fastness performance as regular sulfur dyes, with no negative impact on water consumption, energy consumption or waste generation during dye manufacturing. “Archroma has led the evolution of sulphur dyeing for over a century by advancing what’s technically possible and proving it can pay for itself,” says Julio Perales, technical and product segment manager for denim at Archroma. “FiberColors is that approach in practice – using an agricultural waste output with high disposal costs to replace a petroleum-based input and produce a dye that performs at scale for mills and brands. We’re honoured it has been recognised by ICIS.” The dyes can be applied across multiple processes, including exhaust or continuous dyeing, denim coloration and textile printing for cellulosic fibers such as cotton, viscose, linen, bamboo and kapok, as well as wool. The palette offers warm shades for entire collections, from jeans and chinos to T-shirts, hoodies and home textiles. FiberColors products meet the bluesign criteria, are GOTS approved, and are published on the ZDHC Gateway

articles.s: German Development Cooperation and the Bangladesh Power Management Institute (BPMI) have launched specialised training programmes in solar and wind energy to strengthen the skills of engineering professionals and support Bangladesh’s transition towards renewable energy. The initiative is being imple
articles.x: German Development Cooperation and the Bangladesh Power Management Institute (BPMI) have launched specialised training programmes in solar and wind energy to strengthen the skills of engineering professionals and support Bangladesh’s transition towards renewable energy. The initiative is being implemented under the Skills Development for Sustainable Energy Solutions (Skills4SE) project, commissioned by the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ). Over the past four months, 77 professionals have successfully completed the programmes, including 64 graduates from solar photovoltaic training and 13 from wind power training. To mark the achievement and the strengthened institutional capacity of BPMI, an event titled “Just Energy Transition (JET): Opportunities and Challenges in Developing a Skilled Workforce for the Power Sector” was held in Dhaka on Sunday. The event brought together representatives from government, power utilities, academia, the private sector and development partners to discuss the growing demand for specialised skills as Bangladesh expands its renewable energy initiatives. Participants discussed emerging workforce requirements in areas including solar photovoltaics, wind power, battery energy storage systems (BESS) and hybrid renewable energy systems. articles.s: Italy’s Eurojersey is expanding its performance textile developments beyond its established synthetic stretch fabrics, with new materials targeting applications ranging from yoga and tennis to demanding outdoor and high-intensity sports. Presented under the company’s Out of Frame concept, the develo
articles.x: Italy’s Eurojersey is expanding its performance textile developments beyond its established synthetic stretch fabrics, with new materials targeting applications ranging from yoga and tennis to demanding outdoor and high-intensity sports. Presented under the company’s Out of Frame concept, the developments focus on the different performance requirements created by movement rather than individual sporting disciplines. They address properties including stretch, compression, breathability, moisture management, durability and comfort, with fabrics engineered according to the requirements of different activities. For yoga, wellness and other lower-intensity applications, Eurojersey has developed soft, highly stretchable fabrics designed to follow the body closely while providing freedom of movement and a second-skin feel. For tennis and other fast-moving sports, the emphasis shifts to lightweight, breathable constructions combining moisture management with stretch and comfort during rapid changes in movement. Perhaps the most significant new direction is the company’s first development in knitted cotton. Currently at an early stage, the project combines the natural characteristics of cotton with Eurojersey’s existing textile technology and represents an expansion of its research into new fibre and fabric combinations. At the more technical end of the range, Eurojersey is developing solution-dyed fabrics offering high abrasion resistance, alongside new membrane constructions intended for demanding conditions where protection and durability are priorities. The four areas form part of Eurojersey’s wider strategy to develop performance fabrics around specific functional requirements rather than conventional sportswear categories. articles.o: Global Cotton Production Projected to Outpace Consumption, but Risks Remain
articles.s: Global cotton production is projected to reach 26.2 million tonnes in the 2026/27 season, marginally outpacing estimated consumption of 25.9 million tonnes. However, early-season production risks — including weather volatility and pest pressures — could narrow that buffer as the crop progresses, acc
articles.x: Global cotton production is projected to reach 26.2 million tonnes in the 2026/27 season, marginally outpacing estimated consumption of 25.9 million tonnes. However, early-season production risks — including weather volatility and pest pressures — could narrow that buffer as the crop progresses, according to the September 2026 issue of Cotton This Month , published by the International Cotton Advisory Committee (ICAC). Historically, global production estimates decline by approximately 100,000 tonnes from initial projections as crop conditions clarify. Assuming normal seasonal developments, ICAC projects that 2026/27 production will likely ease toward 26.0-26.1 million tonnes, with steeper declines possible if major weather disruptions or pest outbreaks emerge. Key Regional Highlights China: Ongoing sales from state reserves, which began July 20 and have averaged roughly 8,000 tonnes per auction, are improving near-term domestic availability. However, eventual reserve replenishment — alongside potential weather risks in Xinjiang — could lead ICAC to revise China’s import demand upward later this season. India: Upward revisions bring estimated 2025/26 production to 5.5 million tonnes (+9%) and consumption to nearly 5.9 million tonnes (+7%), driven by strong domestic mill demand and textile export growth. The government’s five-year Cotton Mission and digital initiatives like the Kapas Kisan app (enrolling over 4.1 million farmers) and Kasturi Cotton Bharat’s blockchain traceability framework are bolstering long-term stability. Pakistan: Production remains constrained by climate variability, pest infestations, poor seed quality, and high input costs. articles.o: Bangladesh Innovation Fair 2026 highlights new opportunities for Bangladesh’s textile sector
articles.s: The Bangladesh Innovation Fair 2026 was held from 12 September to 14 September at Novo Theatre in the capital. The fair brought innovation, research, industry and entrepreneurs together with a strong...
articles.x: The Bangladesh Innovation Fair 2026 was held from 12 September to 14 September at Novo Theatre in the capital. The fair brought innovation, research, industry and entrepreneurs together with a strong focus on transforming new ideas into marketable products and economic activities. Prime Minister Tarique Rahman inaugurated the three-day fair as the chief guest. Organized under the theme “Innovation Ecosystem Toward Trillion Dollar Economy,” the event aims to establish an Integrated National Innovation Ecosystem (INIE) connecting innovators, researchers, industries, investors, policymakers, universities and development partners. Textiles and apparel feature prominently at the Innovation Fair 2026, with dedicated sessions alongside AI, green construction, climate resilience, and clean energy. Discussions also extent health, smart agriculture, and the digital economy, highlighting cross‑sector innovation for Bangladesh’s future. The inclusion of apparel and textiles reflects the growing importance of innovation, technology and research in strengthening the competitiveness of Bangladesh’s major export sector. The fair provides an opportunity to connect textile and apparel innovators with manufacturers, investors, technology providers and policymakers and explore pathways for converting research-based solutions into industrial applications. Notably, the fair features more than 1,000 innovations, over 15 sessions and dialogues, more than 50 universities, over 100 industry experts and more than 50 corporate organizations, according to a Ministry of Science and Technology press release. articles.o: ITET Delegation Meets Titas Gas MD, Urges Immediate Increase in Gas Pressure for Industries
articles.s: A delegation of The Institution of Textile Engineers and Technologists (ITET) Bangladesh held a meeting with the Managing Director of Titas Gas Transmission and Distribution Company Limited on Monday, September 14, 2026, to discuss the ongoing severe gas crisis, low gas pressure, and its growing imp
articles.x: A delegation of The Institution of Textile Engineers and Technologists (ITET) Bangladesh held a meeting with the Managing Director of Titas Gas Transmission and Distribution Company Limited on Monday, September 14, 2026, to discuss the ongoing severe gas crisis, low gas pressure, and its growing impact on the country’s textile and industrial sectors. Led by ITET Bangladesh President Engineer Mohammad Enayet Hossain, the delegation presented the ground realities of the gas crisis currently affecting textile mills and other industrial establishments across the country. The delegation highlighted that inadequate gas pressure is severely disrupting production, increasing operational costs, and putting many industrial units at risk of temporary or permanent closure. The delegation strongly urged Titas Gas to take immediate and effective measures to raise gas pressure to the required level in textile and other industrial areas. They called for urgent intervention and practical initiatives from the gas distribution authority to address the situation. During the meeting, the delegation also emphasized that prolonged gas shortages in the textile and related industrial sectors could have serious consequences not only for production and exports but also for employment, workers’ livelihoods, investment, foreign exchange earnings, and the overall industrial economy of Bangladesh. They warned that if industrial establishments continue to face inadequate gas supply and pressure, a growing number of factories could be forced to suspend operations, creating significant social and economic consequences. articles.x: The Ministry of Commerce has suspended its decision to withdraw the bond facility for imports of 10–30 count cotton yarn and require importers to submit bank guarantees, pending further consideration. In a letter to the National Board of Revenue (NBR) chairman on 13 September, the ministry said it had suspended the decision for further review. Courtesy: Collected The ministry had earlier asked the NBR on 7 September to withdraw the bond facility for imports of 10–30 count cotton yarn, citing the need to protect local industries while ensuring access to raw materials for genuine exporters. Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA) President Mahmud Hasan Khan Babu welcomed the latest decision. He said that BGMEA, the Bangladesh Knitwear Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BKMEA) and the Bangladesh Textile Mills Association (BTMA) would soon meet to discuss the issue and work toward a solution. “I hope we will reach a consensus and make a decision under the leadership of the commerce ministry, in the interest of the country,” he added. The suspension comes amid a broader disagreement between textile millers and apparel exporters over restrictions on imported raw materials. The government had previously restricted imports of knit fabrics used by knitwear exporters under the new Import Policy Order. Apparel exporters raised concerns that the restriction could affect export competitiveness. BGMEA and BKMEA had sought withdrawal of the provision in a letter to the commerce minister on 1 September, following which the Commerce Ministry held discussions with industry stakeholders. articles.x: NEW YORK — September 10, 2026 — Intrinsic Advanced Materials is expanding the commercial reach of CiCLO ® technology across home and hospitality textiles this September with ADVANSA and HeiQ, followed by its partnership with Lonely Whale’s Fashion the Future activation during NYC Climate Week. CiCLO® technology expands across home textiles with ADVANSA’s Suprelle® fiberfill made with CiCLO® fibers and new opportunities to pair CiCLO fibers with HeiQ functional technologies. ADVANSA is introducing Suprelle ® fiberfill made with CiCLO fibers, extending CiCLO technology into an established premium fiberfill portfolio designed around comfort and performance. At the same time, a collaboration with HeiQ Materials AG is creating opportunities to pair CiCLO fibers with functional technologies that address specific product needs, including cooling, moisture management, freshness and allergen reduction. Together, the developments give manufacturers, brands and retailers more ways to create products around specific consumer needs while incorporating CiCLO technology designed to help reduce microplastic fiber persistence. Microplastic fiber pollution caused by the shedding of synthetic textiles is one of the most prevalent forms of microplastic pollution. CiCLO ® technology is a patented textile ingredient integrated into polyester and nylon fibers during manufacturing. It creates pathways designed to accelerate biodegradation when microplastic fibers enter end-of-life environments with moisture and microorganisms, reducing their persistence. Third-party laboratories independently test CiCLO fibers using recognized ASTM and ISO methods. articles.x: DHAKA, Bangladesh, September 14, 2026 — Avery Dennison (NYSE: AVY), a global materials science and digital identification solutions company, today opened a new flagship Smart Warehouse at the Dhaka Export Processing Zone (DEPZ) in Savar, expanding its use of integrated automation and digital technology to bolster the competitiveness of manufacturers serving global apparel and footwear markets. The landmark facility signifies a transformative step in the company’s broader Manufacturing 4.0 initiative in Bangladesh. The new facility is engineered to redefine operational efficiency. The 830-square-meter facility features high-end digital infrastructure with seven automated guided vehicles (AGVs), connected packing software, and a warehouse management system, with storage capacity for 25,000 cartons. The connected packing system optimizes workflow and enables 72% faster processing speeds, while the facility is designed to handle five times increase over the previous inbound volume, double outbound velocity and increase inventory density by 50%. U.S. Ambassador to Bangladesh Mr. Brent T. Christensen attended the opening, alongside Executive Chairman of BEPZA (Bangladesh Export Processing Zones Authority), Major General Mr. Mohammad Moazzem Hossain, ndc, afwc, psc, G, MPhil; President of AmCham (American Chamber of Commerce) in Bangladesh, Mr. Syed Mohammad Kamal; and the Avery Dennison executive leadership team whose presence underscores the significance of this milestone for the region’s manufacturing future. articles.x: Manufacturers supplying the absorbent hygiene products (AHPs) and disposable wipes sectors now operate some of the most sophisticated continuous production systems in modern manufacturing, according to a recent INDEX 2026 exhibition newsletter. The enormous volumes demanded by baby diapers, feminine hygiene products, adult incontinence products and wipes have justified decades of investment in polymer science, fibre engineering, web formation, automation and digital process control, creating technologies that are increasingly influencing the wider nonwovens industry. One of the clearest messages to emerge from INDEX 2026 in Geneva was that many of the innovations first developed for disposable hygiene products are now finding wider applications in filtration, medical products and other technical nonwovens. Across the exhibition halls, machinery builders demonstrated how the pursuit of lighter products, greater softness, improved process stability and higher manufacturing efficiency is increasingly delivering benefits. The breadth of technologies on display also underlined the unique position of INDEX in bringing together the complete nonwovens value chain, providing a snapshot of how advances in materials, machinery and digital manufacturing are converging to shape the industry’s future. Reicofil RF5 Among the technologies attracting particular attention in Geneva was Reifenhäuser’s Reicofil RF5 spunmelt platform, which continues to influence hygiene manufacturing almost a decade after its introduction. Earlier generations of spunmelt technology largely focused on increasing output and reducing manufacturing costs. articles.o: GRTS: a broader standard for textiles
articles.s: STUTTGART – Global Standards, the nonprofit behind the Global Organic Textile Standard (GOTS), has introduced GRTS, a new standard for the processing of fibres certified to defined Responsible Fibre Standards. The standard covers a broad range of plant, animal, synthetic, man-made cellulosic and rec
articles.x: STUTTGART – Global Standards, the nonprofit behind the Global Organic Textile Standard (GOTS), has introduced GRTS, a new standard for the processing of fibres certified to defined Responsible Fibre Standards. The standard covers a broad range of plant, animal, synthetic, man-made cellulosic and recycled fibres, providing a new certification route for brands, mills, manufacturers and sourcing teams across the textile industry. A Broader Standard GRTS is a new processing standard that can apply to a broad range of fibres certified to third-party Responsible Fibre Standards. It brings credible environmental and social requirements across the textile supply chain and has been designed to complement the established GOTS framework. For businesses, one of the main benefits is the ability to certify more of their fibre portfolio. GRTS covers eligible textiles made with certified plant, animal, synthetic, man-made cellulosic and recycled fibres, providing a certification route for products that fall outside the organic fibre scope of GOTS. The standard also places a strong emphasis on supply chain visibility. GRTS combines independent third-party certification with traceability, transaction verification and due diligence requirements across the entire textile supply chain. It also builds on an established certification system. GRTS uses the ‘gold-standard’ certification infrastructure and many of the core requirements already established through GOTS. For GOTS-certified companies, certification activities can be aligned with existing systems and audit cycles, helping to reduce duplication and administrative effort. articles.o: Transforming colouration practices
articles.s: The new Melange Horizon Europe project aims to transform colouration practices in the European interior textile industry by moving colour design from the end of the manufacturing process to its beginning As part of a consortium of nine partners led by Aalto University in Finland, Textile ETP in Brus
articles.x: The new Melange Horizon Europe project aims to transform colouration practices in the European interior textile industry by moving colour design from the end of the manufacturing process to its beginning As part of a consortium of nine partners led by Aalto University in Finland, Textile ETP in Brussels will run the dissemination and stakeholder engagement activities. Fabric colouration is one of the most resource-intensive stages in textile production and its impact cannot be solved by more sustainable raw materials and technologies alone. Conventionally, colour is applied at the end of the manufacturing process to achieve repeatability and uniformity, at high cost in water, energy and chemicals. The current pursuit of near-unachievable uniformity in fibres, yarns and fabrics is a key challenge to circularity, wasting materials and resources through trial runs and discouraging the reuse of recycled and naturally variable materials. Melange is responding by using design as a driver of sustainable competitiveness in the European interior textile industry. The project aims to advance low-impact fibre-stage colouration technologies, such as spin, dope and solution dyeing, and treat colour variation as a signature of uniqueness rather than a defect. Its inspiration is from a heritage practice from Prato in Tuscany, of blending pre-coloured recycled fibres by shade, avoiding re-dyeing and treating variation as a valued aesthetic. By shifting colouration upstream and making imperfection desirable, Melange aims to cut water and chemical use by up to 50% compared with conventional finishing-stage processes. articles.x: Karl Mayer has introduced an extra-wide version of its HKS 3-M EL three-bar tricot machine, targeting maximum productivity across sporting goods, apparel, home textiles and technical textile applications. The new HKS 3-M EL has a standard working width of 330 inches, which can be expanded by a further 10 inches to 340 inches. Despite its XXL format, the machine can operate at production speeds of up to 2,800 rpm, setting new performance benchmarks particularly for the manufacture of modern sporting goods. “With the HKS 3-M EL in 340 inches, we offer the most productive machine in this configuration on the market,” said Michael Ahrendt, Global Head of Performance Fabrics at Karl Mayer. Michael Ahrendt, Global Head of Performance Fabrics at Karl Mayer. © Karl Mayer In addition to its combination of width and speed, the new machine incorporates energy-efficient technologies, intelligent automation and low-maintenance features. Karl Mayer says flexibility is another key advantage, allowing manufacturers to address a broad spectrum of textile markets with a single machine platform. The HKS 3-M EL can produce fabrics featuring a wide variety of designs and high stitch densities for fashion and apparel, home textiles and technical textiles. The machine is particularly suited to sports, activewear and athleisure applications. It can also be used for the efficient production of soft and warm outdoor textiles, including fluffy, napped and brushed fleece fabrics of the type commonly employed in softshell applications. © Karl Mayer Karl Mayer says the versatile tricot machine also opens up opportunities for processing sustainable yarns. articles.o: Archroma and Lameirinho partner in pioneering deployment of InOneGO single-step dyeing
articles.s: Archroma, a global leader in specialty chemicals, and Lameirinho, a leading home textiles manufacturer based in Portugal, are collaborating to bring InOneGO by Archroma, a new single-step dyeing process, into commercial production. Lameirinho’s first InOneGo bedlinens collection is now available wor
articles.x: Archroma, a global leader in specialty chemicals, and Lameirinho, a leading home textiles manufacturer based in Portugal, are collaborating to bring InOneGO by Archroma , a new single-step dyeing process, into commercial production. Lameirinho’s first InOneGo bedlinens collection is now available worldwide. InOneGO by Archroma is an innovative continuous dyeing process that combines coloration, fixation and softening into a single pad-dry application step. “This new InOneGO by Archroma process enables Lameirinho to achieve a wide range of shades and effects – including authentic indigo denim looks, wash-down effects and vintage-inspired finishes – bringing depth, character and a contemporary aesthetic to home textiles. At the same time, it simplifies the dyeing process by reducing the number of processing steps, and decreases resource consumption,” said Jorge Leitão, Innovation and Development Manager at Lameirinho. Developed for woven cellulosic textiles, including denim and fashion wear, as well as home textiles, InOneGO is compatible with Archroma’s advanced sulfur dyestuffs: the DIRESUL ® RDT range of pre-reduced low-sulfur liquid dyes, and the EarthColors ® and FiberColors ® biomass-based sulfur dyes. This gives mills and brands a lower-impact way to produce wash-down effects, without compromising on fastness or shade range across earthy tones, deep blues and dark blacks. “Achieving the washed-down look conventionally requires multiple washes, with extra water and energy needed at each stage. InOneGO is a genuine structural innovation. Presented under the theme Fabric Solutions for Every Sport, the concept brings together textile devel
articles.x: Eurojersey is broadening its approach to sportswear with Out of Frame, a new concept that looks beyond individual sporting disciplines to focus on the performance requirements of the body in motion. Presented under the theme Fabric Solutions for Every Sport, the concept brings together textile developments addressing a wide range of movement and performance needs, from the softness and freedom required for wellness activities to the speed of tennis and the protection and durability demanded by more extreme applications. The Italian manufacturer says its continuing textile research is focused on translating characteristics including stretch, compression, breathability, moisture management, durability and comfort into fabric solutions developed around specific performance requirements. Out of Frame is structured around four perspectives on sport – Soft Movement, Tennis Fast Surfaces, The Cotton Chapter and Performance Peak – each examining different demands placed on fabrics by the moving body. Soft Movement focuses on yoga and wellness activities, where fluidity, balance and control are important. Eurojersey has developed exceptionally soft fabrics intended to follow the body naturally, combining comfort and stretch with a second-skin feel. Tennis Fast Surfaces addresses the acceleration, reaction and rapid changes of direction associated with the game. Fabrics developed for these applications combine light weight, breathability and moisture management with comfort and freedom of movement. The Cotton Chapter marks a new direction for Eurojersey’s research and includes a first preview of a development in knitted cotton. articles.x: The Institution of Textile Engineers and Technologists (ITET) Bangladesh has urged Titas Gas Transmission and Distribution Company Limited to take immediate measures to restore adequate gas pressure for textile and other industrial units amid an ongoing gas crisis. A delegation led by ITET Bangladesh President Engr. Md. Enayet Hossain held a view-exchange meeting with the Managing Director of Titas Gas on Monday, 14 September, to discuss the severe gas shortage, low pressure and its impact on industrial production. During the meeting, the delegation highlighted the situation faced by textile and manufacturing factories, saying inadequate gas pressure is severely disrupting production and increasing operational costs. They also warned that prolonged shortages could push a number of industrial units towards closure. The ITET delegation called on Titas Gas authorities to take urgent and effective steps to ensure adequate gas supply and restore pressure to the level required by textile and other manufacturing industries. The engineers also warned that a prolonged gas crisis could have wider consequences for Bangladesh’s industrial economy, affecting production, export earnings, employment, workers’ livelihoods, investment and foreign exchange earnings. Sequential factory closures, they said, could create significant social and economic challenges. The meeting was attended by senior ITET leaders, including Senior Vice President Engr. articles.s: A new cohort of circular champions, with 16 representatives from eight textile organizations, successfully graduated from the CIRCO program, learning to implement circular business models that balance profitability with environmental responsibility. CIRCO Hub Bangladesh has successfully concluded Tr
articles.x: A new cohort of circular champions, with 16 representatives from eight textile organizations, successfully graduated from the CIRCO program, learning to implement circular business models that balance profitability with environmental responsibility. CIRCO Hub Bangladesh has successfully concluded Track 4 in Dhaka on September 7, 2026, marking another significant milestone in the country’s transition toward a sustainable, circular industrial ecosystem. The intensive three-day programme brought together a cohort of enterprises from Bangladesh’s Ready-Made Garment (RMG) and textile sectors to design and refine circular business models using the globally recognised CIRCO methodology of the Delft University of Technology. The three-day workshop, conducted over a period of three weeks, was organized by LightCastle Partners with support from the Embassy of the Kingdom of the Netherlands in Bangladesh, the Netherlands Enterprise Agency (RVO), and CIRCO International. Since its launch in early 2026, CIRCO Hub Bangladesh has conducted four successful Tracks, each bringing together a diverse group of industry players committed to exploring circular solutions. Track 4 continued the Hub’s mission to equip Bangladeshi companies with the tools and strategies needed to move beyond the traditional linear “take-make-dispose” model toward regenerative systems where materials are reused, recycled, and reintegrated into production cycles. As global markets continue to evolve, CIRCO Hub Bangladesh’s work remains critical to ensuring the country’s industrial sector is equipped to meet the demands of a more sustainable, resource-conscious future. articles.o: Kipas pushes textile recycling toward commercial scale with fibR-e
articles.s: Textile-to-textile recycling is moving closer to commercial scale as Kipas Textiles expands its fibR-e recycling platform to process up to 100 tons of textile waste a day. The facility, which started...
articles.x: Textile-to-textile recycling is moving closer to commercial scale as Kipas Textiles expands its fibR-e recycling platform to process up to 100 tons of textile waste a day. The facility, which started operations at the end of 2025, targets one of recycling’s biggest challenges: complex textile waste. Its process can handle polyester-rich waste, including polyester-elastane blends, mixed colors, and garments with trims attached. At full capacity, the facility could process around 36,500 tons of waste annually. This is significant as less than 1% of the global fiber market currently comes from recycled textiles made from textile waste, according to Textile Exchange. fibR-e uses molecular recycling to break polyester waste down into its basic components and rebuild it into recycled polyester. The resulting material can then be converted into staple fiber and filament yarn for new textile production. The approach could also reduce the environmental impact of polyester recycling. Kipas says its textile-to-textile process can deliver nearly 74% lower emissions than virgin polyester production. The European Union is also strengthening textile waste rules, including separate collection and producer responsibility requirements that will increase pressure on companies from 2028. For the industry, the key shift is from proving that textile-to-textile recycling works to building enough capacity to process waste at scale. Kipas’ 100-ton daily capacity shows how recycling infrastructure is beginning to move in that direction.

articles.s: The ACT-MULTI system developed by Eltex – a member of TMAS, the Swedish textile machinery association – is bringing individual yarn tension monitoring and automatic control to the heat-setting process, helping manufacturers maintain consistent processing conditions across every yarn position. As a c
articles.x: The ACT-MULTI system developed by Eltex – a member of TMAS, the Swedish textile machinery association – is bringing individual yarn tension monitoring and automatic control to the heat-setting process, helping manufacturers maintain consistent processing conditions across every yarn position. As a critical stage in the production of synthetic and blended yarns, heat-setting relies on precise, consistent processing conditions to stabilize yarn structures, lock in twist and bulk, and ensure predictable performance during subsequent processes such as dyeing and finishing, before or after weaving, knitting, or tufting. Photo: The ACT-MULTI is designed for straightforward installation and maintenance. This is particularly important in carpet yarn production, where carefully controlled heat treatment relieves internal stresses and improves bulk, resilience, dimensional stability and dye uptake. Variations in yarn tension during the process can therefore affect both processing consistency and the quality of the finished carpet. The ACT-MULTI addresses this challenge by individually monitoring and automatically controlling yarn tension on the input side of the heat-setting machine tunnel. Its fast response enables highly precise tension control, and the system also incorporates integrated yarn break detection. An external display lets operators monitor the entire system quickly and clearly, while active yarn positions can be learned quickly when new orders are introduced. articles.x: The country’s textile mills would be able to buy US cotton locally from November, as the first privately operated US cotton warehouse in Bangladesh is set to open at Anwara in Chattogram, reducing sourcing lead times and potentially lowering procurement costs. The AmeriBangla US Cotton Warehouse is scheduled to begin operations on November 18 at a leased facility near the government-designated Free Trade Zone, with an initial inventory of 80-100 tonnes. AmeriBangla Corporation, led by Bangladeshi-American entrepreneur Aswar Rahman, is establishing the warehouse as part of a broader initiative to strengthen the supply chain between US cotton producers and Bangladesh’s textile and apparel industry. ‘We are planning to launch operations on 18 November. Around 100 tonnes of cotton have already left a US port for Bangladesh,’ Aswar, chief executive officer of AmeriBangla, said in an interview with New Age. He also said that the company planned to start with three shipments of US cotton and gradually increase inventory according to demand. The initiative is being implemented with a local partner. The warehouse would allow spinning mills to purchase cotton from locally held stocks instead of arranging individual imports and waiting for shipments to arrive. US cotton imports have already been rising. Bangladesh imported US cotton worth $346 million in financial year 2024-25, up from $278 million in FY24, accounting for about 10 percent of the country’s total cotton imports. Aswar Rahman said that the industry leaders believed imports of US cotton could eventually reach $2 billion a year if the country can take advantage of emerging trade opportunities with the United States.
