articles.x: 300 global garment brands and retailers have signed the International Accord for Health and Safety in the Textile and Garment Industry (International Accord) with global unions, IndustriALL and UNI, marking the highest number of signatories for any Accord agreement to date. These signatory brands are headquartered across 26 countries and annually source goods worth approximately USD $26 billion from Bangladesh and Pakistan. Collectively, the Accord brands source from over 2,000 factories with over 3.4 million workers in Bangladesh and Pakistan. The International Accord was renewed in 2023 as a framework agreement for a three-year term, with automatic renewal for an additional three years, making it the longest commitment in the Accord’s history. It builds upon the 2013 and 2018 Accords on Fire and Building Safety in Bangladesh, as well as the 2021 International Accord, each of which progressively expanded its scope and commitments. The International Accord is a legally binding agreement between global brands and trade unions, to create and maintain garment factories where no worker fears fires, building collapses or other accidents that can be prevented with reasonable health and safety measures. It promotes worker health and safety through factory inspections to identify risks; remediation to implement life-saving improvements; worker safety training to raise awareness of workers’ rights, responsibilities, and health and safety risks; and a trusted Complaints Mechanism for workers to raise health and safety concerns. The Accord Secretariat thanks all brands, trade unions and civil society organisations who have made this milestone possible. We look forward to welcoming even more brands as we continue working together towards a safer textile and garment industry. Watch

articles.x: On Monday, 7 September 2026, RMG leaders and energy experts stressed that Bangladesh must place renewable-energy transition and energy sovereignty at the centre of its long-term industrial strategy as the continuing energy crisis, rising fuel-import dependence and unreliable supply increasingly threaten RMG’s sustainability. The call came at the “Rapid Energy Transition Conference: Powering Security, Sustainability and Growth in Bangladesh RMG,” convened by Ethical Trading Initiative (ETI) Bangladesh, which brought together 108 representatives from RMG factories. Speakers included representatives from BGMEA, BKMEA and BSREA, alongside international brands, financial institutions, renewable-energy companies and technical organisations. The conference featured three working sessions examining the urgency of renewable-energy transition, available financing and technology pathways, and the role of business associations in supporting industry-wide implementation, respectively. In his opening speech, Abil Bin Amin, Executive Director of ETI Bangladesh , called for a just and collaborative energy transition, stressing that factories and workers should not bear the costs of meeting international climate targets and transitioning to renewables, without collective stakeholder engagement and support. Eng. Imran Kader Turjo, Director of BKMEA , warned that Bangladesh could not secure the RMG sector’s energy future through rooftop solar alone. “We are already late; these renewable-energy and infrastructure initiatives should have been implemented 10 to 12 years ago. articles.x: Standfirst: A visual nostalgia wave becomes economically relevant to the industrial apparel sector only when it structurally alters product design, processing chemistry and manufacturing lead times. For manufacturers, the commercial question is whether additional design complexity can be converted into value capture rather than absorbed as uncompensated operational cost. THE LONG-TERM MACRO REVIVAL: A 7-YEAR SYSTEMIC EVOLUTION The global apparel architecture is consolidating a major revival of 1980s shapes, proportions and design attitudes —a direction that has been building for several years rather than appearing as a single-season trend. To understand its significance, the timeline matters. Bangladesh has operated at global garment-manufacturing scale since the late 1970s, building its competitive position around agility, adaptability and high-volume execution. The return of stronger, more structured and volume-led product therefore does not represent an entirely foreign manufacturing challenge. The opportunity is to apply that established production base to a more technically demanding product cycle. According to WGSN Fashion Vision , wide-leg jeans—the clearest denim manifestation of the current ’80s direction—recorded a 9.4 percentage-point increase in catwalk mix compared with previous cycles, reaching a 32% share of the tracked denim mix. Historical collection tracking referenced through McKinsey Apparel Intelligence and Vogue Business also indicates that the shift away from ultra-minimal, skin-tight proportions has been developing for approximately seven to eight years . articles.s: WATTWIL, Switzerland — September 9, 2026 — Heberlein, a globally recognized provider of air interlacing and air texturing jets for synthetic filament yarns, is consolidating its success in the Chinese market with its APh- and APe-series for DTY applications. articles.x: WATTWIL, Switzerland — September 9, 2026 — Heberlein, a globally recognized provider of air interlacing and air texturing jets for synthetic filament yarns, is consolidating its success in the Chinese market with its APh- and APe-series for DTY applications. Particularly in the field of Air Covering, Heberlein technologies combine excellent quality with significant savings in compressed-air consumption. A new service hub in Shengze City underlines the company’s long-term commitment in the Chinese market. Over the past 20 years, Heberlein has achieved considerable success in China. The Swiss brand stands for innovation, reliability and trust. Heberlein DTY jets are used both for the retrofitting of existing facilities and in new investments. Compressed-air consumption is an important KPI for mills, as compressed air is a cost-intensive resource. Heberlein’s compressed-air-saving technology therefore gives its solutions a major competitive advantage. Heberlein will present its successful APh- and APe-series at upcoming ITMA Asia + CITME 2026. Air Covering for required yarn qualities Heberlein Air Covering Solutions Demand for Air Covering has been high in the Chinese market. Air Covering combines elastane with a covering yarn by interlacing the two components at regular intervals using a controlled air jet. The resulting yarns offer good stretch, comfort and surface properties. They are widely used in leggings and sportswear, underwear, hosiery and socks. Other applications include stretch fabrics for trousers and jeans, elasticated cuffs, as well as medical and compression textiles. articles.o: Lycra targets the workwear market
articles.s: The Lycra Company is targeting the workwear and protective clothing market with a portfolio of fibre technologies designed to improve comfort, durability and performance in demanding working environments. The company will make its first appearance at the NSC Safety Congress and Expo in Indianapolis
articles.x: The Lycra Company is targeting the workwear and protective clothing market with a portfolio of fibre technologies designed to improve comfort, durability and performance in demanding working environments. The company will make its first appearance at the NSC Safety Congress and Expo in Indianapolis from September 14-16, where it will introduce its Fibers That Work portfolio to the North American market. The portfolio brings together existing and new fibre technologies for workwear, uniforms and protective apparel, addressing requirements including moisture management, visibility, antistatic protection, stretch and durability. “Comfort is fundamental to workwear performance,” says Tara Maurer-Mackay, product category director of branded specialty products at The Lycra Company. “Our innovations help workers adapt to changing conditions throughout the day with fibres that move moisture to keep them dry if they sweat, stretch that allows them to move freely, and solutions that enhance visibility for safety. “Leveraging our decades of innovation in comfort technologies, we are well positioned to help our customers create garments that workers can trust in demanding environments.” Among the technologies being highlighted is Lycra Antistatic fibre, which provides inherent antistatic properties while retaining stretch, comfort and fit. Lycra T400 fibre is meanwhile designed for durable workwear requiring comfort stretch, consistent fit and moisture management. According to the company, fabrics incorporating the fibre can withstand up to 100 industrial wash cycles. The wider Fibers That Work portfolio reflects growing demand for workwear that combines protection with greater wearer comfort and durability. articles.s: AUCKLAND – Researchers in New Zealand have found that cotton textile waste can be broken down to produce biogas. The findings raise the prospect of another end-of-life route for natural-fibre clothing that cannot be reused or recycled. The University of Auckland study tested cotton, wool and polyest
articles.x: AUCKLAND – Researchers in New Zealand have found that cotton textile waste can be broken down to produce biogas. The findings raise the prospect of another end-of-life route for natural-fibre clothing that cannot be reused or recycled. The University of Auckland study tested cotton, wool and polyester-cotton blends using anaerobic digestion. This is a process already widely used to treat food waste, farm waste and sewage sludge. articles.o: GORE-TEX® Fabrics: 50 Years Proven — Built For What’s Next
articles.s: ELKTON, MD — May 11, 2026 — W. L. Gore & Associates (Gore), founder of the GORE-TEX® Brand, marks 50 years of product innovation and leadership in fabrics. Since its consumer introduction in the Early Winters Light Dimension™ tent in 1976, Gore has expanded its portfolio into a globally trusted solu
articles.x: ELKTON, MD — May 11, 2026 — W. L. Gore & Associates (Gore), founder of the GORE-TEX® Brand, marks 50 years of product innovation and leadership in fabrics. Since its consumer introduction in the Early Winters Light Dimension tent in 1976, Gore has expanded its portfolio into a globally trusted solution across garments, footwear, gloves. Today, GORE-TEX® Brand fabrics continue to add comfort while protecting people from everyday situations to the world’s most demanding conditions. As Gore marks this milestone, the company is not only reflecting on its legacy of innovation but also setting the course for the future. Since Bob Gore’s 1969 discovery of a lightweight, microporous material, GORE-TEX® Product technology has been driven by science-led exploration, transforming a breakthrough insight into one of the most influential materials platforms in performance fabrics. Today, that legacy continues through ongoing innovation and a commitment to advance responsible performance, the belief that performance, durability, and sustainability must advance together. These efforts span the brand’s fabrics business that extends across outdoor, professional, and defense applications, where reliable protection is critical. “For five decades, GORE‑TEX® Products have enabled people to perform in the toughest conditions,” said Michelle Augustine, Gore fabrics business leader. “We continue to build on this foundation through innovation that helps our partners meet evolving needs while advancing responsible performance for the future.” Durability has long been a focus for Gore, and the company is now bringing that commitment to the forefront, emphasizing the design of longer-lasting products to help reduce resource use while maintaining performance over time. articles.t: Woolmark Company, Bangladesh 기술 대표로 Ismail Hossain Tushar 임명
articles.o: The Woolmark Company appoints Ismail Hossain Tushar as Technical Representative for Bangladesh
articles.s: Textile engineer and business strategist Ismail Hossain Tushar has joined The Woolmark Company as Business Development and Technical Representative for Bangladesh. Figure: Ismail Hossain Tushar, Busi...
articles.x: Textile engineer and business strategist Ismail Hossain Tushar has joined The Woolmark Company as Business Development and Technical Representative for Bangladesh. Figure: Ismail Hossain Tushar, Business Development & Technical Representative (Bangladesh), The Woolmark Company The Woolmark Company operates as a global authority on wool and functions as a subsidiary of Australian Wool Innovation. It drives research, technical development, and quality assurance for Australian Merino wool across international supply chains. The organization connects woolgrowers, apparel manufacturers, and global fashion brands through quality certification, technical education, and supply chain optimization. Ismail Hossain Tushar brings more than 13 years of experience across the textile value chain to his new position. He holds a degree in Textile Engineering from Ahsanullah University of Science and Technology (AUST). He also earned an MBA from BRAC University and a Postgraduate Diploma in Textile Management from the Bangladesh University of Textiles (BUTEX). His professional background includes commercial and technical positions at Shore to Shore, Groz-Beckert, Dysin Group, and Sieger Spintech. In his new role, Tushar focuses on connecting Bangladesh's manufacturing base with global wool supply chains. His work centers on providing technical support to local factories, facilitating knowledge transfer, and assisting manufacturers in developing wool and wool-blend products for export markets.

articles.o: BRM brings 3D woven composites to CAMX
articles.s: Bally Ribbon Mills (BRM) will showcase its latest 3D woven composite technologies at CAMX 2026, taking place at the Georgia World Congress Center in Atlanta from September 21-24. The US company will exhibit 3D woven joints, thermal protection systems and other engineered composite structures at stan
articles.x: Bally Ribbon Mills (BRM) will showcase its latest 3D woven composite technologies at CAMX 2026, taking place at the Georgia World Congress Center in Atlanta from September 21-24. The US company will exhibit 3D woven joints, thermal protection systems and other engineered composite structures at stand K46, highlighting applications ranging from spacecraft heat protection to aircraft engines and structural components. BRM uses continuous 3D weaving to produce complex reinforcement structures in which fibres are integrated throughout all three dimensions of the weave. Its woven joints can be produced in a variety of shaped profiles, with the fibre architecture tailored to the load requirements of individual components. The technology is designed to provide continuous reinforcement across joined substructures, offering an alternative to conventional joining methods, and in some applications, metallic components. Using woven carbon fibre composite structures in place of metal can provide significant weight savings while maintaining the structural performance required for demanding aerospace applications. From structural joints to heat shields BRM is also applying its 3D weaving expertise to thermal protection systems for spacecraft and other extreme-temperature applications. Different yarn types, densities, thicknesses, widths and resin systems can be combined to develop woven structures for specific thermal and mechanical requirements. One of the company’s most significant developments in this field resulted from its work with NASA on 3DMAT, a three-dimensional orthogonally woven quartz material developed for compression pads on the Orion spacecraft. articles.s: CHARLOTTE, N.C. — September 9, 2026 — Following the success of its inaugural 2026 event, Textiles Recycling Expo USA is inviting industry experts, innovators, researchers and thought leaders to submit speaker proposals for its 2027 conference, taking place April 7–8 at the Charlotte Convention Cente
articles.x: CHARLOTTE, N.C. — September 9, 2026 — Following the success of its inaugural 2026 event, Textiles Recycling Expo USA is inviting industry experts, innovators, researchers and thought leaders to submit speaker proposals for its 2027 conference, taking place April 7–8 at the Charlotte Convention Center, North Carolina. The call for speakers is now open as organizers begin building the program for the second edition of Textiles Recycling Expo USA, North America’s dedicated exhibition and conference focused on textile recycling and circularity. Structural Partner, Accelerating Circularity is working closely with the organizers to help identify key industry challenges and ensure the program reflects the priorities and conversations shaping the sector. Along with addressing the core continuing impact of evolving legislation, infrastructure, and technology on the textiles recycling industry, the event is also expanding their focus to explore the role of re-use and repair, and the responsibilities the US textiles industry has to countries in the global south. The 2027 conference is seeking speakers with expertise across areas including: EPR & the New Compliance Landscape Sorting Technology: The Bottleneck and the Fix Fiber-to-Fiber Recycling & Recycled Fiber End Markets Collection Infrastructure & Reverse Logistics Reuse, Resale & Repair as the First Circular Loop Traceability, Brand Accountability & Circular Business Models – NEW for 2027 Global Trade Flows: Burdens, Opportunities & Accountability in the Global South – NEW for 2027 Textiles Recycling Expo USA provides speakers with the opportunity to share their expertise with an international audience of brands, recyclers, manufacturers, technology providers, policymakers, researchers and industry professionals. articles.x: BURLINGTON, N.C. — September 10, 2026 — Trivantage, a supplier of specialty fabrics, hardware, and accessories, is pleased to announce the appointment of James Dillport as an outside sales representative serving Missouri, Indiana, Tennessee, Kentucky, and Arkansas. James Dillport Photo – Mark Skalny (c)2024 James brings 10 years of industry experience to Trivantage. Throughout his career, he has developed a strong understanding of the industry, from fabrication and product applications to the day-to-day needs and challenges customers face. In his new role, James will draw on his industry experience in a fabrication shop and leadership background to serve as a well-versed resource for customers. Having worked directly in the environments his customers operate in every day, he understands the realities of fabrication, product selection and application, and the challenges that can impact efficiency and project success. That firsthand experience allows James to approach each customer as a knowledgeable industry partner who understands their business and can offer practical, informed solutions. James will use that perspective to help customers confidently navigate products, applications, and emerging innovations. articles.s: 미미박스가 상반기 경영성과를 임직원 보상과 글로벌 유통 확대로 연결하고 있다.미미박스는 2026년 상반기 경영성과를 바탕으로 임직원에게 경영성과 인센티브를 지급했다고 11일 밝혔다. 회사는 소수 핵심 제품에 판매 역량을 집중한 뒤 제품 구성과 유통 채널을 확장하는 전략을 추진하고 있다.미미박스 측에 따르면 2026년 2분기 매출은 전년 동기와 직전 분기보다 각각 50% 이상 증가했다. articles.t: 새로운 Aersulate의 유망 시장
articles.o: Promising markets for new Aersulate
articles.s: Outlast Technologies, based in Heidenheim/Brenz, Germany, is targeting sportswear and military applications for its thin, lightweight Aersulate insulation technology following encouraging initial tests with prospective customers. The German temperature management specialist developed Aersulate using
articles.x: Outlast Technologies, based in Heidenheim/Brenz, Germany, is targeting sportswear and military applications for its thin, lightweight Aersulate insulation technology following encouraging initial tests with prospective customers. The German temperature management specialist developed Aersulate using Naerogel, the aerogel material supplied by Sweden’s Svenska Aerogel, and is now in discussions with companies in both sectors over potential applications. The development follows an initial ramp-up order for Naerogel placed by Outlast with Svenska Aerogel in late 2025, suggesting the technology is moving beyond initial development towards commercial evaluation. Aerogels are highly porous, extremely lightweight materials known for their low thermal conductivity, making them attractive for applications where high levels of insulation are required without the weight and bulk associated with conventional insulating materials. In Aersulate, Outlast has incorporated Naerogel into a textile insulation designed to provide thermal protection in a thin and lightweight format. This could prove particularly relevant in performance sportswear and military clothing, where reducing garment bulk while maintaining protection from cold conditions is a continuing challenge. Initial testing for these applications has now produced positive results, according to Outlast, providing the basis for further discussions with prospective customers. “Sportswear and military products are areas where thin, lightweight insulation could offer valuable benefits,” says Martin Bentz, CEO of Outlast Technologies. “We are exploring potential applications with companies in these sectors, and the positive initial test results encourage us to pursue these opportunities further.” Specialist woven structures for aeros

articles.t: Tonello 기술로 스리랑카 허브를 강화하다
articles.o: Tonello technology powers Sri Lankan hub
articles.s: Tonello has partnered with Asahi Dyes and Chemicals and Asons to establish a new garment finishing innovation hub in Sri Lanka, providing manufacturers and brands with facilities to develop and test a wide range of finishing processes. The new hub brings together Asahi’s expertise in textile chemica
articles.x: Tonello has partnered with Asahi Dyes and Chemicals and Asons to establish a new garment finishing innovation hub in Sri Lanka, providing manufacturers and brands with facilities to develop and test a wide range of finishing processes. The new hub brings together Asahi’s expertise in textile chemicals, Asons’ established presence in Sri Lanka’s textile supply sector and Tonello’s garment finishing technologies. At the centre of the facility is Tonello’s complete technology portfolio, enabling manufacturers, brands and other industry partners to develop and test washing, dyeing, laser, ozone and drying processes at a single location. The facility also incorporates Tonello’s digital process control technologies, allowing different treatments and process combinations to be evaluated, adjusted and refined before being transferred to industrial production. According to Tonello, the integrated approach enables garment manufacturers to consider chemistry, machinery and process parameters together, rather than developing individual stages of the finishing process in isolation. The hub has been conceived as a practical development environment where companies can experiment with new treatments, assess different combinations of chemicals and technologies, and develop processes capable of being scaled to commercial production. It will also provide a platform for collaboration between chemical suppliers, technology developers, manufacturers and brands seeking to improve garment finishing performance while reducing the environmental impact of production. articles.o: Heberlein reinforces its commitment to the Chinese market
articles.s: Advanced DTY jet technology and a new service hub bring performance and technical support closer to customers. Wattwil, Switzerland, September 9, 2026 – Heberlein, globally recognised as a leading provider of air interlacing and air texturing jets for synthetic filament yarns, is consolidating its s
articles.x: Advanced DTY jet technology and a new service hub bring performance and technical support closer to customers . Wattwil, Switzerland, September 9, 2026 – Heberlein, globally recognised as a leading provider of air interlacing and air texturing jets for synthetic filament yarns, is consolidating its success in the Chinese market with its APh- and APe-series for DTY applications. Particularly in the field of Air Covering, Heberlein technologies combine excellent quality with significant savings in compressed-air consumption. A new service hub in Shengze City underlines the company’s long-term commitment in the Chinese market. SlideJet-FT15-2 with the APe-series Over the past 20 years, Heberlein has achieved considerable success in China. The Swiss brand stands for innovation, reliability and trust. Heberlein DTY jets are used both for the retrofitting of existing facilities and in new investments. Compressed-air consumption is an important KPI for mills, as compressed air is a cost-intensive resource. Heberlein’s compressed-air-saving technology therefore gives its solutions a major competitive advantage. Heberlein will present its successful APh- and APe-series at upcoming ITMA Asia + CITME 2026. Air Covering for required yarn qualities Demand for Air Covering has been high in the Chinese market. Air Covering combines elastane with a covering yarn by interlacing the two components at regular intervals using a controlled air jet. The resulting yarns offer good stretch, comfort and surface properties. They are widely used in leggings and sportswear, underwear, hosiery and socks. articles.o: From Textile to Fibre Opportunity: Ismail Hossain Tushar Takes on a New Role to Develop Bangladesh’s Wool Ecosystem
articles.s: Bangladesh has built one of the world’s most extensive textile and apparel manufacturing ecosystems, with strong capabilities across spinning, knitting, weaving, dyeing, finishing, garment manufacturing and product development. Yet, when it comes to wool, the country’s story remains relatively limit
articles.x: Bangladesh has built one of the world’s most extensive textile and apparel manufacturing ecosystems, with strong capabilities across spinning, knitting, weaving, dyeing, finishing, garment manufacturing and product development. Yet, when it comes to wool, the country’s story remains relatively limited. Ismail Hossain Tushar, with more than 13 years of experience across Bangladesh’s textile value chain, is taking on a new role with The Woolmark Company to explore how Bangladesh’s strong manufacturing capabilities can connect with the global wool ecosystem—and help develop a new story for wool in Bangladesh. Figure: Ismail Hossain Tushar, Business Development & Technical Representative (Bangladesh), The Woolmark Company Against this backdrop, Ismail Hossain Tushar is beginning a new professional chapter with The Woolmark Company as Business Development & Technical Representative – Bangladesh , effective 10 September 2026. But the significance of the move extends beyond a new professional appointment. At the centre of his activities will be a broader question: how can Bangladesh build a meaningful ecosystem around wool, and how can its existing textile capabilities connect with the wider global wool industry? Looking at wool through the Bangladesh textile lens Tushar brings more than 13 years of experience across different areas of Bangladesh’s textile industry. A Textile Engineering graduate from Ahsanullah University of Science and Technology (AUST), he later complemented his technical background with an MBA in Marketing from BRAC University and a Postgraduate Diploma in Textile Management from Bangladesh University of Textiles (BUTEX). articles.s: 패션그룹형지가 크로커다일레이디·샤트렌·올리비아하슬러 등 여성복 핵심 3개 브랜드를 하나의 운영 체제로 묶는다.브랜드별로 흩어져 있던 기획·디자인·소싱·구매 기능을 통합하고 AI를 접목해 비용과 업무 효율을 동시에 끌어올린다는 전략이다. 정체된 가두점과 레거시 어덜트 패션 시장에서 기존 방식으로는 성장에 한계가 있다고 판단, 올해 초부터 추진해 온 전사 경영 효율화를 상품과 조직 전반의 체질 개선으로 확대한다.핵심은 브랜드별·기능별로 분절돼 있던 상품기획, 디자인, 소싱, 구매 업무를 하나의 유기적인 원스톱 프로세스로 전환하는 것이다
